title: 庄子的哲学：以人的立场来看物
folderName: 02_庄子的哲学：以人的立场来看物
audioPath: 02_庄子的哲学：以人的立场来看物/audio.m4a
quoteCardPath: 02_庄子的哲学：以人的立场来看物/quote_card.jpg
transcriptZh:
大家好，我是余秋雨，我们继续讲课。
上次我把老子的行于大道，相反相成，无为而治，和光同尘，直到最后的韬光养晦，这整整的思维，最后概括成一个非常具有高度的思想，叫做上善若水，他不是计谋，他是一个至善，和阴谋正好相反的。这个正是我们对老子有一种重新认识了，我上次结束的时候讲，我这一生有好多世界上著名的思想曾经帮助过我，但是对我帮助最大的是老子的上善若水，滋润万物而不争，一向处于低位，很安静地对着万物微笑的这种思维是最好的思维，这对我帮助很大。
恢复老子哲学的真面目
在我的一生当中，很多很多困惑，因为这个哲学就可以迎刃而解。经常有学生问我，老师你为什么无视高位的诱惑，无视外来的各种挑衅，还能够坚持天天写作，写作几十年，书一本本地出，完全不理会外面的喧闹，你怎么能够做到这样？而且不理会外面的诱惑，什么协会也不参加，什么会也不参与，怎么会是这样？
我对学生总是淡淡的一笑，然后就讲水，讲老子的水。学生们就会问，他说老师你既然讲到水，我们就想起了一个比喻，中国的一个成语，叫水滴石穿，你是不是用水的方式，把石头滴穿它，你就胜利了。我说不对，这里边没有胜利这一说。因为水滴石穿这个思维，水并没有把石头当作敌人、当作对手，甚至于根本没有把石头当作对象；穿石，或者说石穿，并不是预计的设计，而是自然的安排。这个自然的安排，就是天体自然的安排，这就是道了。
我们慢慢地写，慢慢地讲，几十年的时间把什么东西弄穿了，这不是我们的目标，因为我们并不觉得眼前有块石头是我们的斗争对象，我一定要慢慢地动用水滴把它滴穿，如果是这样的话，我那个水滴也太慢了，我为什么不做水，我们做个大力士把石头搬走，这不就干脆一点吗？这里边不存在我们想象的一个长时间躲起来的谋略，和一个对手周旋，最后安静的我方却反而胜利了。因为按照老子的哲学，没有胜败，我们只是滋润万物而已。
我这么讲讲以后，大家就明白了，我们不能把老子的大善变成大伪，虚伪的伪，也不能把老子的大道变成邪道。我看到很多很多的有学问的学者，他们在写老子的时候，都笑眯眯的说，老子是个老滑头，老子是个阴谋家等等，这都搞错了，这是很对不起老子。
老子是利万物而不争的思维的提出者，是上善若水的提出者，所以，我作为一个学者，作为一个文化人，恢复老子的本意，是一种学术责任，更是一种道义责任。尤其我自己受到老子那么好的影响，这就成了一种生命的责任了。我想我的学员也应该如此，我们正面地来理解老子的了不起的上善思维。
我们中国文化当中，阴谋论的东西很多，其实从中国历史上阴谋没那么多，至少没有我们现在电视剧里所写的那么多，没那么多，所以我经常给纽约的朋友讲，到纽约讲课，我有几个纽约的朋友说，我也想了解中国文化，我们终于看了已经翻译成英文的中国的有几个电视剧，一看以后吓坏了，中国怎么有那么多那么多的阴谋，这宫廷上下，每一个台阶，每一张笑脸，每一个美丽的宫女都是阴谋家。
我说，不是，中国阴谋没那么多，这是过去官方的史学家，后来我们可爱的当代的编剧想象出来的。我说，你看中国的历史书上确实写了很多阴谋，但是几百年就那么几个阴谋，这个阴谋中国老百姓不知道，因为在很长的时间，中国老百姓还是文盲更多一点，他们完全读不懂，看不清楚。我说我小的时候在农村，后来长时间在农村劳动，在文革当中也在农场劳动，我非常了解中国农民，我告诉纽约的朋友，中国的农民真的阴谋不多。他们的缺点呢，是比较吝啬，比较小气，不讲卫生，就这么几个缺点，很少有阴谋，如果说有阴谋的话，可能是有一点攀比，有一点保守，如此而已。
在这个问题上，我们在学习中国哲学的时候，一定要明白，我们的首席哲学家老子，把他歪曲成阴谋家是错的。他是一个传播最高道德的人，水利万物而不争，是这样的一个思维，中国应该普及这样的思维到我们的生活当中去。我们的无为而治不是阴谋，我们的相反相成不是阴谋，我们韬光养晦也不是阴谋，理由是，老子不是阴谋家。这样我就把老子已经讲得比较完整了。
庄子的哲学：物物者非物
接下来，毫无疑问要讲讲庄子，庄子呢，在道家看来，教主是老子，没有把庄子当作教主，但是实际上，庄子在老子的身边，身边我不是说时间上的身边了，而是哲学思想上的身边，在他的身边就构成了一种比较完整的叫老庄哲学。他们其实隔的时间还比较长，但是构成了一种老庄哲学。这个老庄哲学，我们在看道家的他们的教主的思维，他们的宗教的一种哲学根基的时候，大概是离不开庄子的。
庄子，我想讲短一点，因为老子我讲的比较长了。反正大家知道，我在《北大授课》这本书里边，专门写了庄子的一些文章，而且不断地在论庄子、抄庄子。抄庄子就是把庄子的东西写成书法，《逍遥游》我是用草书写的，还翻译庄子，这个读者都不难找到，所以，我庄子可以讲得比较简略一点了。我因为非常喜欢庄子，一讲有可能在篇幅上失度了，讲着讲着就又讲多了。
大家还记得我曾经把先秦诸子的文学品相做了个排位，我把庄子放在第一位了，孟子第二，老子第三，孔子第四，这大家还有印象。伟大的孔子那么了不起，你怎么放到第四，我还讲了理由，因为我们不是从哲学思维和影响力上来讲，我们是从文学品味上来讲。庄子，以一个小孩的陌生的眼光，提出很多问题，而不是在高台上回答很多问题，他是提出问题的，然后以小孩的方式做整体的回答，这就是个艺术家了，而且用的方式是寓言，寓言，寓言，有好多好多寓言，是个大艺术家。
我呢，特别强调在庄子哲学里边的两个概念，一个概念，大家可能比较陌生的，说起来有点绕口，少少的五个字里边有三个是同一个字，叫物质的物，他的哲学概念叫“物物者非物”，这就是庄子的一个非常重要的概念。
什么叫“物物者非物”？第一个物是动词，它指的是创造事物的一种力量，物物者，就创造事物的人，创造物质的人，他本身不是物质。“物物者非物”，大家能够理解我讲的意思吗？让物成为物的那种力量，本身并不是物。也就是我们要成为造物者，造物者不是物，这个观念我们一定要认真地体会一下。
他在《秋水篇》里边专门讲了个概念，他的概念如果用我们现在的话讲，就是我们要以人的立场来看物，不要以物的立场来看物。什么叫以物的立场来看物？就是我的存款是300万，他的存款是400万，以此来判断我们的等级的话，就是以物论物了。庄子说不，我们要以道来论物，以人来论物，这个观念是庄子的一个重要思维。
我们今天讲到这。
transcriptEn:
Hello everyone, I am Yu Qiuyu, let’s continue the lecture.
Last time, I summed up Lao Tzu's idea of ​​walking on the road, complementing each other, governing by doing nothing, being in harmony with the light, and keeping a low profile until the end. This whole thought was finally summarized into a very high-level thought, called the Supreme Good Like Water. It is not a strategy, it is a supreme good, which is exactly the opposite of conspiracy. This is how we have a new understanding of Lao Tzu. I said at the end of the last time that many famous ideas in the world have helped me in my life, but the one that has helped me the most is Lao Tzu's idea of ​​being as good as water, nourishing all things without fighting, always being in a low position, and smiling quietly at all things. This kind of thinking is the best way of thinking, and it helps me a lot.
Restore the true face of Laozi’s philosophy
In my life, many confusions can be easily solved because of this philosophy. Students often ask me, teacher, why do you ignore the temptation of a high position, ignore all kinds of external provocations, and still insist on writing every day, writing for decades, publishing books one after another, and completely ignoring the noise outside? How can you do this? And he ignores the temptations from the outside, doesn’t join any associations, and doesn’t participate in any conferences. How could this be?
I always give my students a faint smile and then talk about water, Lao Tzu’s water. Students will ask, he said, teacher, since you talked about water, we are reminded of a metaphor, a Chinese idiom, which is called water dripping through a stone. If you use water to drip through the stone, you will win. I said no, there is no such thing as victory here. Because of the idea of ​​water dripping through stone, water does not regard the stone as an enemy or opponent, or even regards the stone as an object at all; passing through the stone, or in other words, passing through the stone, is not an expected design, but a natural arrangement. This natural arrangement is the natural arrangement of the heavenly bodies, and this is the Tao.
We write slowly and talk slowly. It takes decades to penetrate something. This is not our goal, because we do not think that there is a stone in front of us as the object of our struggle. I must slowly use water droplets to penetrate it. If this is the case, my water droplets are too slow. Why don’t I be water? Let’s be strong men and move the stone away. Isn’t this simpler? There is no strategy of hiding for a long time as we imagined, dealing with an opponent, but in the end, our quiet side won. Because according to Laozi's philosophy, there is no victory or defeat, we just nourish all things.
After I said this, everyone will understand that we cannot turn Lao Tzu's great kindness into great hypocrisy and hypocrisy, nor can we turn Lao Tzu's great way into evil. I have seen many, many knowledgeable scholars. When they wrote about Lao Tzu, they all said with a smile that I was a cunning old man, a conspirator, etc. They were all wrong. This is very sorry for me.
Lao Tzu is the originator of the idea of ​​benefiting all things without fighting, and the originator of the idea that the best is as good as water. Therefore, as a scholar and a cultural person, it is an academic responsibility for me, as well as a moral responsibility, to restore Lao Tzu's original intention. Especially since I have been so well influenced by Lao Tzu, this has become a life responsibility. I think my students should do the same. We should understand Lao Tzu's great thinking of the Supreme Good in a positive way.
There are a lot of conspiracy theories in our Chinese culture. In fact, there were not that many conspiracies in Chinese history, at least not as many as what we write in TV dramas now. Not that many, so I often tell my friends in New York and give lectures in New York. Several of my friends in New York said, We also wanted to understand Chinese culture, so we finally watched a few Chinese TV series that had been translated into English. After watching them, we were horrified. Why are there so many conspiracies in China? Every step, every smiling face, and every beautiful palace maid in the palace is a conspirator.
I said, no, there are not that many conspiracies in China. This was imagined by the official historians of the past and later by our lovely contemporary screenwriters. I said, you see, there are indeed many conspiracies written in Chinese history books, but there are only a few conspiracies over hundreds of years. The Chinese people do not know about this conspiracy, because for a long time, the Chinese people were more illiterate, and they could not read or see clearly. I said that I lived in the countryside when I was a child, and later worked in the countryside for a long time. I also worked on the farm during the Cultural Revolution. I know Chinese farmers very well. I told my friends in New York that Chinese farmers really don’t have many conspiracies. Their shortcomings are that they are stingy, stingy, and not hygienic. These are just a few shortcomings. There is little conspiracy. If there is a conspiracy, it may be a little comparison and a little conservative, that's all.
On this issue, when we study Chinese philosophy, we must understand that our chief philosopher, Lao Tzu, is wrong to misrepresent him as a conspirator. He is a person who spreads the highest morals. Water benefits all things without fighting. This is such a thinking. China should popularize this kind of thinking into our lives. Our inaction is not a conspiracy, our opposites and mutual complementation are not a conspiracy, and our keeping a low profile is not a conspiracy. The reason is that I am not a conspiracy. In this way I have explained what I have said more completely.
Zhuangzi's philosophy: Things are not things.
Next, I will undoubtedly talk about Zhuangzi. As for Zhuangzi, in the Taoist view, the leader is Laozi, and Zhuangzi is not regarded as the leader. But in fact, Zhuangzi is by Laozi's side. I don't mean by his side in terms of time, but by his side in philosophy. Being by his side constitutes a relatively complete philosophy called Laozi and Zhuangzi. They are actually separated by a relatively long time, but they form a kind of Lao-Zhuang philosophy. This Lao-Zhuang philosophy is probably inseparable from Zhuangzi when we look at the thinking of their Taoist leaders and the philosophical foundation of their religion.
Zhuangzi, I want to make it shorter, because I made it longer. Anyway, as you all know, I specifically wrote some articles on Zhuangzi in the book "Lectures at Peking University", and I continued to discuss and copy Zhuangzi. Copying Zhuangzi means writing Zhuangzi's things into calligraphy. I wrote "Xiaoyaoyou" in cursive and also translated Zhuangzi. It is not difficult for readers to find this, so I, Zhuangzi, can talk about it more briefly. Because I like Zhuangzi very much, I may have lost the space in the first lecture, and I talked too much as I went on.
Everyone still remembers that I once ranked the literary qualities of the pre-Qin scholars. I put Zhuangzi first, Mencius second, Laozi third, and Confucius fourth. Everyone still has an impression of this. The great Confucius is so great, why did you put it fourth? I also gave the reason, because we are not talking about philosophical thinking and influence, we are talking about literary taste. Zhuangzi, with the unfamiliar eyes of a child, asked many questions instead of answering many questions on a high platform. He asked questions and then gave overall answers in a child's way. This is an artist, and the way he used it was allegory, allegory, allegory. There were many, many allegories. He was a great artist.
I particularly emphasize two concepts in Zhuangzi's philosophy. One concept may be unfamiliar to you, and it is a bit confusing to talk about. Three of the five words in Shaoshao are the same word, called material things. His philosophical concept is called "things are not things". This is a very important concept of Zhuangzi.
What is "things are not things"? The first thing is a verb, which refers to a force that creates things. The person who creates things is the person who creates things. The person who creates matter is not a matter itself. "Things are not things." Do you understand what I mean? The power that makes a thing a thing is not itself a thing. That is to say, we must become creators, and creators are not things. We must seriously understand this concept.
He specifically talked about a concept in "Autumn Waters". If his concept is expressed in our current terms, it means that we should look at things from the standpoint of humans, not from the standpoint of things. What does it mean to look at things from their perspective? That is, my deposit is 3 million, and his deposit is 4 million. If we judge our level based on this, we are judging things based on things. Zhuangzi said no, we must use Tao to judge things and people to judge things. This concept is an important thinking of Zhuangzi.
We're talking about this today.

summary.gistZh: 庄子哲学强调突破人类自我中心主义，以万物平等的视角审视自然与人生，追求超脱世俗名利的精神自由（逍遥游）。
summary.gistEn: Zhuangzi's philosophy emphasizes transcending human anthropocentrism, viewing nature and life through absolute equality, and pursuing spiritual freedom ('Carefree Wandering') beyond worldly fame and wealth.

highlights.zh: 万物平等视角：从「人的立场」转向「自然的立场」，打破人为划分的贵贱与成败。
highlights.en: Equality of All Things: Shifting from a human-centric stance to a natural stance, breaking down artificial distinctions of status and success.

highlights.zh: 老子与庄子的继承：老子讲「上善若水、滋润万物而不争」，庄子将其延伸为个体精神的绝对自由。
highlights.en: Laozi & Zhuangzi Connection: Laozi espouses 'supreme goodness is like water—nourishing all things without conflict', which Zhuangzi expands into absolute individual spiritual freedom.

highlights.zh: 逍遥游的精神境界：不受外界毁誉和实用功利的羁绊，实现心灵的彻底解放。
highlights.en: Spirit of 'Carefree Wandering': Unfettered by external praise, blame, or utilitarian gain, achieving complete liberation of the soul.

highlights.zh: 对现代人的启示：在功利竞争激烈的社会中，庄子给中国心灵提供了一剂精神解毒剂。
highlights.en: Relevance Today: In a hyper-competitive, utilitarian society, Zhuangzi offers a vital spiritual antidote for the human mind.

title: 君子人格：理想化的人格结构
folderName: 03_君子人格：理想化的人格结构
audioPath: 03_君子人格：理想化的人格结构/audio.m4a
quoteCardPath: 03_君子人格：理想化的人格结构/quote_card.jpg
transcriptZh:
大家好，我是余秋雨，我们正好在讲中国文化的人格结构。人格结构，我们首先要遇到的一个最重要的人格结构，叫做君子人格。那我上一次曾经把君子人格和世界上其他的集体人格，比如像绅士人格、骑士人格、武士人格，可能还有牛仔人格等等这些人格作对比了，我们中国无可替代的是君子人格。
暗礁与海床
这里边牵涉到一个西方的概念，叫做集体无意识。就是我们进入这个人格以后，大家都没有意识到我们进入了，但是你已经进入了，所以有的时候无意识也说成是潜意识。那么这个最早应该是弗洛伊德提出来的，但是他的学生后来也是他的对手的荣格，我已经讲过好几次，中文翻译光荣的荣，及格的格，心理学家荣格，对弗洛伊德的学说有一点矫正，他认为重要的并不是深层的潜意识，重要的是它的集体性，集体的无意识，这个才重要。
那么我所说的人格也是一种集体的无意识，大家无意识地进入了一种人格结构，这不是浮在表面上的，不是你考学位、背古诗能够体现得出来的。它是暗礁，所以国际学术界有个说法，说弗洛伊德找到了大海波涛下的暗礁，而荣格找到了暗礁底下的海床！这个比喻，比较大，也比较深入。有一点难，大家听听吧。就是弗洛伊德找到了人类心理这个波涛下的暗礁，而荣格找到了暗礁底下的海床。
我用我们大家比较习惯的说法来说，也是荣格的一个说法了。所谓集体人格为什么走到海床呢，就是我们找到了叫做有故乡的灵魂，或者反过来讲也一样，找到了有灵魂的故乡。那我们所说的集体人格，不管是君子还是什么集体人格，其实并不是形成于我们的有生之年。所以我们为什么说是集体潜意识，它形成的时候，并不是我们出生以后慢慢的一点点形成的。
对一个民族来说，最早的种子可能在神话时代已经播下了。每一个古老的民族都有很多大神话，后来又会引发出很多小神话。这些大神话、小神话，我们经常会把它说成是一个民族的梦，或者说成是原型、原始意象，然后组合变成了一个民族的自画像，反复地出现在集体的心理活动当中。
请大家注意，我说的是一个民族的自画像反复地出现在我们的集体心理活动当中，那么我们心底也埋藏着一个民族的自画像，我们尽管自己感觉不到它存在。大神话，比如不管你知道不知道，我们每一个中国人心底其实多埋藏着女娲补天、精卫填海、夸父逐日、嫦娥奔月等等这些神话，它是我们的心理故乡。我们的很多很多心理是由他们作为原始因素慢慢建立的，后来就变成了一个非常复杂的人类学工程了。我们现代的很多学者对这一点还不太了解，总以为我们的教育就能够改变我们思想当中的一切，总以为我们看几本书，就能把我们的人格结构都变化了，我们听几个故事，就会把我们的心理走向逆反了，其实不是这样的。
东方文明的独特人格
我们现在的学者按照现在的科学思维，经常把这个问题有点看浅了。这里我可以举个例子，就是我前面不断的讲到荣格，那么当时中国有一个大学者去拜访了他，拜访了荣格，这个人就是我们谁都知道的胡适，胡适之先生。我们很尊重的胡适之先生，他比较早的向我们中国传达了西方的文明，传达了很多重要的思想。
他去拜访荣格，荣格一见面就问他，你对《易经》怎么看？胡适之非常惊讶，他怎么知道《易经》？胡适告诉他，这个我不太相信，这个《易经》好像是魔术和符咒。如果说你居然认为《易经》是魔术和符咒，你有没有尝试过用它来观察我们的生活。胡适点头，点头以后还认为这是魔术和符咒。这时候荣格深深一叹，不断地问他有关《易经》的问题，而且荣格在书里边说，中国的当代学者已经渐渐地走向了西方的科学境界，对他们自己的传统文化已经产生了深深的怀疑。胡适之先生，他基本上属于现代的，被荣格所说的对自己的文化产生了深深怀疑的这样的一群学者，他的功劳很大，但是他的局限也非常明显。
那一天，胡适之先生完全不知道荣格对中国文化的研究深度，他不知道这个坐在眼前的荣格，他曾经为有个叫威廉翻译的《易经》的译本，他写了17页的引言，而且这个荣格在这篇引言里边说，中国的《易经》和中国古代的科学，它是紧紧连在一起的，而且比现代的西方科学的因果律高出很多。因果律，靠的只不过是统计，数字统计。如果按照中国古代的智慧，那情况就完全不一样了。譬如荣格指出物极必反，这么个基本法则就高出于西方的以自我为中心的这种人格结构。因为荣格是研究人格的，他也介绍人格结构，他认为《易经》已经改变了西方的对于人格的这种思维方式，中国建立的是另外一种人格。因为胡适比荣格小了十六岁，无论在年龄的辈分上，还是在学术的辈分上，他都不能和荣格相比。
那天胡适之先生说的有点草率了，但是他这个草率有个好处，让荣格非常着急。所以今后只要一有机会，他一写书总是劝告中国文明，不要跟着西方文明跑。他反复地讲这句话，那么其实在胡适之时代，也有一些人很明白，我们的东方文明有自己独特的人格结构，不要完全跟着西方跑。我曾经看到过孙中山先生在日本的一个演讲。孙中山先生，他说日本的人格结构很奇怪，既有西方的霸道文化，又有东方的王道文化。那么我希望你们认真地对自己的人格结构作出选择，到底选王道还是选霸道你们自己要审慎。
后来有一个日本企业家，就前些年不多久，他在天津有个演讲，他说遗憾的是我们日本没有走上孙中山所说的那个王道文化这条路，反而走上了一条既有西方文化，又有东方文化的不良的两个面的组合，所以就走到邪路上去了。这是一个日本企业家的一个说法。但是他们这些谈论说来说去全部都在讲集体人格，大家听懂了没有？就是我们无论在讲胡适之和荣格他们两个人的讨论，也无论说孙中山在日本的演讲，这讨论来讨论去都在讲一个民族的集体人格。
我觉得在这个问题上已经大体已经说明，君子人格和其他人格结构的不一样的重要性，到底最后的界限在哪里？中国把君子作为一个理想化的人格结构。那这个平心而论，它几乎把中国文化的好多精华都吸附到自己身上了，都吸附到君子之道里边了。如果了解了君子之道，中国文化的很多成分都能建立，如果没有君子之道，好多都是徒劳的了。
所以对于儒家来说，它说了千言万语，儒家的学者在中国历史上也是成群结队，但是如果说他们讲了那么多那么多话，归根结底是一句什么话，就是要做个君子，这才是一个最合格的中国人。我再讲一遍，儒家千言万语，它讲的最后一句话是做个君子，这也是最合格的中国人。
好，今天讲到这。
transcriptEn:
Hello everyone, my name is Yu Qiuyu, and we are just talking about the personality structure of Chinese culture. Personality structure, the first and most important personality structure we have to encounter is called gentleman personality. Well, last time I compared the gentleman personality with other collective personalities in the world, such as gentleman personality, knight personality, warrior personality, and maybe cowboy personality, etc. The irreplaceable thing in China is the gentleman personality.
Reefs and seabed
This involves a Western concept called collective unconsciousness. Even after we enter this personality, no one realizes that we have entered, but you have already entered, so sometimes the unconscious is also called the subconscious. So this should have been proposed by Freud first, but his student and later his opponent Jung, I have talked about it several times. The Chinese translation of Glorious Jung, Passing Pass, the psychologist Jung, made some corrections to Freud's theory. He believed that what is important is not the deep subconscious, but its collective nature, the collective unconscious, which is important.
So the personality I am talking about is also a kind of collective unconsciousness. Everyone has entered a personality structure unconsciously. This is not superficial, and it cannot be reflected by taking a degree exam or memorizing ancient poems. It is a reef, so there is a saying in the international academic community that Freud found the reef under the waves of the sea, and Jung found the seabed under the reef! This metaphor is relatively large and in-depth. It’s a bit difficult, so please listen to it. It was Freud who found the reef beneath the waves of human psychology, and Jung found the seabed beneath the reef.
I use the term that we are all more accustomed to, and it is also a Jungian term. The reason why the so-called collective personality has reached the seabed is that we have found a soul called a hometown, or conversely, we have found a hometown with a soul. Then what we call collective personality, whether it is a gentleman or any collective personality, is not actually formed in our lifetime. So why do we call it the collective subconscious? When it was formed, it did not form slowly bit by bit after we were born.
For a nation, the earliest seeds may have been sown in the age of myth. Every ancient nation has many big myths, which later lead to many small myths. We often describe these big myths and small myths as the dream of a nation, or as prototypes and primitive images, and then combine them into a self-portrait of a nation, which appears repeatedly in collective psychological activities.
Please note that what I am talking about is that the self-portrait of a nation appears repeatedly in our collective psychological activities, so there is also a self-portrait of a nation buried deep in our hearts, even though we cannot feel its existence. Big myths, for example, whether you know it or not, there are actually many myths buried in the heart of each of us Chinese, such as Nuwa filling the sky, Jingwei filling the sea, Kuafu chasing the sun, Chang'e flying to the moon, etc. It is our psychological hometown. Much of our psychology was slowly built up from them as primitive factors, and later it became a very complex anthropological project. Many of our modern scholars don’t know much about this. They always think that our education can change everything in our thoughts. They always think that if we read a few books, our personality structure will be changed, and if we listen to a few stories, our psychology will be reversed. In fact, this is not the case.
The unique personality of Eastern civilization
According to the current scientific thinking, our current scholars often take this issue a bit lightly. I can give you an example here. I have been talking about Jung before. At that time, a great scholar in China went to visit him and Jung. This person was Hu Shi, Mr. Hu Shizhi, whom all of us know. Mr. Hu Shizhi, whom we respect very much, conveyed Western civilization to China relatively early and conveyed many important ideas.
He went to visit Jung, and Jung asked him as soon as they met, what do you think of the "I Ching"? Hu Shizhi was very surprised. How did he know the "Book of Changes"? Hu Shi told him that I don't really believe this. This "Book of Changes" seems to be magic and spells. If you actually think that the "Book of Changes" is magic and spells, have you ever tried to use it to observe our lives? Hu Shi nodded. After nodding, he thought it was magic and a spell. At this time, Jung sighed deeply and kept asking him questions about the "Book of Changes". Moreover, Jung said in the book that contemporary Chinese scholars have gradually moved towards the Western scientific realm and have developed deep doubts about their own traditional culture. Mr. Hu Shizhi basically belongs to the modern group of scholars who Jung said were deeply suspicious of their own culture. He has made great contributions, but his limitations are also very obvious.
On that day, Mr. Hu Shizhi had no idea about the depth of Jung's research on Chinese culture. He didn't know that Jung was sitting in front of him. He had written a 17-page introduction for a translation of the "Book of Changes" by William Translator. In addition, Jung said in this introduction that the Chinese "Book of Changes" and ancient Chinese science are closely connected, and the law of cause and effect is much higher than that of modern Western science. The law of cause and effect only relies on statistics and numerical statistics. If we follow ancient Chinese wisdom, the situation would be completely different. For example, Jung pointed out that things must reverse themselves when they reach their extremes. This basic law is higher than the self-centered personality structure of the West. Because Jung studied personality, he also introduced personality structure. He believed that the "Book of Changes" had changed the Western way of thinking about personality, and China established a different kind of personality. Because Hu Shi was sixteen years younger than Jung, he could not compare with Jung in terms of age or academic seniority.
What Mr. Hu Shizhi said that day was a bit hasty, but his haste had an advantage, which made Jung very anxious. Therefore, whenever he has the opportunity in the future, he will always advise Chinese civilization not to follow Western civilization when he writes a book. He said this repeatedly, so in fact, in Hu Shi's era, some people understood very well that our Eastern civilization has its own unique personality structure and should not completely follow the West. I once saw a speech given by Mr. Sun Yat-sen in Japan. Mr. Sun Yat-sen, he said that Japan has a very strange personality structure, with both Western hegemonic culture and Eastern kingly culture. Then I hope you will make a serious choice about your personality structure. You should be careful whether you choose to be kingly or domineering.
Later, a Japanese entrepreneur gave a speech in Tianjin not long ago. He said that unfortunately, Japan did not follow the path of kingly culture mentioned by Sun Yat-sen, but instead embarked on a bad combination of Western culture and Eastern culture, so it went down the wrong path. This is a saying from a Japanese entrepreneur. But all their discussions are about collective personality. Do you understand? That is, whether we are talking about the discussion between Hu Shizhi and Jung, or whether we are talking about Sun Yat-sen's speech in Japan, these discussions are all about the collective personality of a nation.
I think this issue has been roughly explained on the different importance of a gentleman's personality and other personality structures. Where is the final limit? China regards the gentleman as an ideal personality structure. To be fair, it has absorbed almost all the essence of Chinese culture into itself, into the way of a gentleman. If you understand the way of a gentleman, many elements of Chinese culture can be established. If you don’t have the way of a gentleman, many elements of Chinese culture will be in vain.
So for Confucianism, it has said thousands of words. Confucian scholars have also been in groups in Chinese history, but if they say so many words, in the final analysis, they say one thing, that is, to be a gentleman, this is the most qualified Chinese. Let me say it again, Confucianism has a thousand words, but the last word it talks about is to be a gentleman, which is also the most qualified Chinese person.
Okay, that’s it for today.

summary.gistZh: 「君子人格」是中国文化独一无二的核心集体人格，不同于西方的绅士或骑士，它注重内在道德修养、社会责任感与中庸圆融。
summary.gistEn: The 'Junzi' (Noble Person) is Chinese culture's unique core collective personality—unlike Western gentlemen or knights, it emphasizes inner moral cultivation, social responsibility, and harmonious balance.

highlights.zh: 集体人格对比：对比西方绅士人格、骑士人格与日本武士人格，君子是中国文化的独特标志。
highlights.en: Collective Personality Comparison: Compared to Western gentlemen, medieval knights, or Japanese samurai, the Junzi is the indispensable symbol of Chinese civilization.

highlights.zh: 君子的核心标准：德行第一、重义轻利、文质彬彬，兼具社会担当与个修养。
highlights.en: Core Criteria of a Junzi: Virtue first, valuing righteousness over profit, cultured yet refined, combining social duty with self-cultivation.

highlights.zh: 君子与小人的界限：小人同而不和、择利而动；君子和而不同、择善而固执。
highlights.en: Junzi vs. Xiaoren (Petty Person): The petty person seeks uniformity without harmony for profit; the Junzi seeks harmony without conformity for virtue.

highlights.zh: 文化的避风港：即便历史遭遇劫难，只要君子人格尚存，中国文明的火种就不会熄灭。
highlights.en: Cultural Sanctuary: Even during historical catastrophes, as long as the Junzi ideal endures, the embers of Chinese civilization remain alive.

title: 中庸之道：数千年的集体选择
folderName: 04_中庸之道：数千年的集体选择
audioPath: 04_中庸之道：数千年的集体选择/audio.m4a
quoteCardPath: 04_中庸之道：数千年的集体选择/quote_card.jpg
transcriptZh:
上一次，我终于把中国文化长寿的第六原因淡化竞争讲完了，现在我要进入到第七个原因，叫防范极端。这个原因是中国文化长寿最重要的原因。我讲了八个原因，但是最重要的原因就是这第七个原因。我现在光这么一讲，大家还不明白，我细细地讲下去大家就清楚了。
中国文化在所有同龄的文化一一凋零之后，它还能够磕磕绊绊的一直走下来，走到今天，还会不断走下去的一个非常重要的原因，就是我们这种文化在基本思路上防范极端。实际上知道的人都明白，我就是在讲中庸之道。对于中庸之道我讲过很多次，但是在课堂当中我要非常明确地讲，这是我对中国文化的一个核心价值的把握，我觉得中国文化非常重要的一点就是中庸之道。
中庸之道和极端主义
“中”是中间值的意思；“庸”指的是寻常态，也就是普通老百姓的状态，也可以理解为平庸状态。因为寻常状态，其实也就是普通的延续状态。我再讲一遍，“中庸”两个字，“中”指的是中间值，“庸”指的是寻常态和延续态。这个清楚了以后，我们就知道中国文化非常长寿的原因就是，它在一切大的问题上都取中间值，都取寻常态，然后求得延续。这个看起来只是一种工作方法，其实它是一种重要的思维选择。
表面上看，它是一种办事方式，我们在做事情的时候总是要向前看，把事情做成功。但是，要把事情真的做成功，就要回过头来看一看比较正常的一般情形，要设法找一条合适的路、恰当的路、可行的路，多数人能够接受的路。我再讲一遍，你要办成事情，当然要往前看。你在往前看的时候，你又要把头回过来，看一看比较正常的一般情形，找一条合适的路、恰当的路、可行的路，多数人都能接受的路。
要做到这样，你就不应该扮演激烈，不应该哗众取宠。在哲学上说的高深一点，这种弹性哲学是一种灵活的松软状态，一种平静的两相妥协，一种灰色的宽厚地带，这是中华文化几千年来的精神主轴和行为主轴。
所以，我对“中庸”这两个字在中国文化史上的地位非常看重，而且我认为就是这种弹性哲学，就是这种松软状态，就是这种宽厚地带，把中国文化一直引下来，走过了几千年，一直走到今天，还会不断地走下去。
中国文化历史那么长，遭受的灾祸那么多，在很多时候好像走不下去了，那就像世界上其他伟大的文明终于在那一天倒地不起一样。但奇怪的是，中国却一次一次的都走通了，越过了灾难，越过了灭亡，一步一步地存活下来。仔细地看，他在每一个生死关口到底是怎么样转变过来的？中庸起到了很重要的作用。
中庸为什么能够避祸呢？这一点我在世界各地一讲，往往会迎来掌声。我说，中庸你们光以为是中国的一个哲学概念，我告诉你，中庸最根本的思路是反对一切极端主义。
我想告诉大家的是，极端主义非常有魅力，极端主义它的可怕就可怕在它非常有魅力。如果极端主义从里到外都是很丑陋的话，那它就不可怕了。它可怕的是，它往往像站在悬崖峭壁上的普罗米修斯，往往像一个不怕牺牲的好汉，浑身散发着英雄的光辉，他们的口号是那么的响亮，那么的爽利，令人感动。因此，极端主义总是拥有大量的追随者、崇拜者、死忠者，劝也劝不回。
我们也曾经历过这样的极端主义，比如近代有义和团，在当代有“文革”。极端主义的这些代表人物，当他刚刚出现的时候，确实让人感觉到是站在悬崖峭壁边上的好汉，讲的话是那么的响亮，那么的动听，那么的让人忍不住想喊口号。但是对于广大民众来说，口号不是路标，好汉不是向导，悬崖不是大道。对于这些在悬崖峭壁边上的好汉来说，其实已经没路。为什么站在悬崖峭壁边上呢？因为他已经没地方可以走了，他们还会闹腾一阵子，但是事情本质上已经结束。
这是一种响亮的短命，激烈的速朽。极端主义者不但会隔断时间速朽了，而且会隔断空间。他们迟早连那些追随者、劝告者、谏言者、修正者也无法容忍，而且把这些人都当作叛逆者一一驱逐，孤苦伶仃地固守着越来越狭小的所谓原教旨主义。于是，他们空间的局促又加剧了时间的局促，所以灭亡是不可避免的。
文化本能
中庸和他们一比，就没有那么让人感动的好汉形象了。中庸总是那么平淡、那么家常、那么低调，引不来任何喝彩和欢呼。中庸只是在轻脚慢步地四处探问，只是在轻声慢语地商量劝说，但是过不久，一条小路找到了，一种谅解达成了，一番口舌省掉了，一场恶斗躲过了。看起来好像什么也没有发生，只不过大家可以活下去了，而且是以平顺快乐的方式活下去了。
中华文化在整体上拒绝极端主义，信奉中庸。我在《君子之道》这本书当中，曾经介绍了古代经典在这个问题上反复的教导，这一教导非常有效，几千年来已经深入到了大地人心。结果即使那些很容易陷入极端主义的外来宗教，一融入中华文化，就马上减去了杀伐之气，增添了圆融的风范。
中国也有一段时间一些人物，受到极端主义的蛊惑，但是这无法改变全体民众数千年的集体选择。所以极端主义在中国由于老被反对，一旦冒出来的时候，方式可能更加极端。但是再极端也没用，它只是过眼云烟。因为数千年的集体选择，沉淀成了集体人格。结果，中庸不是一种权宜之计，而是一种文化本能。
那么在各大文明当中，为什么中国能够全方位地实践中庸呢？说到底这还是和农耕文明有点关系。农耕文明是靠天吃饭，服从四季循环。你问乡下农民都知道，就是天气冷冷不到极端，冷到极端，春色已开；夏天热也热不到极端，热到极端，秋风又起。这种天人合一的思维经过《周易》的提升，又经过孔子他们的总结，就变成了一种文化共识。《礼记》里边更明确地做出了“君子中庸，小人反中庸”的经典宣判，这也就是在集体人格上道出了中国文化的基本准则，就是你如果反中庸的话，在人格上就不是真正的中国人。
世界上有一些其他宗教和哲学，也有过中庸的道理。比如像印度一个非常著名的龙树，我们有的时候叫龙树菩萨，他提出过中道，我在研究佛教的时候经常用到他的观念。但是，只有在中国中庸变成世俗生活当中的长久普及，变成了一个谁也无法忽略的实践状态。请记住，不是理论状态，而是实践状态。而且不是少数人的实践，是绝大多数中国普通百姓的世俗生活中的实践。
谢谢，我下次再讲下去。
transcriptEn:
Last time, I finally finished talking about the sixth reason for the longevity of Chinese culture and downplaying competition. Now I want to move on to the seventh reason, which is to guard against extremes. This reason is the most important reason for the longevity of Chinese culture. I talked about eight reasons, but the most important reason is the seventh reason. If I just talk about it now, you still don’t understand it. But if I explain it in detail, everyone will understand it.
After all the cultures of the same age have withered one by one, Chinese culture has been able to continue stumbling down. A very important reason why it will continue to go forward today is that our culture guards against extremes in its basic thinking. In fact, everyone who knows knows that I am talking about the golden mean. I have talked about the golden mean many times, but I want to make it very clear in class that this is my grasp of a core value of Chinese culture. I think a very important point in Chinese culture is the golden mean.
Moderation and extremism
"Zhong" means the middle value; "Yong" refers to the ordinary state, that is, the state of ordinary people, which can also be understood as the mediocre state. Because the ordinary state is actually an ordinary continued state. Let me say it again, the word "zhongyong", "zhong" refers to the middle value, and "yong" refers to the normal state and the continuation state. Once this is clear, we will know that the reason why Chinese culture has a very long life is that it takes the middle value and the normal state on all major issues, and then seeks continuation. This seems to be just a working method, but in fact it is an important thinking choice.
On the surface, it is a way of doing things. When we do things, we must always look forward and make things successful. However, if you want to really do something successfully, you have to look back at the more normal general situation, and try to find a suitable, appropriate, feasible way, a way that most people can accept. Let me say it again, if you want to accomplish something, of course you have to look ahead. When you look forward, you have to look back, take a look at the more normal general situation, and find a suitable way, a proper way, a feasible way, and a way that most people can accept.
To do this, you should not act intensely or be sensational. To put it more philosophically, this flexible philosophy is a flexible and soft state, a calm two-phase compromise, and a gray zone of generosity. This has been the spiritual and behavioral main axis of Chinese culture for thousands of years.
Therefore, I attach great importance to the position of the word "gold mean" in the history of Chinese culture, and I think it is this flexible philosophy, this soft state, and this zone of generosity that has led Chinese culture down through thousands of years to today, and will continue to do so.
Chinese culture has such a long history and has suffered so many disasters. At many times, it seems that it can no longer go on, just like other great civilizations in the world that finally collapsed on that day. But the strange thing is that China has made it through time and time again, overcoming disasters and destruction, and surviving step by step. Look carefully, how did he transform at each critical moment of life and death? Moderation plays a very important role.
Why can moderation avoid disaster? When I speak about this point around the world, I often receive applause. I said, you just think that Doctrine of the Mean is a Chinese philosophical concept. Let me tell you, the most fundamental idea of ​​Doctrine of the Mean is to oppose all extremism.
What I want to tell you is that extremism is very charming, and what is scary about extremism is that it is very charming. Extremism wouldn't be scary if it was ugly inside and out. The scary thing about it is that it is often like Prometheus standing on a cliff, often like a hero who is not afraid of sacrifice, exuding the glory of heroes, and their slogans are so loud, so refreshing, and touching. Therefore, extremism always has a large number of followers, admirers, and die-hard loyalists, and it is impossible to persuade them back.
We have also experienced such extremism, such as the Boxer Rebellion in modern times and the "Cultural Revolution" in contemporary times. When these representatives of extremism first appeared, they really made people feel like heroes standing on the edge of a cliff. Their words were so loud and melodious, and they made people want to shout slogans. But for the general public, slogans are not road signs, heroes are not guides, and cliffs are not highways. For these heroes on the edge of the cliff, there is actually no way out. Why are you standing on the edge of a cliff? Since he had no place to go, they would still have a fuss for a while, but the matter was essentially over.
This is a loud short-lived, fierce rapid decay. Extremists will not only block time and decay, but also block space. Sooner or later, they cannot even tolerate those followers, exhorters, remonstrators, and correctors, and expel these people one by one as rebels, clinging to an increasingly narrow so-called fundamentalism all alone. Therefore, their cramped space intensified their cramped time, so their demise was inevitable.
cultural instinct
Compared with them, Zhongyong doesn't have such a moving image of a hero. Moderation is always so plain, so homely, so low-key, and does not attract any cheers or cheers. Zhongyong was just walking slowly and slowly, asking around, just discussing and persuading in a low voice, but after a while, a path was found, an understanding was reached, a lot of words were saved, and a fierce fight was avoided. It seems like nothing happened, except that everyone can live on, and live on in a smooth and happy way.
Chinese culture as a whole rejects extremism and believes in moderation. In my book "The Way of the Gentleman", I introduced the repeated teachings of ancient classics on this issue. This teaching is very effective and has penetrated deeply into the hearts of the earth for thousands of years. As a result, even those foreign religions that easily fall into extremism lose their murderous spirit and gain a harmonious demeanor as soon as they integrate into Chinese culture.
There has been a period in China when some figures were bewitched by extremism, but this cannot change the collective choices of the entire people over thousands of years. Therefore, since extremism has always been opposed in China, once it emerges, its methods may become even more extreme. But it’s useless no matter how extreme it is, it’s just a passing cloud. Because of thousands of years of collective choices, collective personality has been precipitated. As a result, moderation is not an expedient but a cultural instinct.
So among all major civilizations, why can China practice moderation in all aspects? After all, this has something to do with farming civilization. Agricultural civilization depends on the weather and obeys the cycle of the four seasons. If you ask the farmers in the countryside, they all know that even if the weather is not extremely cold, if it is extremely cold, spring has bloomed; if it is not extremely hot in summer, if it is extremely hot, the autumn wind will start again. This thinking of the unity of nature and man has become a cultural consensus after the promotion of "Book of Changes" and the summary by Confucius and others. The "Book of Rites" more clearly makes the classic judgment that "a gentleman is against the mean, and a villain is against the mean." This also expresses the basic principle of Chinese culture in terms of collective personality, that is, if you are against the mean, you are not a true Chinese in terms of personality.
There are some other religions and philosophies in the world that also have the doctrine of moderation. For example, there is a very famous Nagarjuna in India, sometimes called Nagarjuna Bodhisattva. He proposed the Middle Way. I often use his concepts when studying Buddhism. However, it was only in China that Doctrine became a long-term popularization in secular life and became a practical state that no one can ignore. Remember, not a theoretical state, but a practical state. And it is not a practice of a few people, but a practice in the secular life of the vast majority of ordinary Chinese people.
Thank you, I will talk about it next time.

summary.gistZh: 「中庸之道」并非平庸妥协，而是数千年来中华民族在复杂历史环境下的集体生存智慧——寻找极致与偏激之间的黄金平衡点。
summary.gistEn: The 'Doctrine of the Mean' (Zhongyong) is not mediocre compromise, but thousands of years of collective survival wisdom—seeking the golden balance between extremes and radicalism.

highlights.zh: 中庸的真正含义：「中」指不偏不倚的精准适度，「庸」指常态与持久，结合即为可持续的最高智慧。
highlights.en: True Meaning of Zhongyong: 'Zhong' denotes unswerving balance and appropriateness, while 'Yong' signifies constancy; combined, they form sustainable supreme wisdom.

highlights.zh: 民族集体选择：经历无数战乱与变迁后，中华文明选择中庸作为维持大一统与社会稳定的社会契约。
highlights.en: Nation's Collective Choice: Through endless conflicts, Chinese civilization adopted moderation as a social contract for unity and stability.

highlights.zh: 反极端主义：警惕极端偏执与情绪化言行，用理性中和的力量化解矛盾。
highlights.en: Anti-Extremism: Guarding against radicalism and emotional fervor, resolving conflicts through rational, harmonizing strength.

highlights.zh: 现代价值：在分化加剧的世界中，中庸之道为国际沟通与社会治理提供了宝贵的协调智慧。
highlights.en: Modern Value: In a polarized world, the Doctrine of the Mean provides invaluable wisdom for international dialogue and governance.

title: 家国同构：大秩序和小秩序是不一样的
folderName: 05_家国同构：大秩序和小秩序是不一样的
audioPath: 05_家国同构：大秩序和小秩序是不一样的/audio.m4a
quoteCardPath: 05_家国同构：大秩序和小秩序是不一样的/quote_card.jpg
transcriptZh:
大家好，我是余秋雨。
我上次讲到秩序的问题，我们要严于秩序，这是我们祖先在很早很早的时候的一种构想。孔子奔波了那么长的时间，都在呼唤建立一种类似于周朝的秩序，它的秩序是以礼仪的方式来体现的。我上次讲到，各种文明都在追求秩序，但只有中国把秩序的建设当作了第一要务，秩序在我们生活当中有好多负面效应，我们怎么显得不自由、不情愿、不舒畅，因此我们老是要推倒旧秩序、建立新秩序。
但是像我这样的人，在年轻时候开始总想着要建立新秩序，完全没想到没秩序是怎么回事，而世界性的考察给了我很大的启发。我出去考察的时候，中国当时的社会情况还是不太好，还是非常贫困落后，还是脏乱差，到处都有这样的情况。也有很多地方没有秩序，但是我们真的没看到一个地方彻底的没有秩序将会是怎么样。
一整套的秩序
我去到一个国家的时候，他们的首都的公共汽车不停站，老的、少的、男的、女的，看到车开过来，就像猴子一样跳上跳下。对这我就非常非常惊讶了，怎么会不停站。 墓地就在城市的最当中，好多流浪汉甚至于越狱出来的人都住在那儿，警察没有权力去查，因为这是墓地。所有的建筑至少三分之一都没有封顶，钢筋都露在外面，已经十年了还是这样。你问他们，他们会说这样才让我们感觉到住在新房子里。这是乱说，实际上是为了避税。
这就叫做很无序了，但是我们又看到了更无序的情景。就是我刚才讲到那么一个国家里边，听说我们这几个人要去闯伊拉克，他们还开了隆重的欢送会欢送我们，欢送中国英雄，他们觉得我们怎么会到那些地方去？我说你们已经乱到这个程度了，里边又会乱到什么程度呢？老人家笑着说，你进去看看吧。后来大家看我的书就知道了，我们看到的情景确实是很恐怖了。
但是很多似乎实际上是很友好的国家，我们也看到难以想象的情景。譬如火车上、车窗上、车门上，吊着几千个游客，几千个乘客。好好的客车，买来以后就改装，改装成三层楼。最上的一层摇摇晃晃，坐的全是小学生。每天的车祸无穷无尽，这是严重的无序了。
这种无序会有一种非常快的蔓延程度，很难得到整治。我在南亚和西亚的一些历史国家考察的时候，经常看到这样的情景。那些城市里边到处都是灰尘，从十三四岁到七十几岁的男性，站在垃圾堆上，这垃圾堆大得你一看就是几十年没有清理了。站在垃圾队上的男人也都是灰尘，只有眼白和牙齿是白的。一批批站在那，他们在干什么？没干什么，只是互相看。你看我、我看你，也不多讲话，偶尔讲几句。
我们到了以后，他们觉得今天的好事情来了，都看着我们了。我问他们吃的是什么？他们说，有的时候政府和市长为了选举会发给他们一些粮食，发给他们一些饼啊什么的。他们都身强力壮，七十几岁还直挺挺地站在垃圾堆上，十三四岁年纪那么轻，身体当然非常好。和我一起去的同伴就想了一个问题，如果有一个市长或者一个区长让这些人弯下腰去，清理脚下几十年的垃圾，这块土地就属于他们了，让他们来耕种，那不就好了吗？我相信我们中国人都会有这个想法，我也有这个想法，把垃圾运走，填在一个什么地方，然后这块土地耕种一下，种上当地所需要的农产品，不就好了吗？
但是，接下来的问题就来了，如果要耕种这块土地的话，那么农具来自于何方？种子来自于何方？灌溉来自于何方？运输来自于何方？一切都没有。所以，仅仅是要清理一块小土地、种农作物，我们面对的是一整套的秩序，这个秩序就是系统工程，哪一个环节一脱落，整个系统全部垮台。
所以，我们现在在过一种比较正常的生活的时候，大家知道吗？每一种正常生活后面都躲藏着大量严密的秩序，只要一个螺丝扣不对，这个秩序就不存在了。所以建立秩序是多少年辛辛苦苦的积累，才能够支撑起来。所以凭这一点，我们一定要对我们的祖先表示某种感谢了。我看着外国那一批批站在垃圾堆上的男人，从十几岁到七十几岁的男人，只有眼白和牙齿是白的，我不能不一次次感谢我们华夏前辈的辛劳和守护。
大秩序和小秩序
但是要建立秩序，这些站在垃圾堆上的人，和我们中国古代的一般的老百姓一样，他们是建立不起强有力的欲望的。为什么要建立秩序呢？你们建立秩序以后多麻烦，我们怎么能成为秩序过程当中的螺丝钉呢？
在这种情况下面，孔子有了一个非常好的构想，他这个构想就是大的秩序一定要用一个小的秩序来说服，用一个小的秩序来做示范，由一个小的秩序来进行试点。小的秩序的完整、小的秩序的圆满，一定能够带来大的秩序的完整和圆满。所以孔子创造了一个建立秩序的很好的构思，这个构思我们叫做“家国同构”，就是把家庭和国家放进同一个结构系统当中来进行比拟。
家庭的秩序是由血缘、辈分、长幼、排行、婚嫁来逐一设定的，所以非常清晰。从这种秩序派生出来的礼仪、规矩也是人所共知的。那么如果把这些家庭秩序逐一地放大、外移、扩散，成为社会秩序呢？如果用这个来成为国家秩序呢？就是从天然的家庭秩序，慢慢地扩大成社会秩序和国家秩序，这个想法使他们非常兴奋，所以他们提出了一个由家到国的程序，叫做修身齐家治国平天下。把齐家和治国连在一起了，家齐了，国家也治了。也就是说，一个以私人的空间秩序比较着公共的空间秩序的工程就启动了。这个工程就是我所说的“家国同构”。
这就使建立社会秩序和国家秩序的一条逻辑的桥梁搭建起来了。搭建这个桥梁的人开始很可能只是爱家、爱亲人，但是慢慢地衍生开去，从自己的老人想到外面的老人，从自己的孩子想到外面的孩子，这样一点点地衍生开去的时候，家庭秩序就变成了社会秩序的一种模型了。在中国古代的经典之作《周易》里边有一段话，其中把家和国混成了一个持续的构想，我读一下：
有天地，然后有万物；有万物，然后有男女；有男女，然后有夫妻；有夫妻，然后有父子；有父子，然后有君臣；有君臣，然后有上下；有上下，然后礼仪有所错。
它是把天地万物的秩序、家庭的秩序、性别的秩序、父子的秩序和君臣的秩序连在一起了。这个连接有个好处是，把天地的秩序和家庭的秩序放在前面，把君臣的秩序说成是派生的一种秩序，这和后来的君王所设想的不一样。
但是这种家国同构的工程，确实也存在着很多问题。那问题在于哪呢？就是社会正义不能混同于家庭的内规，政治的理性不可能出自于家长的判断。明末清初那些启蒙思想者，就是我所说的黄宗羲、顾炎武、王夫之这些人，他们就一直讲到，广大民众没有理由像原谅自己的老父亲一样，去原谅那个皇帝。国家要提防滑到家天下的泥潭当中，这是启蒙主义反复提出的，也是对“家国同构”这个构思的一个非常重要的矫正。
在中国古代确实是这样，“家国同构”的“国”主要是指朝廷，和我们现在讲的祖国什么不太一样，他们很少考虑到公共空间。在古代讲到国的时候，这个国主要指朝廷，很少考虑到公共空间。因此，他们也考虑不到那些站在垃圾堆上无所事事的人群。这个问题后来欧洲倒是解决的很好。公共空间的问题，我以后专门要讲。这个问题欧洲解决的比我们要好，虽然我们很长寿，但是我们的游客到了欧洲去旅游、到了外地去，经常会出现好多汗颜的事情。所以我们的“家国同构”里边就产生了一个非常大的裂痕，就是社会的大秩序和家庭的小秩序是不一样的。
我过去经常到上海的一些房子里边，看到上海好多小市民都这样，家里边那真叫做非常干净，也非常美观。但是就在一扇门之外，所有的垃圾都扔在那儿，所有的破烂都扔在那儿，互相之间都不管。公共空间要踮着脚走，敲开门以后，里面才是美丽的私人空间。所以家国同构其实只是象征，很难说完全解决了问题。原因很简单，因为在古典社会、在封建社会里边，国的概念是不具体的，它不是我们现在理解的公共空间。当国只是理解成朝廷的话，你的“家国同构”只是要求人们像对自己的家长一样去面对皇帝，如果是这样的一个思维，关于公共秩序的建立的问题就非常大了。
在中国古代，儒家有温馨的“家国同构”的想法，但是法家就不一样了，它要建立社会秩序的话，用的是非常厉害的手段，它用的是防范天下。当然，它的手段是很有效。尽管好多统治者口头上用的是儒家的话语，但实际上使用的却是法家的权术。后来，秩序虽然建立了，文明虽然延续了，但是这种秩序却打上了某种不好的朝廷的烙印，并且这种烙印也同样长寿，所以这个就是多年以来我们要来纠正中华文明的各种各样弊病的时候，需要注意的。它确实带来了中国文明的延续，带来了中国文化的长寿，但是他也同时带来了和它有关的另一种不良因素的长寿，这是中国文化需要不断改进的内容。
简化思维
我现在已经讲了四个秘密了，地大人多，从不远征，追求统一，严于秩序，这几个都是比较大的方面，但这几个大的方面还没有完全涉及到我们的文化本体。我们讲的是一个宏观的选择，中华文化在宏观的历史上、在宏观的社会走向上，做了刚才讲的这种选择、这种定位。有的不是选择，确实是自己存在，比如地大人多；不远征、求统一、求秩序，这是我们认真的选择。
但是这一切落实在文化本体上，就会产生哪一些很好的特长，使中华文化长寿下去呢？这也是中华文化的优势，这个本体上的特点我上次宣布过，我现在再讲一下，一个就是简化思维，另外一个是淡化竞争，还有个是防范极端，最后一个是实行科举，这些我慢慢地一点点讲下去。
现在我先讲一点就是简化思维，因为这一点一定会引起一些人的不理解。因为我们现在好多学者喜欢把中国古代的那些典籍说得非常复杂、非常艰深，就像我前面讲到的那些总裁国学班，拉了厚厚的窗帘，一讲讲几个月，慢慢地在讲，好像里边有多少极复杂的秘密需要在这个黑屋子里边，不能让大家偷听到，需要一点一点的破解。其实中国文化能够长寿的本体原因，一打头上来就是简明。
中华文化一直保持着一种瘦精精、乐呵呵的行者的形象，什么叫行者的形象呢？大家还记得我前面讲过活到很高寿很高寿的那个黄宗羲吗？直刺那个杀害自己父亲的仇人，然后组织游击队抗清，然后讲学，做那么多、那么多的事情，又活到高寿。还有那个更让我佩服的顾炎武，骑着马、骑着骡子，全中国的走，越是艰难的地方越是去，把书挂在牛角上，自己一个人在那慢慢走，写了那么多书，为中国文化留下了那么好的东西，这就是一个瘦精精的行者形象。中国文化的基本形象从来没有脑肥肠满、大腹便便，从来没有过。
非常重要的原因就是，我们中国文化一上来就需要简单。千言万语要抓住命脉，譬如《周易》里边说中华文化的命脉就是人文，观乎人文以化成天下。“观乎人文化成天下”指的是什么呢？就是对鬼神的传说，中国文化敬而远之，讲鬼讲神和中国文化本体无关。万物争奇，疏而蔽之，玩物伤志，对于非常奇怪的东西、非常珍贵的东西，远远地看一眼就避开了。对于高谈玄论，笑一笑，听而过之。
它和其他文明相比，中国文化不知道省了多少口舌，省了多少一卷一卷的高谈阔论，没有鬼神的传说，没有对珍奇的深入的破析，没有对高谈玄论的一厚本的发挥。一下子就走向了简易，上来就是如此。我们的典籍之首《周易》，这个“易”字，第一含义就是简易，第二含义就是变易。以简易的方式来研究变易和不易，研究的方式又不抽象，而是用卜卦的概率来呈现，这居然是中国文明的首领之作。
由此可见，简易是我们非常重要的一个文化特征。
transcriptEn:
Hello everyone, my name is Yu Qiuyu.
I talked about the issue of order last time. We must be strict with order. This is an idea that our ancestors had very early on. Confucius had been running around for such a long time, calling for the establishment of an order similar to that of the Zhou Dynasty. Its order was embodied in the form of etiquette. I mentioned last time that all civilizations are pursuing order, but only China regards the construction of order as the first priority. Order has many negative effects in our lives. Why do we seem to be unfree, unwilling, and uncomfortable, so we always have to overthrow the old order and establish a new order.
But for people like me, when I was young, I always thought about establishing a new order. I never thought about what would happen if there was no order. The world-wide inspection gave me a lot of inspiration. When I went out for inspection, the social situation in China was still not very good. It was still very poor and backward, and it was still dirty and messy. This situation existed everywhere. There are also many places where there is no order, but we really haven’t seen what it will be like if a place is completely out of order.
a whole set of order
When I visited a country, the buses in their capital never stopped. Old people, young people, men, and women would jump up and down like monkeys when they saw the buses coming. I was very, very surprised by this. Why didn't I stop? The cemetery is in the middle of the city. Many homeless people and even people who have escaped from prison live there. The police have no right to investigate because this is a cemetery. At least one-third of all buildings are uncapped and the steel bars are exposed. This is still the case even after ten years. If you ask them, they will say that this makes us feel like we are living in a new house. This is nonsense, but it is actually for tax avoidance.
This is called very disordered, but we have seen even more disordered scenes. In the country I just talked about, they heard that a few of us were going to invade Iraq. They even held a grand farewell party to bid farewell to us and the Chinese heroes. Why did they think we went to those places? I said you have already reached this level of chaos. How much chaos will it get inside? The old man smiled and said, go in and have a look. Later, when you read my book, you will know that the scene we saw was indeed terrifying.
But in many countries that seem to be actually very friendly, we also see unimaginable scenarios. For example, there are thousands of tourists and thousands of passengers hanging on the train, on the windows, and on the doors. A good passenger car is modified after buying it and converted into a three-story building. The top floor was rickety and filled with primary school students. There are endless car accidents every day, which is a serious disorder.
This kind of disorder can spread very quickly and be difficult to rectify. When I visited some historical countries in South and West Asia, I often saw such scenes. There is dust everywhere in those cities. Men ranging from thirteen or fourteen to seventy-something years old stand on the garbage pile. The garbage pile is so big that you can tell that it has not been cleaned for decades. The man standing on the garbage line was also covered in dust, with only the whites of his eyes and teeth white. Groups of people were standing there, what were they doing? Not doing much, just looking at each other. You look at me and I look at you, and you don’t talk much, just a few words occasionally.
After we arrived, they felt that something good had happened today and they all looked at us. I asked them what they were eating. They said that sometimes the government and the mayor would give them some food, cakes and so on for the election. They are all strong and strong. They are still standing upright on the garbage heap in their seventies. They are so young at thirteen or fourteen years old, so of course they are in very good health. The companion who went with me thought about a question. Wouldn't it be great if a mayor or a district chief asked these people to bend down and clean up the rubbish that has been accumulated for decades under their feet? This land would belong to them and let them cultivate it. I believe that we Chinese all have this idea, and I also have this idea. Wouldn't it be great to transport the garbage away, fill it somewhere, and then cultivate the land to grow the agricultural products needed by the local area?
However, the next question arises, if this land is to be cultivated, where will the agricultural tools come from? Where do the seeds come from? Where does irrigation come from? Where does the transportation come from? Nothing. Therefore, just to clear a small piece of land and plant crops, we are faced with a whole set of order. This order is a system engineering. Once any link falls off, the entire system collapses.
So, do you know that we are living a relatively normal life now? There is a lot of strict order hidden behind every normal life. As long as one turnbuckle is wrong, this order will no longer exist. Therefore, it takes many years of hard work to establish order before it can be sustained. So based on this, we must express some kind of gratitude to our ancestors. I look at the groups of foreign men standing on the garbage dump, from teenagers to men in their seventies, only the whites of their eyes and teeth are white. I can't help but thank our Chinese predecessors for their hard work and protection again and again.
big order and little order
But when it comes to establishing order, these people standing on the garbage dump are just like ordinary people in ancient China. They cannot establish strong desires. Why establish order? It will be so troublesome for you to establish order. How can we become the screws in the order process?
Under this situation, Confucius had a very good idea. His idea was that a large order must be persuaded by a small order, demonstrated by a small order, and piloted by a small order. The integrity and perfection of the small order will definitely bring about the completeness and perfection of the large order. Therefore, Confucius created a very good concept for establishing order. This concept is called "family-state isomorphism", which means that the family and the country are put into the same structural system for comparison.
The order of the family is set one by one by blood, seniority, age, rank, and marriage, so it is very clear. The etiquette and rules derived from this order are also well known. So what if these family orders are enlarged, moved outward, and diffused one by one, and become a social order? What if we use this to become a national order? It is to slowly expand from the natural family order to social order and national order. This idea made them very excited, so they proposed a process from home to country, called self-cultivation, harmonizing the family, governing the country and bringing peace to the world. Organizing the family and governing the country are connected. When the family is in order, the country is also governed. In other words, a project was launched that compared the private spatial order with the public spatial order. This project is what I call "home-state isomorphism."
This builds a logical bridge between social order and national order. The person who built this bridge probably only loved his family and relatives at first, but slowly it spread, from his own elders to the elders outside, from his own children to the children outside. When it spreads bit by bit, the family order becomes a model of social order. There is a passage in the ancient Chinese classic "The Book of Changes" in which family and country are mixed into a continuous concept. Let me read it:
There is heaven and earth, and then there are all things; there are all things, and then there are men and women; there are men and women, and then there are husband and wife; there are husband and wife, and then there are father and son; there are father and son, and then there are monarchs and ministers; there are monarchs and ministers, and then there are up and down; there are up and down, and then there is something wrong with etiquette.
It connects the order of heaven and earth, the order of family, the order of gender, the order of father and son, and the order of monarch and ministers. The advantage of this connection is that it puts the order of heaven and earth and the order of family first, and describes the order of kings and ministers as a derived order, which is different from what later kings imagined.
However, there are indeed many problems with this kind of project that is homogeneous for the country and the country. So what's the problem? That is, social justice cannot be confused with family internal rules, and political rationality cannot come from the judgment of parents. Those enlightenment thinkers in the late Ming and early Qing Dynasties, the people I call Huang Zongxi, Gu Yanwu, and Wang Fuzhi, have always said that the general public has no reason to forgive the emperor like they forgive their old father. The state must be careful not to slip into the quagmire of the family and the world. This is repeatedly proposed by the Enlightenment, and it is also a very important correction to the concept of "the isomorphism of the family and the state."
This was indeed the case in ancient China. The "country" in the "family-state isomorphism" mainly refers to the imperial court, which is different from the motherland we talk about now. They rarely considered the public space. When talking about the country in ancient times, the country mainly referred to the imperial court and rarely considered the public space. Therefore, they do not take into account the people standing on the garbage dump doing nothing. This problem was later solved very well in Europe. I will talk specifically about the issue of public space later. Europe has solved this problem better than we do. Although we live a long life, many embarrassing things often happen to our tourists when they travel to Europe or go to other places. Therefore, there is a very big rift in our "family-state isomorphism", that is, the general order of society and the small order of the family are different.
I used to often go to some houses in Shanghai and saw that many ordinary people in Shanghai were like this. The houses in their homes were really clean and beautiful. But just outside a door, all the rubbish is thrown there, all the rags are thrown there, ignoring each other. You should walk on tiptoe in public spaces. After knocking on the door, you will find a beautiful private space inside. Therefore, the isomorphism of family and state is actually just a symbol, and it is difficult to say that it completely solves the problem. The reason is very simple, because in classical society and feudal society, the concept of country was not specific, and it was not a public space as we understand it now. When the country is only understood as the imperial court, your "family-state isomorphism" only requires people to face the emperor like their own parents. If this is such a thinking, the problem of establishing public order will be very big.
In ancient China, Confucianism had a warm idea of ​​"the isomorphism of family and state", but Legalism was different. If it wanted to establish social order, it used very powerful means to protect the world. Of course, its methods are very effective. Although many rulers verbally used Confucian discourse, they actually used Legalist tactics. Later, although order was established and civilization continued, this order was branded with a certain bad court, and this brand also had a long life, so this is what we need to pay attention to when we want to correct various ills of Chinese civilization over the years. It does bring about the continuation of Chinese civilization and the longevity of Chinese culture, but it also brings about the longevity of another bad factor related to it, which is something that Chinese culture needs to continuously improve.
Simplify thinking
I have already talked about four secrets. The land is large and the people are large, we never go on expeditions, we pursue unity, and we are strict about order. These are all relatively big aspects, but these big aspects have not yet fully touched upon the ontology of our culture. What we are talking about is a macro-choice. Chinese culture has made the choice and positioning just mentioned in the macro-history and in the macro-social direction. Some are not choices, they are indeed our own existence. For example, the land is large and there are many people; not going on an expedition and seeking unity and order are our serious choices.
But when all this is implemented in the ontology of culture, what good specialties will emerge to make Chinese culture live longer? This is also the advantage of Chinese culture. I announced this ontological characteristic last time. I will talk about it again now. One is to simplify thinking, another is to downplay competition, another is to guard against extremes, and the last one is to implement imperial examinations. I will talk about these slowly and little by little.
Now let me talk about simplifying thinking first, because this will definitely cause some people to not understand. Because many of our scholars now like to describe ancient Chinese classics as very complex and difficult. Just like those CEO Chinese Studies classes I mentioned earlier, they drew thick curtains and taught for several months at a time, slowly and slowly, as if there were many extremely complicated secrets inside that needed to be kept in this dark room and not allowed to be overheard by everyone. They needed to be deciphered bit by bit. In fact, the main reason why Chinese culture can live long is simple from the very beginning.
Chinese culture has always maintained the image of a lean, lean, cheerful traveler. What is the image of a traveler? Do you still remember Huang Zongxi, whom I talked about earlier, who lived to a very long life? He stabbed the enemy who killed his father, organized guerrillas to fight against the Qing Dynasty, gave lectures, did so many things, and lived to a ripe old age. There is also Gu Yanwu, who I admire even more. He rode a horse or a mule all over China, going to the more difficult places. He hung his books on the horns of an ox and walked slowly by himself. He wrote so many books and left so many good things for Chinese culture. This is the image of a lean and lean traveler. The basic image of Chinese culture has never been fat-brained, full-bodied, pot-bellied, never has been.
The very important reason is that our Chinese culture needs to be simple from the beginning. There are thousands of words to grasp the lifeblood. For example, "The Book of Changes" says that the lifeblood of Chinese culture is humanities, and looking at humanities can transform the world. What does "seeing human culture transform the world" mean? Chinese culture keeps a respectful distance from the legends of ghosts and gods. Talking about ghosts and gods has nothing to do with the ontology of Chinese culture. All things strive for wonder, keep them in a sparse manner, and playing with things hurts your will. For very strange things and very precious things, you can avoid them by just looking at them from a distance. Just laugh at the high-spirited talk and ignore it.
Compared with other civilizations, Chinese culture saves countless words and volumes of high-minded talk. There are no legends of ghosts and gods, no in-depth analysis of rare things, and no thick volumes of high-level talks. All of a sudden, it's easy, and that's it from the beginning. The first of our classics, "Zhouyi", the word "Yi" has the first meaning of simplicity and the second meaning of change. Studying changes and difficulties in a simple way, and the research method is not abstract, but presented with the probability of divination. This is actually the pioneer work of Chinese civilization.
It can be seen that simplicity is a very important cultural feature of ours.

summary.gistZh: 「家国同构」解释了中国社会小秩序（家庭伦理）与大秩序（国家治理）的无缝衔接，使国家治理具备了深厚的伦理情感根基。
summary.gistEn: 'Isomorphism of Family and State' explains the seamless alignment between micro-order (family ethics) and macro-order (state governance), providing statecraft with deep ethical and emotional roots.

highlights.zh: 大秩序与小秩序：家庭是国家的微缩版，国家是家庭的放大版，孝亲与忠国在逻辑上高度统一。
highlights.en: Macro & Micro Orders: The family is a microcosm of the state, and the state is an expanded family; filial piety and patriotism share logical unity.

highlights.zh: 伦理作为治理工具：不同于依赖法律强制的治理，中国传统社会通过家庭伦理实现低成本的自主治安与社会凝聚。
highlights.en: Ethics as Governance: Unlike governance relying purely on legal coercion, traditional China achieved low-cost self-governance via family ethics.

highlights.zh: 家国情怀的双刃剑：赋予文明强大的凝聚力与抗风险能力，但也需要现代公民意识的调和。
highlights.en: Double-Edged Sword: It bestows immense social cohesion and resilience, yet requires balancing with modern civic awareness.

highlights.zh: 文明长寿的奥秘：家国同构让社会基本单元（家庭）在战乱中能迅速重建文明秩序。
highlights.en: Secret of Longevity: This structure allowed the basic social unit (family) to rapidly rebuild civil order even after disastrous wars.

title: 统一文字：难以消灭的文化基因
folderName: 06_统一文字：难以消灭的文化基因
