transcriptZh:
大家好，我是余秋雨。
上次我从德国社会学家马克斯·韦伯的论述里边，分析了中国文化强调统一的生态原因。他从两条大河流进十几个省的角度谈起，认为这十几个省如果没有统一的政府的领导，他们可以随意坑害上游和下游的任何其他省。他以此作为中国必须大一统的理由，只要这两条大河还在流，只要这两条大河还是中国的生态基础，中国文化的统一思维就不会断绝，这说得很好。
那么今天我要重复一下曾经讲起过的，秦始皇他们做的一件非常重要的事情，就是他们在很早的时候，就用统一文字的重要实验来告诉大家，统一是能够做到的，这是一件非常了不起的事情。
追求统一
大家想想看，中国地方那么大，方言那么多，人口那么密，流转那么快，文字居然统一了，这简直是难以想象的事情。世界上很难有国家在比较早的时候就做到这一点，因为当时各种统治的手段还不齐备，居然都做到了。大家知道这对中国文化的延续有什么价值吗？“统一”猛一听，好像是对我们中国这个国家很重要，其实严格讲起来，是对文化非常重要，对中国文化非常重要。
我说一个最通俗的例子，如果我们的文字不统一，那么我们设想一下，如果文字不统一的话，一定会产生文化的自我消灭。怎么会这么说呢？我举个例子，如果哪一年山西和山东打仗，山西把山东打败了，打败以后要做一件事，让山东人停止用山东的文字，全部改用山西的文字，任何胜利者都会做这件事。
但是，这个事情很容易成功，为什么呢？因为从世界历史看，要改变一个地方的文字很方便。只要把识字的人学校改变，只要把那个识字的人赶走，如果不赶走的话，让那个识字的人老死以后，新一代再也不认识这些字了，这些字就变成天书了，我们在埃及、在其他地方都能看到这种情景。
但是，山东用了山西的文字，问题是山西难道不会被别的省份打败吗？好，别的身份来了，河南把山西打败了，结果剩下了河南的文字。大家知道吗？这样结果是，当山东的文字消失以后，山东的历史也消失了。当山西的文字消失以后，山西的历史也消失了，当河南的文字消失以后，河南的历史也消失了。如果文字不统一的话，那么每一种文字都想成为凌驾于别人的文字，别人的文字在消灭的时候，就把中华文化的历史一块一块地消灭了。
统一文字就成了通码，大家共用的通码。即使这个省把那个省打败了，它也无法消灭这个省的文字，它可以收缴它的某一种史籍是可能的，但文字不消灭的话，文化的基因就没有消灭，一切记忆就没有消灭，很多潜藏的史料都可以复活。所以，在中国这么一个内战还是不少的一个国家里，文字统一对于文化的流传起的作用太大了。
我们现在有一个成语，我们叫同文同宗。大家注意同文放在同宗前面，这一点非常重要，正是这种同样的文字、统一的文字，保证了我们心理文化的统一，否则的话，同宗也没用。尽管你也是黑头发、黑眼珠、黄皮肤，但是当文化不同的时候，几代文化不同的时候，其实血缘真的不能转化成文化。中华文化不灭的一个非常重要的原因，就是一种统一的文字使它成了很难灭的文化基座。这个文化就一直延续下去了。
文字是这样，其他方面也同样是这样。我曾经讲过很多这样的话，在中国历史上，大一统对中国文化带来了毛病很多，但是唯独对于文字的统一，对于文化的统一，我一直给予非常正面的评价，因为这是一种伟大的留存，这是一种非常正面的、民族的、精华的延续，所以我们没有理由在这方面有任何错误的想法。
这个一统或者说这个统一，首先是我们非常追求统一的思维，毫无疑问地延续着我们的中华文化。在这我必须讲这么一段话，就是在中国几千年历史上，出现了很多追求统一的人，也出现了很多追求分裂的人。
我们必须要明白，无论是追求统一的人，还是追求分裂的人，两方面都有很多极为聪明，极为能干的政治家和军事家。他们就个人的智能上都非常优秀，理由也非常充分。但是硬要把他们比一比的话，我们就会发现主张统一的人往往更有远见，因此也更得人心。他们因为大气而握着大脉，掌控的大局，他们是统、裂之间的大者。
我再讲一遍，统一和分裂之间，有大者和小者，有大道和小智。我们追求的是大者和大道，而追求统一在我看来是大道和大智。正是由于这些人，中国一次次由分裂走向统一，也正是由于他们，多数中国人在文化基座上养成了自己作为大国国民的心理适应。正是这种心理适应，指引着历史的步履，使中国始终没有在分裂的泥潭当中沉没。
保持秩序
大家能够明白吗？追求统一，是中国文化延续的第三个原因。下面讲第四个原因。第四个原因顺着我们的逻辑来讲，统一有可能产生一个弊病，统一是统一了，但是很散，我们叫一盘散沙，一盘散沙就谈不上整体生命力了。世界上也有这样的国家，被淡淡地、散散地统治着，但是统治没有效，国家也没有什么进步，生产也永远是滞后，文明也永远停留在原始的基础上，这样的国家也看到过不少，“统”不见得是力量的源泉。
所以在这个问题上，就产生了要建立一种秩序的强烈的欲望，而这个欲望是中国古人非常机智的文化选择。在非常早的时候，古人觉得这个国家最需要的是秩序。所以在非常遥远的古代，当巴比伦人在研究天文学和数学的时候，当埃及人在墓道里刻画一连串的生和死的图景的时候，当印度人在山间洞窟里一批批苦修的时候，中国人在干什么呢？中国人却花费极大的精力在排练着维系秩序的礼仪，礼仪的目的是为了把秩序保持下来。
孔子他奔波大半辈子，主要目的是为了恢复周礼，重建西周时候的社会秩序。其实比起西周的社会秩序，他还有更多的设想，这是他的一个非常重要的想法。所以前不久有个地方恢复古迹，是我们一个重要的文明故地，有一条道路叫什么大道，我建议改成周礼大道，因为这是孔子的梦想，也是我们中华文化的一个非常重要的一个特征。就是追求从朝廷到家庭，从集市到街情，都秩序井然、上下归附。
秩序哪一个文明不向往呢？但是在所有文明的主宰者里边，只有中国人把秩序当作治理的第一要务。因此其他文明，好多都因为失序而破败，只有中国让秩序成为社会的经纬。
在中国古代，秩序是由统治者来设计的，而且严格管理，它变成了一种礼仪分级，在社会上形成了半强制性的整体结构。有了秩序，不管是社会还是人，都有了前后左右、上下尊卑，这既保持了统治的充分有效，又避免了无序所带来的杂乱互伤。
我所说的这种秩序，当然也会产生很多负面效应。譬如有一种时时需要顾盼周际的不自由，还有我们时时需要无奈地服从权势的不情愿，我们甚至于还有一种必须蜷曲于一大堆规则中的不舒畅。因此，长期生活在有序社会中的人士，常常要区分什么是老秩序，什么是新秩序，什么是正秩序，什么是负秩序，并且努力的要去弊立正，除旧布新。
但是无序会怎么样呢？这个我要给我同学们讲一讲了。我们这一代人，我们一直生活在要破除旧秩序、建立新秩序的激动当中，我们脑子当中天天想着新秩序如何建立，如何立新破旧，如何除旧布新，我们年轻的时候想的全是这个。
作为中国的智者们，从来没有一个人想过一件事，无序将是什么样的？没想过。至少我是这样，我脑子当中想的是新秩序、旧秩序，没想过无秩序。所以我下堂课要给大家讲一讲，无秩序将会给文明带来多大的损害。
谢谢。
transcriptEn:
Hello everyone, my name is Yu Qiuyu.
Last time, I analyzed the ecological reasons why Chinese culture emphasizes unity based on the discussion of German sociologist Max Weber. He started from the perspective of two major rivers flowing into more than a dozen provinces. He believed that if these dozen provinces did not have the leadership of a unified government, they could harm any other provinces upstream and downstream at will. He used this as the reason why China must be unified. As long as these two rivers are still flowing and as long as these two rivers are China's ecological foundation, the unified thinking of Chinese culture will not be cut off. This is very good.
So today I want to repeat what I have said before. One of the very important things Qin Shihuang and others did was that they used the important experiment of unifying the script very early to tell everyone that unification can be achieved. This is a very remarkable thing.
pursue unity
Think about it, everyone, China is so big, has so many dialects, the population is so dense, and the circulation is so fast. It is simply unimaginable that the writing system is unified. It is difficult for any country in the world to achieve this at an early stage, because the various means of governance were not yet available at that time, but they actually achieved it. Do you know what value this has for the continuation of Chinese culture? At first glance, "unification" sounds like it is very important to our country, China. In fact, strictly speaking, it is very important to culture and Chinese culture.
Let me give you the most popular example. If our writing is not unified, then let’s imagine that if our writing is not unified, there will definitely be self-annihilation of culture. How could you say that? Let me give you an example. If one year Shanxi and Shandong go to war and Shanxi defeats Shandong, they will do one thing after the defeat. Let the Shandong people stop using Shandong characters and switch to Shanxi characters. Any winner will do this.
However, this thing is easy to succeed. Why? Because from the perspective of world history, it is very convenient to change the writing of a place. As long as the school of the literate person is changed, as long as the literate person is driven away, if the literate person is not driven away, after the literate person dies of old age, the new generation will no longer know these words, and these words will become a sacred book. We can see this situation in Egypt and other places.
However, Shandong uses Shanxi's characters. The question is, won't Shanxi be defeated by other provinces? Well, another identity came, Henan defeated Shanxi, and the words of Henan were left. Does anyone know? The result is that when the characters of Shandong disappear, the history of Shandong also disappears. When the characters of Shanxi disappear, the history of Shanxi also disappears. When the characters of Henan disappear, the history of Henan also disappears. If the writing is not unified, then each writing will want to be superior to others. When other people's writing is eliminated, the history of Chinese culture will be wiped out piece by piece.
The unified text becomes a common code, a common code shared by everyone. Even if this province defeats that province, it cannot eliminate its writing. It is possible that it can confiscate certain historical records. But if the writing is not eliminated, the cultural genes will not be eliminated, all memories will not be eliminated, and many hidden historical materials can be resurrected. Therefore, in a country like China where there are still many civil wars, the unification of writing plays a great role in the spread of culture.
We now have an idiom called Tongwen Tongzong. It is very important to note that the same text is placed before the same sect. It is this same text and unified text that ensures the unity of our psychology and culture. Otherwise, the same sect is useless. Even though you also have black hair, black eyes, and yellow skin, when the cultures are different, or when the cultures of several generations are different, blood relations really cannot be transformed into culture. A very important reason why Chinese culture is immortal is that a unified script makes it a cultural base that is difficult to destroy. This culture has continued.
This is true for words, and it is also true for other aspects. I have said many things like this. In Chinese history, unification has brought many problems to Chinese culture, but I have always given a very positive evaluation to the unification of words and culture, because this is a great preservation, a very positive, national, and essence continuation, so we have no reason to have any wrong ideas in this regard.
This unification or this unification, first of all, is our pursuit of unified thinking, which undoubtedly continues our Chinese culture. I must say something like this: In China's thousands of years of history, there have been many people who pursued unification, and many people who have pursued division.
We must understand that whether we are those who pursue unity or those who pursue division, there are many extremely smart and capable politicians and military strategists on both sides. They are all very good in terms of personal intelligence, and the reasons are very good. But if we compare them, we will find that those who advocate unification tend to be more far-sighted and therefore more popular. Because of their atmosphere, they hold the main line and control the overall situation. They are the big ones between unification and division.
Let me say it again, between unity and division, there are big ones and small ones, great ways and small wisdoms. What we pursue is greatness and great wisdom, and the pursuit of unity, in my opinion, is great truth and great wisdom. It is precisely because of these people that China has moved from division to unity time and time again, and it is precisely because of them that most Chinese people have developed their psychological adaptation as citizens of a great country on the basis of culture. It is this kind of psychological adaptation that guides the steps of history and keeps China from sinking in the quagmire of division.
keep order
Can everyone understand? The pursuit of unity is the third reason for the continuation of Chinese culture. Let’s talk about the fourth reason. The fourth reason is that following our logic, unification may cause a drawback. Unification is unified, but it is very scattered. We call it a loose sand. A loose sand cannot be said to have overall vitality. There are countries like this in the world that are ruled lightly and scatteredly, but the rule is ineffective, the country makes little progress, production always lags behind, and civilization always stays on the primitive basis. We have seen many such countries, and "unification" is not necessarily the source of strength.
Therefore, on this issue, there is a strong desire to establish an order, and this desire is a very clever cultural choice of the ancient Chinese. In very early times, the ancients felt that what this country needed most was order. So in very distant ancient times, when the Babylonians were studying astronomy and mathematics, when the Egyptians were carving a series of scenes of life and death in tomb passages, and when the Indians were doing ascetic practices in batches in mountain caves, what were the Chinese doing? The Chinese people spend a lot of energy rehearsing the etiquette to maintain order. The purpose of etiquette is to maintain order.
Confucius traveled for most of his life, and his main purpose was to restore Zhou rituals and rebuild the social order of the Western Zhou Dynasty. In fact, he had more ideas than the social order of the Western Zhou Dynasty. This was a very important idea of ​​his. So not long ago, there was a place where historical sites were restored, which is an important place of civilization for us. There is a road called the Avenue. I suggest changing it to Zhouli Avenue, because this is the dream of Confucius and it is also a very important feature of our Chinese culture. It is the pursuit of everything from the court to the family, from the market to the street, everything is in order and everyone is in compliance.
Which civilization doesn’t yearn for order? But among all the masters of civilization, only the Chinese regard order as the first priority of governance. Therefore, many other civilizations have collapsed due to disorder. Only China has made order the latitude and longitude of society.
In ancient China, order was designed by rulers and strictly managed. It became a ritual hierarchy and formed a semi-mandatory overall structure in society. With order, both society and people have front, back, left, right, superior and inferior, which not only maintains the full effectiveness of rule, but also avoids the chaos and mutual harm caused by disorder.
The order I am talking about will of course also produce many negative effects. For example, there is a kind of unfreedom that requires us to always look around, and there is also a reluctance that we always need to helplessly obey the authority. We even have an uncomfortable feeling of having to curl up in a lot of rules. Therefore, people who have lived in an orderly society for a long time often have to distinguish what is the old order, what is the new order, what is the positive order, and what is the negative order, and work hard to eliminate the old and establish the new.
But what happens to disorder? I want to tell my classmates about this. Our generation has been living in the excitement of destroying the old order and establishing a new one. We think about how to establish a new order every day, how to establish the new and the old, and how to remove the old and replace the old. When we were young, this was all we thought about.
As Chinese wise men, no one has ever thought about one thing, what will disorder be like? Never thought about it. At least that's the case for me. What I think about in my mind is the new order and the old order, and I don't think about disorder. So I will tell you in the next class how much damage disorder will bring to civilization.
Thanks.

summary.gistZh: 秦始皇统一文字是中国文明史上最伟大的战略决策，汉字超越了方言隔阂与时代变迁，成为凝聚数亿人的不可消灭的文化基因。
summary.gistEn: The standardization of written Chinese by Qin Shi Huang was the single greatest strategic decision in Chinese history—written Chinese transcended dialect barriers and time, becoming an indestructible cultural gene.

highlights.zh: 文字超越方言：即便各地口音相隔万里无法听懂，相同的方块字让政令、思想与文化毫无障碍地交流。
highlights.en: Transcending Dialects: Even when spoken dialects are mutually incomprehensible across regions, identical written characters enable seamless communication.

highlights.zh: 跨越时空的阅读：现代中国人能直接阅读两千年前的先秦古籍，这在拼音文字文明中是难以想象的。
highlights.en: Reading Across Millennia: Modern Chinese can directly read classical texts from 2,000 years ago, a phenomenon nearly impossible in alphabetic civilizations.

highlights.zh: 大一统的文化基石：统一文字锁定了中华文明的共同心理认同，使得中国即便分崩离析也必然重新走向统一。
highlights.en: Bedrock of Unity: Standardized writing anchored a shared psychological identity, ensuring China's eventual reunification even after collapses.

highlights.zh: 汉字的审美与艺术：汉字不仅是信息载体，更是书法艺术与审美哲学的载体。
highlights.en: Aesthetics of Chinese Characters: Chinese characters serve not just as informational tools, but as vessels for calligraphy and aesthetic philosophy.

title: 凉州风范：超越血缘的文化基因
folderName: 07_凉州风范：超越血缘的文化基因
audioPath: 07_凉州风范：超越血缘的文化基因/audio.m4a
quoteCardPath: 07_凉州风范：超越血缘的文化基因/quote_card.jpg
transcriptZh:
昨天讲到苻坚要用一场长途跋涉的战争，去争抢一个文化人、一个佛教哲学家，下的决心很大，他派出吕光将军作为这场抢人远征的司令。终于在公元382年，吕光赢得了战争，抢到了鸠摩罗什。抢到了就要送回长安，但路确实太远了，走了一半才到凉州，就是现在的甘肃武威。
到了凉州，吕光听到了一个惊人的消息，派他出来抢人的国君苻坚已经下台了。苻坚先是惨败于著名的淝水之战，然后又被部落里的人杀掉了。既然这样，我们为什么还要回长安呢？干脆就在凉州住下吧，反正有军队，一切都能安顿下来。他，吕光就做起了凉州的统治者。
那么被他抢来的鸠摩罗什该怎么处置呢？吕光对他的学问并不太懂，但他知道这是人人争抢的宝贝，必须严加看守。就这样，鸠摩罗什在凉州，在严密的看守下，居然住了整整十七年。
那我就要介绍几句这位鸠摩罗什了。鸠是斑鸠的“鸠”，摩是摩天大楼的“摩”，罗是梭罗的“罗”，什是北京什刹海的那个“什”，鸠摩罗什。他的父亲是印度人，母亲前面说了是龟兹国王的妹妹。他在龟兹乃至整个西域，都是最高等级的佛学家。这么一位大学者滞留凉州十七年，他能做什么呢？这个我们还需要考证，但是从种种资料看，他除了继续精研佛理外，还在汉语学习上下了极大的功夫。
正好，吕光派到他身边看守的那些士兵，来自于中国很多地方。鸠摩罗什就顺便学了汉语里边的很多方言，十七年已经使他成了一位精通汉文的语言学家，这为他后来在长安主持翻译工作起到了极大的作用。他在中国文化史上是一位与唐代的玄奘齐名的大翻译家，连玄奘的很多翻译还要运用他的经典译法，例如我们都知道《心经》里边的名句，“色即是空，空即是色”，最早就是鸠摩罗什的译法，译的准确而凝炼，很难更改。
凉州风范
说到他到长安主持翻译工作，那又是另一场文化争抢大战了。原来新的后秦君主姚兴，突然想到前辈有一个稀世的宝贝遗落在凉州了，就下决心要抢回来。凉州怎么肯放呢？因此，姚兴居然派出10万雄师讨伐凉州。结果，公元401年，鸠摩罗什终于被姚兴抢到了，来到了长安。
同样是由长安出发的争抢，第一次抢，鸠摩罗什还很年轻，但这条争抢的道路怎么这样长呢？当他真的到长安的时候已经58岁。你看，为了争抢一位文化人、一位哲学家、一位翻译家，居然一次次都派出雄兵争抢，而且争抢的路途又非常遥远。这样的中国虽然有点荒唐，却让我感到无比骄傲，这样的中国一定孕育着一个伟大的时代。
好，那我们再回头看看被抢走了鸠摩罗什的凉州。鸠摩罗什被争抢者暗藏在凉州，终于被发现以后又抢走了。几十年的马蹄，动不动就几万、几十万，一会夹着一个文化大使来了，一会又夹着一个文化大师走了。对这一点，凉州一点也不悲哀。因为文化不像财富权势那样，一说抢走就被抢走了，文化有根、有气、有脉，只要来过就播下了种子。抢走了一位文化大师，却抢不走这里已经形成的文化氛围。凉州，不见了鸠摩罗什的凉州，依然是文化中心。
因此在鸠摩罗什被抢走的38年之后，又有浩浩荡荡的军队来抢文化了，那就是我前面讲的北魏王朝的军队。他们胃口很大，一口气抢走了3万人，这下凉州应该空了吧？也没有。就在3万人被抢走之后的80年，我的家乡浙江上虞出生的僧人慧校编的《高僧传》14卷，里边所收的名单，凉州高僧还占据了一半。当然，“被抢走的凉州”在各地更加蔚成风气。
首先是大同的云冈石窟，尤其是处在中心地位的昙曜五窟，早已成为世界级的文化景观。接着是洛阳的龙门石窟，最终落脚于长安，可以说几乎整个黄河流域都被凉州渗透了。考古学家苏白先生,曾把这种现象说成是“凉州模式”。我在北大讲课的时候，把它改成了“凉州风范”，因为模式有点局限，其实变化很大。凉州风范因为在文化上功劳巨大，竟然获得了不可思议的报偿，那就是出现了一个归集性的世界级的盛典，这是所有的地域文化当中绝无仅有的。
一次古代的世界博览会
我指的是，我在讲述上述这些故事的一百多年之后，隋炀帝在凉州举办了一次隆重的古代世界博览会。原来隋炀帝在公元七世纪初期即位以后，便接受裴炬关于进一步拓展西域商路的建议。他让河西走廊和凉州又一次鲜明地进入了朝野视野。
山西人裴炬，火炬的“炬”，他目光巨大，在我看来是当时少有的宏观经济学家。他以互市的观念来反对各种贸易保护主义，而且编制了《西域图记》，标明丝绸之路的三条行进路线，因此是重新疏通国际通道的关键人物。
在裴炬的鼓动下，隋炀帝居然在公元609年，到河西走廊与武威相邻的张掖举办了一次隆重的国际贸易盟会，有西域27个国家参加，请记住多达27个国家。
隋炀帝下令武威、张掖两地的侍女必须盛装出席，除了大量的商品之外，凉州的乐舞、西域的各种艺术以及中原艺术家都集中在那里，参与的人数摆出了延绵数十里的阵仗，西域各国的使臣商贾在那里，再度为中国文化的宏伟气魄所震撼。这是一次真正意义上的古代的世界博览会。初看是以贸易为重，其实是中原王朝与西域各国全方位交流的重新启动，因此这又是以最鲜明、最隆重的方式展现了中国文化的世界身份。
隋炀帝这个人在中国历史上，是唯一亲临河西走廊的中原君主，他亲自重新疏通了丝绸之路的壮举，又让我联想到他开凿大运河。一条横向的走廊，一条竖向的运河，这实在是中华文明的两大命脉。他在位才14年，竟然准确地把握了这两大命脉，实在不容易。
不少史书对他颇有贬义，因为他实在过于好大喜功、奢靡无度，但我对他的大思路一直颇为肯定。隋炀帝一死，唐朝就建立了。唐朝的话题很多，但是显然一直保留着隆重的凉州风范。在这里我不妨读两首大家都熟悉的《凉州词》，说明凉州在唐诗当中的地位和魅力。一首是王之涣的：
黄河远上白云间，一片孤城万仞山。羌笛何须怨杨柳，春风不度玉门关。
另一首大家也知道，也叫《凉州词》，是王翰的：
葡萄美酒夜光杯，欲饮琵琶马上催。醉卧沙场君莫笑，古来征战几人回。
这种豪放乐观的壮士情怀正是唐文化的主调，在那么多的唐代诗人心中，怎么也放不下这个凉州。我在北京大学讲授中国文化史课程的时候，有位女学生希望我多讲一讲凉州文化，因为她对这个“凉”字很有好感。我听她一问就讲了一大篇，使得学生们都非常吃惊，因为这是他们在寻常的课程当中听不到的，其中有几个学生读到过我的记忆文学《吾家小史》，就开玩笑地问，这是不是与我作为一个凉州后裔的身份有关？这个话题很有趣，我要顺便说几句。
超越血缘的文化基因
三年前，江苏有一个地方请我写“余阙庙”三个字，因为他们修建的这座庙宇，格式非常新颖，有好多地方是透明的，我喜欢，于是就提笔题写了。这个“阙”就是“不知天上宫阙，今夕是何年”中的“阙”字。余阙是公元14世纪元朝的守将，守卫着安庆城。1358年安庆城被陈友谅所破，他当即自杀，妻子和子女全部都投井而死。这不仅受到敌人陈友谅的尊重，也被朱元璋表彰。他的传记还是宋濂写的，宋濂一动笔就立即写到，他是凉州人，党项族。
记得很多年前，宁夏有位西夏史专家告诉我，党项人在建立西夏王朝，最后被成吉思汗所灭，其中部分人就加入了成吉思汗的蒙古人的部队。后来蒙古人失败的时候，很多人由铁木氏改姓余，其中有不少人前往浙江一带。余阙也是以党项人的身份成了元蒙的将军，但他的姓氏好像原来就有，不是临时改过来的。
这些年我多次收到大量的论文和名册，作者多姓余，都来自于铁木氏改过来的，都自称是这样。看起来，改姓这件事不仅确实存在，而且规模不小。由此来推断，我极可能是祖籍武威的党项人的后裔。
鲜卑由西夏而入蒙，蒙败以后，改姓而入江浙。但是我曾经开玩笑地讲过，在我们余姓当中，只要是亲近大漠、无畏长途、精力旺盛、不屈不挠的人物，多半具有在西北疆场上摸爬滚打的血缘，至少我自己就是这样的特质。现在DNA的基因测试技术突飞猛进，先祖后裔的血缘问题迟早会有更清晰的答案。
但是作为一个文化人，我更看重一种超越血缘的文化基因，凉州显然与我有一种神秘的精神连接。现在已经知道，连基因也可以改造，那么不管怎么说，我的基因曾经被凉州文化改造过。
让我感到愉快的是，现在武威市很多民众都把我当做他们的家乡人。我去的时候，他们特意安排了我向余阙的塑像献花的仪式，还邀请我为凉州文化研究院的院名题词，甚至在研究院里边还专设了我的书房。我在参观了种种古迹之后，非常感谢他们把鸠摩罗什寺修得很好，只不过对鸠摩罗什的雕像有一点点异议，就是雕得太像一个普通的汉族的和尚了。
请想想看，他父亲是印度人，他母亲是龟兹国王的妹妹，他的形貌会引起多少雕塑家的兴趣啊。太汉族了的话，就掩盖了他作为世界级的国际文化和中国文化深度沟通者的身份。相比之下，吴为山先生在山西的云冈石窟雕塑的昙曜的立像，就好的多了。
另外我希望武威能够成为一个现代旅行者的热门选择点。理由就是那么多我刚刚讲的激动人心的增强文化的古代故事，它在古代就是一个大通道当中的大驿站，那么现代的交通也应该更通畅。
transcriptEn:
Yesterday we talked about Fu Jian's determination to fight for a cultural man and a Buddhist philosopher in a long-distance war. He sent General Lu Guang as the commander of this expedition to snatch people. Finally in 382 AD, Lu Guang won the war and captured Kumarajiva. After grabbing it, I had to send it back to Chang'an, but the journey was indeed too far. I walked halfway before reaching Liangzhou, which is now Wuwei, Gansu.
When he arrived in Liangzhou, Lu Guang heard the shocking news that the monarch Fu Jian who sent him out to rob people had resigned. Fu Jian was first defeated in the famous Battle of Feishui, and then was killed by the tribesmen. In this case, why should we go back to Chang'an? Just stay in Liangzhou. Anyway, with the army, everything can be settled. He, Lu Guang, became the ruler of Liangzhou.
So what should he do with Kumarajiva who was snatched away by him? Lu Guang didn't know much about his knowledge, but he knew that this was a treasure that everyone was fighting for and must be carefully guarded. In this way, Kumarajiva lived in Liangzhou for seventeen years under strict guard.
Then I will introduce a few words about Kumarajiva. Jiu is the "jiu" of Turtle Dove, Mo is the "Mo" of skyscraper, Luo is the "Luo" of Thoreau, Shi is the "Shi" of Shichahai in Beijing, Kumarajiva. His father is Indian, and his mother, as mentioned earlier, is the sister of King Kucha. He is the highest-ranking Buddhist scholar in Qiuci and even in the entire Western Region. Such a great scholar has stayed in Liangzhou for seventeen years. What can he do? We still need to verify this, but judging from various information, in addition to continuing to study Buddhism intensively, he also made great efforts in learning Chinese.
Coincidentally, the soldiers Lu Guang sent to guard him came from many places in China. Kumarajiva learned many dialects of Chinese by the way. Seventeen years have made him a linguist proficient in Chinese, which played a great role in his later management of translation work in Chang'an. He is a great translator as famous as Xuanzang in the Tang Dynasty in the history of Chinese culture. Many of Xuanzang's translations still use his classic translation method. For example, we all know the famous sentence in the Heart Sutra, "Form is emptiness, emptiness is form." The earliest translation was Kumarajiva's. The translation is accurate and concise, and it is difficult to change.
Liangzhou style
Speaking of him going to Chang'an to take charge of the translation work, it was another cultural war. It turned out that Yao Xing, the new monarch of the Later Qin Dynasty, suddenly thought that his predecessor had a rare treasure left in Liangzhou, so he made up his mind to snatch it back. How could Liangzhou be willing to let it go? Therefore, Yao Xing actually sent 100,000 troops to attack Liangzhou. As a result, in 401 AD, Kumarajiva was finally snatched by Yao Xing and came to Chang'an.
It was also a fight starting from Chang'an. Kumarajiva was still very young for the first time, but why was the road to this fight so long? When he really arrived in Chang'an, he was already 58 years old. You see, in order to compete for a cultural person, a philosopher, and a translator, huge troops are sent out time and time again to compete, and the distance to compete is very long. Although this kind of China is a bit absurd, it makes me feel extremely proud. This kind of China must be pregnant with a great era.
Okay, let's look back at Liangzhou where Kumarajiva was robbed. Kumarajiva was hidden in Liangzhou by the robbers, but was finally discovered and snatched away. The horseshoes of decades ago can easily cost tens or hundreds of thousands. One moment, a cultural ambassador came, and the next moment, a cultural master left. Liangzhou is not sad at all about this. Because culture is not like wealth and power, which is snatched away as soon as it is said to be snatched away. Culture has roots, vitality, and veins, and the seeds are sown as long as it comes. A cultural master has been taken away, but the cultural atmosphere that has been formed here cannot be taken away. Liangzhou, without Kumarajiva, is still a cultural center.
Therefore, 38 years after Kumarajiva was robbed, another mighty army came to rob the culture. That was the army of the Northern Wei Dynasty that I mentioned earlier. They had a huge appetite and robbed 30,000 people in one go. Liangzhou should be empty now, right? Neither. Just 80 years after 30,000 people were robbed, the 14-volume "Biography of Eminent Monks" edited by Hui Xiao, a monk born in Shangyu, Zhejiang, my hometown, contained half of the lists of eminent monks from Liangzhou. Of course, "Liangzhou was stolen" has become more popular in various places.
The first is the Yungang Grottoes in Datong, especially the Tanyao Five Grottoes in the center, which have long become a world-class cultural landscape. Then came the Longmen Grottoes in Luoyang, and finally settled in Chang'an. It can be said that almost the entire Yellow River Basin was penetrated by Liangzhou. Archaeologist Mr. Su Bai once described this phenomenon as the "Liangzhou model". When I was lecturing at Peking University, I changed it to "Liangzhou Style" because the model was a bit limited, but it actually changed a lot. Because of its huge contribution to culture, Liangzhou style has received an incredible reward, which is the emergence of a collective world-class ceremony, which is unique among all regional cultures.
an ancient world fair
What I mean is that more than a hundred years after I told the above stories, Emperor Yang of the Sui Dynasty held a grand ancient world exposition in Liangzhou. It turns out that after Emperor Sui Yang came to the throne in the early seventh century AD, he accepted Pei Ju's suggestion to further expand trade routes in the Western Regions. He made the Hexi Corridor and Liangzhou clearly come into the view of the government and the public.
Pei Ju, a native of Shanxi, is the "torch" of the torch. He has great vision. In my opinion, he was a rare macroeconomist at that time. He opposed all kinds of trade protectionism with the concept of mutual trade, and compiled the "Illustration of the Western Regions" to mark the three routes of the Silk Road. Therefore, he was a key figure in re-opening international channels.
Under Pei Ju's instigation, Emperor Yang of the Sui Dynasty actually went to Zhangye, adjacent to Wuwei in the Hexi Corridor, to hold a grand international trade alliance in 609 AD. 27 countries from the Western Regions participated. Please remember that there were as many as 27 countries.
Emperor Yang of the Sui Dynasty ordered that the maids from Wuwei and Zhangye must dress up to attend. In addition to a large number of commodities, music and dance from Liangzhou, various arts from the Western Regions, and artists from the Central Plains were gathered there. The number of participants formed a battle array that stretched for dozens of miles. Envoys and merchants from various countries in the Western Regions were there, and they were once again shocked by the magnificence of Chinese culture. This is a truly ancient world's fair. At first glance, it seems to focus on trade, but in fact it is the restart of all-round exchanges between the Central Plains Dynasty and the countries in the Western Regions. Therefore, this shows the world identity of Chinese culture in the most distinctive and solemn way.
In Chinese history, Emperor Yang of the Sui Dynasty was the only monarch from the Central Plains who visited the Hexi Corridor in person. His feat of re-opening the Silk Road personally reminded me of him digging the Grand Canal. A horizontal corridor and a vertical canal are really the two lifebloods of Chinese civilization. He has only been in office for 14 years, but it is not easy to accurately grasp these two lifelines.
Many history books have a derogatory connotation of him because he was too eager for success and extravagant, but I have always been quite positive about his big ideas. As soon as Emperor Yang of Sui Dynasty died, the Tang Dynasty was established. There are many topics about the Tang Dynasty, but the grand Liangzhou style has obviously been retained. Here I might as well read two "Liangzhou Ci" that everyone is familiar with to illustrate the status and charm of Liangzhou in Tang poetry. One is by Wang Zhihuan:
Far up the Yellow River among the white clouds, there is an isolated city called Wanren Mountain. Why should the Qiang flute blame the willows? The spring breeze does not pass through Yumen Pass.
Everyone knows another song, also called "Liangzhou Ci", written by Wang Han:
The luminous cup of grape wine reminds you immediately if you want to drink Pipa. Don't laugh when you are lying drunk on the battlefield. How many people have fought in ancient times.
This bold and optimistic warrior sentiment is the main theme of Tang culture. In the hearts of so many Tang Dynasty poets, they could not let go of Liangzhou. When I was teaching a course on the history of Chinese culture at Peking University, a female student asked me to talk more about Liangzhou culture because she had a good impression of the word "liang". When I heard her ask, she told a long story, which surprised the students because they couldn't hear it in ordinary courses. Several students had read my memory literature "A Brief History of My Family" and asked jokingly, did this have something to do with my identity as a descendant of Liangzhou? This topic is interesting, I'd like to say a few words in passing.
Cultural genes that transcend blood ties
Three years ago, a place in Jiangsu asked me to write the words "Yuque Temple" because the temple they built had a very novel format and many parts were transparent. I liked it, so I wrote the inscription. This "que" is the word "que" in "I don't know the palace in the sky, what year is it today?" Yu Que was a garrison of the Yuan Dynasty in the 14th century AD, guarding Anqing City. In 1358, Anqing city was captured by Chen Youliang. He committed suicide immediately, and his wife and children all threw themselves into a well. This was not only respected by his enemy Chen Youliang, but also praised by Zhu Yuanzhang. His biography was written by Song Lian. As soon as Song Lian started writing, he immediately wrote that he was from Liangzhou and of the Dangxiang clan.
I remember many years ago, an expert on Xixia history in Ningxia told me that the Dangxiang people were establishing the Xixia Dynasty and were eventually destroyed by Genghis Khan. Some of them joined Genghis Khan's Mongolian troops. Later, when the Mongols failed, many people changed their surname from Temu to Yu, and many of them went to Zhejiang. Yu Que also became Yuanmeng's general as a party member, but his surname seems to have been there originally and was not temporarily changed.
Over the years, I have received a large number of papers and rosters many times. Most of the authors' surnames are Yu, and they all come from the Temu clan and claim to be so. It seems that not only does surname change exist, but it is also quite large. It can be inferred from this that I am most likely a descendant of the Dangxiang people whose ancestral home is Wuwei.
Xianbei entered Mongolia from Xixia. After the Mongolian defeat, he changed his surname and entered Jiangsu and Zhejiang. But I once said jokingly that among our surnames, those who are close to the desert, fearless of long distances, energetic, and persevering, most likely have the bloodline to fight on the battlefield in the northwest. At least I have such characteristics. Nowadays, DNA genetic testing technology is advancing by leaps and bounds. Sooner or later, there will be clearer answers to the question of the ancestry of ancestors and descendants.
But as a cultural person, I value a cultural gene that transcends blood ties. Liangzhou obviously has a mysterious spiritual connection with me. Now we know that even genes can be modified, so no matter what, my genes have been modified by Liangzhou culture.
What makes me happy is that many people in Wuwei City now regard me as their hometown person. When I went there, they specially arranged a ceremony for me to lay flowers to the statue of Yu Que, and invited me to write an inscription for the name of the Liangzhou Cultural Research Institute. They even set up a study room for me in the institute. After visiting various historical sites, I am very grateful to them for the good repair of Kumarajiva Temple. I just have a little objection to the statue of Kumarajiva, that is, it looks too much like an ordinary Han monk.
Please think about it, his father is Indian and his mother is the sister of the King of Kucha. How many sculptors will be interested in his appearance. If he is too Han Chinese, it will conceal his identity as a world-class in-depth communicator of international culture and Chinese culture. In comparison, the standing statue of Tan Yao sculpted by Mr. Wu Weishan in the Yungang Grottoes in Shanxi is much better.
In addition, I hope Wuwei can become a popular choice for modern travelers. The reason is that there are so many exciting ancient stories that enhance culture that I just told. In ancient times, it was a big station in a big passage, so modern transportation should also be smoother.

summary.gistZh: 凉州（西北边陲）展现了超越血缘与族群隔阂的文化胸怀，融合多民族文化与西域文明，铸就了中华文化包容吸纳的硬朗基因。
summary.gistEn: Liangzhou (the Northwestern frontier) exemplified a cultural open-mindedness transcending bloodlines and ethnic boundaries, fusing diverse ethnic and Silk Road civilizations into a resilient cultural gene.

highlights.zh: 超越血缘限制：中华文化并非建立在单一族群血缘之上，而是在边陲交融中不断吸纳新鲜血液。
highlights.en: Beyond Bloodlines: Chinese culture is not built on single-ethnic bloodlines, but constantly absorbs fresh vitality from frontier exchanges.

highlights.zh: 丝绸之路的前哨：凉州作为文化交汇重镇，守护并传播了中原文化与佛教文明。
highlights.en: Frontier of the Silk Road: As a hub of cultural crossroads, Liangzhou preserved and disseminated both Central Plain and Buddhist civilizations.

highlights.zh: 强悍与儒雅的结合：凉州风范融合了边塞的雄浑豪迈与中原的文化典雅，展现了中国文化的刚柔相济。
highlights.en: Robustness & Elegance: Liangzhou style fused frontier heroism with Central Plain refined culture, displaying complementary strength and grace.

highlights.zh: 开放包容的示范：证明中国文化越在边疆越具包容性，越能展现生生不息的同化力。
highlights.en: Exemplar of Inclusivity: Proving that Chinese culture expands its inclusivity at frontiers, showcasing immortal assimilative power.

title: 长安：世界性的生活方式
folderName: 08_长安：世界性的生活方式
audioPath: 08_长安：世界性的生活方式/audio.m4a
quoteCardPath: 08_长安：世界性的生活方式/quote_card.jpg
transcriptZh:
大家好，我是余秋雨。现在继续讲课，我们的课我再重复一下，现在的大标题是中国文化的世界身份，副标题是国际视野下的中国文化史。
我们今天终于要讲到唐代了，唐代非常重要，唐代是中国文化的最高荣誉所在，因此也是中国文化取得世界身份的最高一级台阶。后来当然还有很多台阶，有的高有的低，但是在整体高度上都没有能够超过唐代。
既然是最高台阶，当然有标志性的意义了。因此大家都知道，“唐”这个字往往成为中国、中国人、中国文化的最简单的标记。大家到世界各地旅游的时候就会发现，哪儿都有唐人街，还有唐装、唐乐，这就是例证了。
唐人街在欧美不少城市当中大多是华人的聚居区，一般的呢与其他中等高等的社区相比，往往显得等级低一点，往往显得拥挤杂乱，而且还展示出一种艳俗密集的文化图景。这个我们看到有的时候不太愉快，这个是中国近代以来国力衰弱文化走向下行造成的一种对比。那实在是这个“唐”字有点蒙污了。
其实在唐代站在世界上的时候，那些城市所在地还是荒漠一片，而唐代的战略状态呢又是那么的典雅高贵。我们不妨看看现在日本的京都、奈良，那只不过是对中国唐代城市风韵的局部的模拟，但是今天看了，还让人叹为观止。
我们想想也比较有趣了，我们浩浩荡荡人数众多的中国人被两个遥远的朝代命名了，一个就是汉人，第二个就是唐人。比较起来呢，汉人这个称呼主要是在国内表明与其他少数民族的区别，而唐人的称呼呢主要是在国际间指向所有的中国人。可见，唐更具有世界身份。
中国领先世界的至高点
我现在要说的是，唐代不仅仅是中国的最高坐标，也是世界的最高坐标。我这么说并不是中国人自吹自擂的一种判断，不，这是一种世界共识。我到国外一些著名的古城遗址去参观的时候，总会遇到这样的情景。就是有个讲解员在讲，这应该是公元七世纪世界上最壮丽的城市，那观众就好奇地等待着讲解员还没有讲完的那个下半句。下半句是，当然除了长安。
我印象最深的是在埃及的卢克索，一个胖胖的女讲解员，她在说卢克索它的古地名叫做底比斯，是整个古代世界的顶端城市。她刚说到这一句，眼睛瞟到了几个中国人，马上笑着说，当然我没有把中国的唐代放在里面比。
那么国际间的历史学家的论断就更多了。我作为中国人，当然不好意思引述太多，但是对于有一位，他明确表示要构建21世纪全球通史的美国历史学家斯塔夫里阿诺斯（这个人我有一点兴趣），他在最新出版的《全球通史》当中做出了这样的判断，这个判断大家听一听，他说：
罗马崩溃之后，欧洲进入了中世纪，而中国则突飞猛进，一直是世界上人口最多、最富饶、最先进的国家。从公元6世纪到16世纪，中国文明以其顽强的生命力和对人类遗产的巨大贡献，始终居于领先世界的地位。
我想再读一下，这是斯塔夫里阿诺斯的一个论断了。他说罗马崩溃之后，欧洲进入了中世纪，而中国则突飞猛进，一直是世界上人口最多、最富饶、最先进的国家。从公元6世纪到16世纪，中国文明以其顽强的生命力和对人类遗产的巨大贡献，始终居于领先世界的地位。
这位斯塔夫里阿诺斯还特地说明，他说世界在1000年之间被中国引领，这个话还讲的比较保守，因为他说中国早在汉代已经成功地赶上了欧亚大陆的其他文明。如果按照他的这种算法，就是要再加五六百年了。那么我们中国人不妨含蓄一点，就说一千多年吧。在这一千多年当中，有个至高点，这个至高点就是唐代。唐代是让中国领先世界一千多年的那个至高点。
在这我特地要说一下，就是我们中国一直有一些学者认为，唐代并没有我们说的那么好，因为隐藏着很多阶级矛盾。军队打仗呢有的时候也会打败，那我真不知道他们这些学者有关好的标准是什么，是没有阶级矛盾吗？是不打败仗吗？其实按照我们的说法，分好还是坏主要看比较，就是通过比较来衡量、来判断。
空间中的长安
我想，在时间上把唐代和前后的朝代做对比，这是很多朋友都能做到的。我呢想提供一个特殊的方位，也就是从空间上做一些横向比较。这一点我想我们中国的历史学家做的比较少了。
我的比较是这样的，我稍微讲的快一点。在公元7世纪的时候，长安城的人口多达100万，罗马的人口已经不足5万。即使罗马还没有衰落的时候，它在面积上也只有长安的1/7。罗马灭亡以后，欧洲却一直弥漫着中世纪的神学极端主义的阴云，经常燃起那个焚烧异教徒的火堆。比如我曾经在西班牙当时的首都托雷多待过不少时间，仅仅这么一个城市，宗教裁判所就烧死了几十万人。
我们再从欧洲往东看，曾经气魄很大的波斯帝国，已经在7世纪的中叶被阿拉伯势力所占领。唐代为了保护他们的王室，还曾经设立过叫做波斯都护府。印度在差不多这个时间，因为戒日王的去世而陷入了混乱。
如果要比较城市的话，当时世界上比较像样的首都，除了长安之外，还有君士坦丁堡和巴格达。君士坦丁堡是拜占庭帝国的首都，它是连接东西方的一个枢纽。巴格达是当时气势如虹的阿拉伯帝国的中心，但是如果把这两个都城加起来，不管是面积还是人口，还不到长安的一半。这个都城的比较是这样的。
说到这些比较呢我已经有点担心了，因为就怕会引出太多太多有关长安的话题，耗费我们太多的时间。因此必须赶快回到文化上来，不要仅仅讲城市建筑和城市规模了。回到文化上来，大家可能会产生误会，因为我马上就要讲李白杜甫了。不，我们先请这些老人家暂时休息一下，我们先讲一点重要的文化前提，然后慢慢的我们以后还会把他们请出来。
没有国界的商业生活
大家一定还记得，我在课程前面讲述文化定义的时候已经表明，文化首先是一种习惯了的精神价值和生活方式。那我们先讲生活方式吧，我很着急的要告诉大家，唐代的长安已经习惯了一种世界性的生活方式，这是唐文化的重要基础。世界性的生活方式，这是不是说的有点过分？但事实确实如此。
长安人过着一种没有国界的商业生活。我要告诉大家，长安城占地80多平方公里，其中有两个商市，一个叫东市，一个叫西市，它们各占地一平方公里，加在一起它们就两平方公里。和整个长安城80多平方公里一比，它只有1/40，比例不大。但是不管是东市还是西市，这里边很好看了，里边各有一个井字形的街道，井字形的街道就分成了九个商业区，那就非常热闹了。东市和西市相比，西市集中了大量的国外来的客商，所以比东市还要繁荣；东市虽然没有西市这么繁荣，但热闹是足够的。
我曾经在《仰望长安》这篇文章当中，引用过一个日本和尚圆仁的日记，这个圆仁和尚到长安来研习佛法，住在不太繁华的东市。他留下了日记，这个和尚非常喜欢记日记，他这么写到：
6月27日，东市在半夜里边失火，烧毁了曹门以西二十四行的四千四百余家的商铺。
这个简单的记录，实在是一份重要的经济资料。一场大火烧掉了东市的曹门外，二十四行的四千多家店铺。那么要问，东市一共有多少行？据统计有二百二十行，那比二十四行就增加了快十倍了。大家请推算一下，二十四行就有四千多家商铺被烧掉，那么如果是二百二十行，能够烧掉多少商铺？它一共有多少商铺？这我还说的是不太繁荣的东市。
那西市大家想一想会怎么样呢？西市是一派异国情调，而奇怪是，正是这种异国情调成了长安城的主调。饭店酒肆很多，最吸引人的当然是胡姬酒肆。姬是女字边的“姬”，胡姬就是里面的服务小姐，都是中亚和西亚过来的美艳的姑娘。在酒肆的四周，到处可以看到拜占庭风格的建筑、罗马的艺术、印度的杂技，还有很多店铺呢喜欢装饰希腊的缠枝卷叶忍冬花的图案。
我前面已经讲到过，波斯被阿拉伯人占领了，但是在长安街上你既能看得到波斯人，也能看得到阿拉伯人。我在史料当中也没有发现过他们在长安斗殴的记录，可见大体上是相安无事。波斯人在战场是输家，但是在商场上却是赢家。长安的宝石、玛瑙、香料、药品都是他们在经营。
更加让人耳目一新的是，波斯的服装风靡了长安。我们知道，现在伊朗女性的服装有比较多的限制，但在那个时候正好相反，就是因为大胆时尚而引领潮流。不仅衣料很薄，又有美丽的图案，而且紧身低胸、经常变化，让各国女子特别是中国女子大开眼界。现在我们在东方壁画当中还能够看到一些踪影。
这让我想起一段笑话了，前些年有一些国粹派的年轻人强烈呼吁，所有的中国人只要参加奥运会或其他国际活动，必须一律穿汉服。当时我正好在北大上课，有的学生在课堂上的问答环节，问我对这样的主张怎么看？就是怎么看待中国人参加活动一定要穿汉服。我当时的回答有两条，第一条是以强制的方式来统一普通百姓的服装，不管什么借口都不是一件好事；第二条理由是，早在唐代的长安已经很少有人记得汉服是什么样的，唐代已经不这样了。
世界性的生活方式
好，讲了这个插话以后，我们再回到长安，长安是很少有这种极端思维的。在长安的街头外国人非常多，三万多名留学生，其中日本留学生就先后来过1万多。留学生也能参加科举考试，单单在唐代的晚期，这种科举的新罗士子，也就是现在朝鲜这个地方的新罗士子就有50多人。
大家知道所谓科举制度，其实就是文官选拔制度，考上了就能做官，因此那些外籍的考生考上以后，也就获得了在中国担任官职的资格，他们确实也有不少人留在中国做官。不仅有那么多留学生和外国的考生，更难得的是，朝廷对他们非常重视。
几年前，西安出土了一个方形的墓碑，上面刻着墓志铭，说明这个墓是一个19岁的日本留学生的坟墓。他在长安去世了，中国皇帝居然亲自给这个外国留学生写了墓志铭，墓志铭当中提到了“日本国”。请注意，这是历史上第一次正式出现“日本”这两个字，这两个字就出现在这个墓志铭上。记得2006年我到东京参加联合国世界文明大会的时候，日本还在纪念这件事，就是中国皇帝为一个19岁的日本留学生写墓碑这件事。我也参加了隆重的仪式。
我在仪式当中想，天哪，才19岁的一个外国孩子，唐朝皇帝居然亲自为他写墓志铭，这是一个什么样的朝代啊！因此，十几年以前，西安决定修复唐王朝的皇宫所在地大明宫遗址，日本政府决定要对基础工程出资援建。我是这个遗址修复工程的文化顾问，我知道这是外国对唐朝的一种遥远的报恩。
有一位波斯人居然被唐王朝派遣到拜占庭帝国做大使，请注意，他是波斯人，却是唐王朝的大使。他的名字在中国的史册当中叫做阿罗喊，阿是阿拉伯的“阿”，罗是罗马的“罗”，喊是大声喊叫的“喊”，这个字眼居然也进入到了我们的文本当中。现在有一个日本学者叫宇田亨，他认为阿罗喊其实就是阿伯拉罕，是个犹太人当中常见的名字。你想，既然是波斯人又有犹太的名字，因此他极有可能是移居波斯的犹太人。
为了这个阿罗喊，我曾经亲自历险，到伊朗西部一座不大的城市叫哈马丹，去考察犹太人最早移居波斯的遗迹。我不仅看到了古代犹太人在这里安葬的坟墓，而且还见到了活着的伊朗犹太人。我们都知道现在在国际政治当中，伊朗和犹太人似乎关系很不好，但是古代不是这样。一个波斯犹太人居然担任了中国大使，去拜占庭上任。由此可以证明，唐朝由于世界性的生活方式，一切界限都有可能消除。
这种世界性的生活方式又发生在一个世界级的城市环境当中，它的城市环境的等级也是世界级的。长安的朱雀大街，宽155米，比巴黎的香榭丽舍大街还要宽30多米。根据考古发现，长安当时的街道两边，都安置了下水道，下水道边上种了榆树和槐树，这边上还有一米多宽左右的人行道。
长安城里划出了108坊，坊是土字边加一个四方形的“方”。每当太阳下山的时候，长安就宵禁了，把一个个坊都关起来，市民只能在坊里边活动，坊当然也不小。有的市民，比较追求自由的市民，如果觉得住在长安不太方便，那你可以移居到东边的洛阳、四川的成都，当然最自由的地方是南方的扬州，当时扬州已经是一个有大量外国船只来来往往的码头，而夜生活又更加富裕放荡、无拘无束。
就管理而言，长安城的管理比洛阳、扬州都要严格的多，因为它是首都。同时也因为严格的管理，使它成了当时世界各国首都当中最安全的首都。你稍稍比较就可以知道，当时的世界非常动乱。
transcriptEn:
Hello everyone, my name is Yu Qiuyu. Now let’s continue with the lecture. Let me repeat our lesson again. The current title is The World Identity of Chinese Culture, and the subtitle is The History of Chinese Culture from an International Perspective.
Today we are finally going to talk about the Tang Dynasty. The Tang Dynasty is very important. The Tang Dynasty is the highest honor of Chinese culture, and therefore it is also the highest step for Chinese culture to achieve world status. Of course there were many steps later, some high and some low, but none of them surpassed the Tang Dynasty in terms of overall height.
Since it is the highest step, of course it has iconic significance. Therefore, everyone knows that the word "Tang" often becomes the simplest symbol of China, Chinese people, and Chinese culture. When you travel around the world, you will find that there are Chinatowns everywhere, as well as Tang costumes and Tang music. This is an example.
Chinatowns are mostly Chinese settlements in many European and American cities. Generally speaking, compared with other mid-level and high-end communities, Chinatowns often appear to be lower-level, crowded and messy, and also display a gaudy and dense cultural scene. Sometimes we are not happy to see this. This is a contrast caused by the decline of China's national power and the downward trend of its culture in modern times. That’s because the word “Tang” is a bit tainted.
In fact, when the Tang Dynasty stood in the world, those cities were still deserted, and the strategic state of the Tang Dynasty was so elegant and noble. We might as well take a look at Kyoto and Nara in Japan today. They are only partial simulations of the urban charm of the Tang Dynasty in China, but when we look at them today, they are still breathtaking.
It is more interesting when we think about it. Our vast and numerous Chinese people were named by two distant dynasties, one is the Han people, and the second is the Tang people. In comparison, the term Han people mainly refers to the difference from other ethnic minorities domestically, while the term Tang people mainly refers to all Chinese internationally. It can be seen that Tang has a more worldly identity.
China leads the world at its highest point
What I want to say now is that the Tang Dynasty was not only the highest coordinate of China, but also the highest coordinate of the world. What I say is not a judgment that the Chinese are bragging about. No, this is a world consensus. When I visit some famous ancient city ruins abroad, I always encounter such scenes. There was a commentator saying that this should be the most magnificent city in the world in the seventh century AD, and the audience was curiously waiting for the second half of the sentence that the commentator had not yet finished. The second half of the sentence is, except of course Chang'an.
What impressed me most was a fat female guide in Luxor, Egypt. She was saying that the ancient name of Luxor was Thebes, and it was the top city of the entire ancient world. As soon as she said this, she caught sight of a few Chinese people and immediately said with a smile, "Of course I didn't compare China's Tang Dynasty in it."
Then there are more conclusions from international historians. As a Chinese, of course I am embarrassed to quote too much, but there is an American historian, Stavrianos, who has made it clear that he wants to construct a general history of the world in the 21st century (I am a little interested in this person). He made this judgment in his latest publication "A General History of the World". Please listen to this judgment. He said:
After the collapse of Rome, Europe entered the Middle Ages, while China made rapid progress and has always been the most populous, richest, and most advanced country in the world. From the 6th century to the 16th century AD, Chinese civilization has always led the world with its tenacious vitality and great contribution to human heritage.
I want to read it again, this is a statement of Stavrianos. He said that after the collapse of Rome, Europe entered the Middle Ages, while China made rapid progress and has always been the most populous, richest and most advanced country in the world. From the 6th century to the 16th century AD, Chinese civilization has always led the world with its tenacious vitality and great contribution to human heritage.
Stavrianos also specifically stated that he said that the world was led by China within 1,000 years. This statement was relatively conservative, because he said that China had successfully caught up with other civilizations in Eurasia as early as the Han Dynasty. If he follows his calculation, it will take another five to six hundred years. So we Chinese might as well be a little more reserved and say more than a thousand years. During these more than a thousand years, there was a high point, and this high point was the Tang Dynasty. The Tang Dynasty was the highest point that allowed China to lead the world for more than a thousand years.
I would like to say here that some scholars in China have always believed that the Tang Dynasty was not as good as we say because there were many hidden class conflicts. The army sometimes loses in battles, so I really don't know what the good standards are for scholars like them. Is there no class conflict? Isn’t the battle lost? In fact, according to us, whether something is good or bad mainly depends on comparison, that is, to measure and judge through comparison.
Chang'an in space
I think that comparing the Tang Dynasty with the previous and later dynasties in time is something that many friends can do. I want to provide a special perspective, that is, make some horizontal comparisons from space. I think our Chinese historians have done relatively little on this point.
My comparison is this, I speak a little faster. In the 7th century AD, the population of Chang'an City was as high as 1 million, and the population of Rome was less than 50,000. Even before Rome declined, its area was only 1/7 of Chang'an. After the fall of Rome, Europe has been permeated by the dark cloud of medieval theological extremism, which often lit the fire that burned pagans. For example, I once spent a lot of time in Toledo, the capital of Spain at that time. In this city alone, the Inquisition burned hundreds of thousands of people to death.
Looking eastward from Europe, the once powerful Persian Empire was occupied by Arab forces in the middle of the 7th century. In order to protect their royal family, the Tang Dynasty also established a Persian Protectorate. At about this time, India fell into chaos due to the death of King Harsha.
If you want to compare cities, in addition to Chang'an, the more decent capitals in the world at that time were Constantinople and Baghdad. Constantinople was the capital of the Byzantine Empire and a hub connecting the East and the West. Baghdad was the center of the powerful Arab Empire at that time, but if the two capitals were added together, they would be less than half of Chang'an in terms of area and population. The comparison in this capital city is this.
Speaking of these comparisons, I am already a little worried, because I am afraid that it will lead to too many topics about Chang'an and consume too much of our time. Therefore, we must quickly return to culture, and don’t just talk about urban architecture and city scale. Back to culture, you may have misunderstandings, because I will talk about Li Bai and Du Fu soon. No, let's ask these elderly people to take a break first. Let's talk about some important cultural prerequisites first, and then slowly we will invite them out in the future.
Business life without borders
You must still remember that when I explained the definition of culture earlier in the course, I stated that culture is first of all a habitual spiritual value and lifestyle. Let's talk about lifestyle first. I am very anxious to tell you that Chang'an in the Tang Dynasty was accustomed to a cosmopolitan lifestyle, which was an important foundation of Tang culture. A cosmopolitan lifestyle, is this a bit too much? But it is true.
The people of Chang'an live a commercial life without national borders. I want to tell you that the city of Chang'an covers an area of ​​more than 80 square kilometers. There are two commercial markets in it, one is called the East Market and the other is called the West Market. They each cover an area of ​​one square kilometer, and together they account for two square kilometers. Compared with the entire Chang'an City of more than 80 square kilometers, it is only 1/40, which is a small proportion. But whether it is the East Market or the West Market, it is very beautiful here. There is a tic-shaped street in each. The tic-shaped street is divided into nine commercial areas, which is very lively. Compared with the West Market, the West Market has concentrated a large number of foreign merchants, so it is more prosperous than the East Market; although the East Market is not as prosperous as the West Market, it is lively enough.
In the article "Looking Up to Chang'an", I quoted the diary of a Japanese monk Ennin. This monk Ennin came to Chang'an to study Buddhism and lived in the less prosperous Dongshi. He left a diary. This monk liked keeping diaries very much. He wrote:
On June 27, a fire broke out in Dongshi in the middle of the night, burning more than 4,400 shops in the 24th row west of Caomen.
This simple record is really an important piece of economic information. A fire burned down more than 4,000 shops in 24 rows outside Caomen in Dongshi. So I want to ask, how many rows are there in Dongshi? According to statistics, there are two hundred and twenty lines, which is almost ten times more than twenty-four lines. Please do some calculations. In the 24th row, more than 4,000 shops were burned. So if it is 220 rows, how many shops can be burned? How many shops does it have in total? I am also talking about the less prosperous Dongshi.
So what will happen if you think about it in West City? The West Market has an exotic atmosphere, and the strange thing is that it is this exotic atmosphere that has become the main theme of Chang'an City. There are many hotels and restaurants, the most attractive one is of course Orchid Restaurant. Ji is the "ji" next to the female character, and Hu Ji is the service lady inside. They are all beautiful girls from Central and West Asia. Around the wine shop, you can see Byzantine-style architecture, Roman art, Indian acrobatics, and many shops that like to decorate with Greek honeysuckle patterns.
I have already mentioned before that Persia was occupied by the Arabs, but you can see both Persians and Arabs on Chang'an Street. I haven't found any record of them fighting in Chang'an in the historical materials, so it can be seen that they were generally in peace. The Persians were losers on the battlefield, but winners in the marketplace. They are in charge of Chang'an's gems, agates, spices, and medicines.
What is even more refreshing is that Persian clothing became popular in Chang'an. We know that Iranian women's clothing has more restrictions now, but at that time it was just the opposite. They were leading the trend because of their bold fashion. Not only are the fabrics very thin, but they also have beautiful patterns, they are tight-fitting and low-cut, and they change frequently, which is an eye-opener for women from all over the world, especially Chinese women. Now we can still see some traces of it in Eastern murals.
This reminds me of a joke. A few years ago, some young people from the National Essence Party strongly called for all Chinese to wear Hanfu as long as they participate in the Olympics or other international events. I happened to be taking a class at Peking University at that time, and some students asked me during the question and answer session in class what I thought of such a proposition. It’s about how Chinese people must wear Hanfu when participating in activities. I had two answers at the time. The first was that it was not a good thing to unify the clothing of ordinary people in a forced way, no matter what the excuse. The second reason was that as early as the Tang Dynasty, few people in Chang'an remembered what Hanfu looked like, and this was no longer the case in the Tang Dynasty.
cosmopolitan lifestyle
Okay, after this interjection, let's go back to Chang'an. Chang'an rarely has such extreme thinking. There are many foreigners on the streets of Chang'an. There are more than 30,000 international students, including more than 10,000 Japanese students. Foreign students can also take the imperial examination. In the late Tang Dynasty alone, there were more than 50 Silla scholars in this kind of imperial examination, which is now the Silla scholar in North Korea.
Everyone knows that the so-called imperial examination system is actually a civil service selection system. Those who pass the examination can become officials. Therefore, after those foreign candidates pass the examination, they are qualified to hold official positions in China. Indeed, many of them stay in China to serve as officials. Not only are there so many overseas students and foreign candidates, but what is even more rare is that the imperial court attaches great importance to them.
A few years ago, a square tombstone was unearthed in Xi'an, with an epitaph engraved on it, indicating that the tomb was that of a 19-year-old Japanese student studying abroad. He passed away in Chang'an, and the Chinese emperor actually wrote an epitaph for the foreign student himself, and the epitaph mentioned "Japan". Please note that this is the first time in history that the word "Japan" officially appears on this epitaph. I remember that when I went to Tokyo to attend the United Nations World Civilization Conference in 2006, Japan was still commemorating this event, which was the Chinese emperor writing a tombstone for a 19-year-old Japanese student. I also participated in the grand ceremony.
During the ceremony, I thought, my God, the emperor of the Tang Dynasty actually wrote an epitaph for a 19-year-old foreign kid himself. What kind of dynasty was this! Therefore, more than ten years ago, Xi'an decided to restore the ruins of the Daming Palace, where the imperial palace of the Tang Dynasty was located, and the Japanese government decided to fund infrastructure projects. I am the cultural consultant for the restoration project of this site, and I know that this is a distant repayment of gratitude from foreign countries to the Tang Dynasty.
There was a Persian who was actually sent by the Tang Dynasty to the Byzantine Empire as an ambassador. Please note that he was a Persian, but he was the ambassador of the Tang Dynasty. His name is called Aluo Sheng in Chinese history, A is the Arabic "A", Luo is the Roman "Luo", and Sheng is the "Shout" of shouting loudly. This word has actually entered our text. Now there is a Japanese scholar named Hiroshi Uda, who believes that Alo is actually Abraham, a common name among Jews. You think, since he is a Persian and has a Jewish name, he is most likely a Jew who immigrated to Persia.
For this reason, I once personally took an adventure to Hamadan, a small city in western Iran, to inspect the remains of the earliest Jewish immigrants to Persia. Not only did I see the tombs where ancient Jews were buried here, but I also met living Iranian Jews. We all know that Iran and the Jews seem to have a very bad relationship in international politics now, but this was not the case in ancient times. A Persian Jew actually served as China's ambassador to Byzantium. This can prove that due to the cosmopolitan lifestyle of the Tang Dynasty, all boundaries were likely to be eliminated.
This cosmopolitan lifestyle takes place in a world-class urban environment, and the level of its urban environment is also world-class. Chang'an's Zhuque Street is 155 meters wide, which is more than 30 meters wider than the Champs Elysées in Paris. According to archaeological discoveries, sewers were installed on both sides of the streets in Chang'an at that time. Elm and locust trees were planted beside the sewers. There was also a sidewalk about one meter wide.
There are 108 squares designated in Chang'an City. "Fang" is the word "Tu" with a square "square" next to it. Whenever the sun goes down, Chang'an imposes a curfew and locks up each and every workshop. Citizens can only move around inside the workshop. Of course, the workshop is not small. For some citizens who pursue freedom, if they find it inconvenient to live in Chang'an, they can move to Luoyang in the east or Chengdu in Sichuan. Of course, the freest place is Yangzhou in the south. At that time, Yangzhou was already a dock with a large number of foreign ships coming and going, and the nightlife was more affluent, debauched and unrestrained.
In terms of management, the management of Chang'an City is much stricter than that of Luoyang and Yangzhou because it is the capital. At the same time, due to strict management, it became the safest capital among the capitals of the world at that time. As you can see from a little comparison, the world at that time was very turbulent.

summary.gistZh: 唐代长安是古代世界第一座国际化大都市，以开放的胸襟吸引全球商贾、留学生与艺术家，展现了中国文化最辉煌、自信的世界性生活方式。
summary.gistEn: Tang Dynasty Chang'an was the ancient world's premier cosmopolitan metropolis, attracting global merchants, scholars, and artists with open confidence—exemplifying Chinese culture's most brilliant international lifestyle.

highlights.zh: 真正的世界都市：长安人口破百万，外国人占相当比例，官员、将军甚至包括许多外族人士。
highlights.en: A True Global Metropolis: Exceeding a million residents with a large foreign population, even government officials and generals hailed from abroad.

highlights.zh: 文化自信的峰值：不惧外来文化侵蚀，反而兼收并蓄，将西域音乐、服饰与饮食融入日常生活。
highlights.en: Peak Cultural Confidence: Unafraid of foreign influence, Chang'an enthusiastically integrated Silk Road music, fashion, and cuisine into daily life.

highlights.zh: 气度与包容：对待不同宗教（佛教、景教、祆教、伊斯兰教）一视同仁，给予高度自由。
highlights.en: Magnanimity & Freedom: Treating diverse faiths (Buddhism, Nestorianism, Zoroastrianism, Islam) with equal respect and freedom.

highlights.zh: 永恒的盛唐气象：长安不仅是一座城市，更是中国文化心胸开阔、万国来朝的大国象喻。
highlights.en: Immortal Grandeur of Tang: Chang'an was more than a city; it remains a metaphor for Chinese culture's open heart and cosmic grandeur.

title: 利玛窦：中国文化的非侵略本性
