transcriptZh:
大家好，我是余秋雨,我们继续讲课。
我上次讲到米开朗基罗只比王阳明小三岁，他们是同一个时代的人。我现在要讲到，在王阳明去世以后半个世纪，有一个意大利的传教士来到了中国，这个人的名字叫利玛窦。
就是半个世纪多一点，你看，由于欧洲的文艺复兴改变了他们许许多多的社会结构，改变了他们的科技，改变了他们的生存方式。所以就可以用传教的方式来传播西方文明，或者是以传播西方文明的方式来传教，利玛窦来了。
利玛窦的中国札记
这个人来到中国非常重要，这个大家都知道，我不详细讲了。他在17世纪的第一年在南京见到了一个中国官员叫徐光启，光辉的光，启发的启，这个大家都知道的，徐光启。
我认为他重要，所以有一年我专门去了葡萄牙的科英布拉大学，我知道他在那工作过一段时间。但遗憾的是我到那个大学去采访、访问的时候，他们那儿已经不是很清楚。有少数人清楚，但是却需要收取我们比较多的拍摄费。所以我们当时觉得唉呀，只有我们中国人真正能深深地感觉到利玛窦的重要性。
由于利玛窦的来华，他在中国待了很长时间，最后终于写了一部书叫《利玛窦的中国札记》，中国在世界的形象又得到了进一步的矫正。《利玛窦的中国札记》是继《马可波罗游记》之后的又一个重要文本，这个文本在某种意义上是对中国的文化进行了更完整的论述。
因为马可波罗只是一个旅行的旁观者，而利玛窦却不一样了，他是一个深入了很长时间的学者，所以他的发言具有很高的说服力。我曾经用《利玛窦的中国札记》里边的话在国际上来反驳中国威胁论。
因为当年利玛窦到中国来以后，和他一起来的一些欧洲传教士也看到中国的国力很强盛，因为明朝的时候中国国力很强盛，特别是朱元璋、朱棣以后国力还是很强盛，而且部队也很精良。
在他们想象当中按照中国的逻辑，钱不少，军队又很精良，那是一定要侵犯外国的，甚至一定于会打到欧洲去，有一种巨大的不安全感。所以利玛窦认真地研究中国文明，而且他认真地结识中国的各种朋友，高的、低的、官方的和一般的文人，都接触了。
接触下来，最后在他的晚年把自己的结论写在《中国札记》里边了，我就在世界文明大会上专门讲了《利玛窦中国札记》里这样的事情。我把我当时讲的这段话读一下，我说：
继马克波罗之后，另一个完整地用国际眼光来考察中国文明的是意大利天主教耶稣会的传教士利玛窦。与马可波罗不同的是，利玛窦在中国待了整整30年，深入研究了中华文明的历史和经典，与许多中国的学者进行了充分的交往。所以他在晚年所写的《利玛窦的中国札记》的第一卷第六章中，表述了他几十年研究的一个重要答案，那就是中国文明的非侵略、非扩张的本性。
利玛窦说：虽然中国人有装备精良的陆军和海军，很容易征服邻近的国家，但是他们的皇上和人民都从来没有发动过侵略战争，他们很满足于自己已经有的东西，没有征服的野心，在这方面他们与欧洲人很不相同。
利玛窦说：当时有一些欧洲学者写的文章认为，中国曾经或必然会征服邻国，扩张自己的势力范围，与他同行的一些西方传教士也有类似的观点，他认为这种说法是不真实的。所以他的结论是：我仔细研究了中国长达4000年的历史，不得不承认我从未见到这类征服的记录，也没有听说过他们扩展国界的事实。
他还说，他经常拿这个问题询问中国最有学问的历史学家，他们的回答完全一致，从来没有发生过侵略或扩张的事情，也不可能发生这样的事情。利玛窦还专门解释：成吉思汗当时大规模的征服，当时中华文明的主体部位也是被征服的对象而不是征服者。
两种文明的交融碰撞
利玛窦的这本札记在欧洲的影响很大，1615年在德国出版，后来拉丁文本有四种，法文本有三种，德文、西班牙文、意大利文和英文各一种，所以影响非常大。那么我在世界文明大会的主题演讲当中还专门讲，我说：
顺着利玛窦的思路，我也开始了我的学术研究。我翻阅了世界各国的历史文献，我发现古代的希腊人、波斯人、罗马人、阿拉伯人，近代的西班牙人、葡萄牙人、荷兰人、英国人、德国人、日本人，都在历史文献当中留下了一系列征服世界的计划。但是在中国浩如烟海的各类典籍当中，怎么也找不到类似的计划。
我用利玛窦的这个结论去说服了世界上那些对中国文化有疑虑的人，是不是说服了不太清楚，但至少当时在会场上的一部分文化人，他如果有文化逻辑的话，应该能感觉到这里边的前后关系，这是利玛窦的第一个意义，他在《中国札记》当中论述了中国文化的非侵略、非扩张的本性，这一点我们很感谢利玛窦，因为他实在是讲了真话。
另外，利玛窦还有一个文化作用，这个文化作用就是他和徐光启的见面。因为徐光启是一个中国的高官，这不是小事。而且他又是儒家出身，徐光启本身是儒家，他们两个人见面以后一起翻译了六册《几何原本》，中国就开始懂得了西方数学，这具有划时代的作用。
徐光启本身又皈依了天主教，虔诚地信奉，还一直做礼拜。这个给了我们一个信息，就是中国的高层官员如果能够按照利玛窦的路子也接受西方文明的话，那也就可能以和平方式实行两种文明的对接和对话了。
你看，因为徐光启是天主教徒，所以他去世时的墓碑是拉丁文的，可见两种文化连在一起了。他死的时候尽管用的是拉丁文的墓碑，但中国的皇帝还罢朝一日对他表示悼念，你看两种文化是不是有可能和睦相处呢？但结果是后来并没有和睦相处，打起来了。
这里边我必须讲这么一个事实了，就是他的坟墓过了一阵搬到了自己的家乡，那就是在上海城外的一个地方，上海城就是现在的老城乡那一带了。当时城外有个地方，由于他的墓在那儿，所以姓徐的人也都集中在那儿，汇集在那儿，所以那个地方就叫做徐家汇。
后来他们所代表的两种文明对接过、和好过、争吵过，最后终于打仗了。打仗以后首先体现的就是鸦片战争，英国人在香港打了仗以后尽管赢了，但觉得那儿的反抗情绪很强烈，于是就在沿着那个海岸线北上的时候终于看到了一座城市，面对大海，背后有一条浩浩荡荡的长江，那么这地方比其他地方更能够适合他们居住，所以他们就在那定居了。
定居以后他们按照他们的方式来过他们的日子，做他们的礼拜。就在他们做礼拜的时候，突然发现上海有一个地方居然一直举行着天主教的礼拜活动，那就是徐家汇—— 徐光启墓所在地，于是他们就在那造教堂、造学校、造藏书楼，出现了徐家汇文明。
我曾经在《上海人》这篇文章当中专门讲过，我说：徐家汇文明是上海文明的枢纽。那么从这里其实也可以看出一点，如果从文化和文明的视角来看，有一些血迹斑斑的生死搏斗本来有可能以和平的方式解决，民族主义、铁血军事未必是历史的必然。
谢谢大家
！
transcriptEn:
Hello everyone, I am Yu Qiuyu, let’s continue the lecture.
I mentioned last time that Michelangelo was only three years younger than Wang Yangming, and they were from the same era. I want to talk about it now. Half a century after Wang Yangming’s death, an Italian missionary came to China. This man’s name was Matteo Ricci.
Just over half a century, you see, the Renaissance in Europe changed many of their social structures, their technology, and their way of survival. So we can use missionary methods to spread Western civilization, or we can use missionary methods to spread Western civilization. Matteo Ricci is here.
Matteo Ricci's Notes on China
It is very important for this person to come to China. Everyone knows this, so I won’t go into details. In the first year of the 17th century, he met a Chinese official named Xu Guangqi in Nanjing, the glorious light, the enlightening Qi, everyone knows this, Xu Guangqi.
I thought he was important, so one year I went to the University of Coimbra in Portugal, and I knew he had worked there for a while. But unfortunately, when I went to that university to interview and visit, they were no longer very clear about it. A few people know it, but they need to charge us a relatively high filming fee. So we thought at that time, alas, only we Chinese can truly feel the importance of Matteo Ricci deeply.
Because of Matteo Ricci's visit to China, he stayed in China for a long time and finally wrote a book called "Matteo Ricci's Notes on China", which further corrected China's image in the world. "Matteo Ricci's Notes on China" is another important text after "Marco Polo's Travels". In a sense, this text provides a more complete discussion of Chinese culture.
Because Marco Polo was just a traveling bystander, but Matteo Ricci was different. He was a scholar who had been in depth for a long time, so his speech was highly persuasive. I once used the words in "Matteo Ricci's Notes on China" to refute the China threat theory internationally.
Because after Matteo Ricci came to China, some European missionaries who came with him also saw that China's national power was very strong, because China's national power was very strong during the Ming Dynasty, especially after Zhu Yuanzhang and Zhu Di, its national power was still very strong, and its troops were also very sophisticated.
In their imagination, according to China's logic, if they have a lot of money and a very sophisticated army, they will definitely invade foreign countries, and they will even attack Europe. They feel a huge sense of insecurity. Therefore, Matteo Ricci seriously studied Chinese civilization, and he seriously made friends with various Chinese friends, including high-level, low-level, official, and ordinary literati.
After getting in touch with him, he finally wrote his conclusions in "Notes on China" in his later years. I talked about such things in "Matteo Ricci's Notes on China" at the World Civilization Conference. I read what I said at that time, and I said:
After Marco Polo, another person who completely examined Chinese civilization from an international perspective was the Italian Catholic Jesuit missionary Matteo Ricci. Unlike Marco Polo, Matteo Ricci stayed in China for a full 30 years, studied the history and classics of Chinese civilization in depth, and had full interactions with many Chinese scholars. Therefore, in Chapter 6 of the first volume of "Matteo Ricci's Notes on China" written in his later years, he expressed an important answer to his decades of research, which is the non-aggression and non-expansion nature of Chinese civilization.
Matteo Ricci said: Although the Chinese have a well-equipped army and navy and can easily conquer neighboring countries, their emperor and people have never launched an aggressive war. They are content with what they already have and have no ambition to conquer. In this regard, they are very different from Europeans.
Matteo Ricci said: At that time, some European scholars wrote articles that believed that China had or would inevitably conquer neighboring countries and expand its sphere of influence. Some Western missionaries who traveled with him also had similar views. He believed that this statement was untrue. So his conclusion is: I have carefully studied China's 4,000-year history, and I have to admit that I have never seen records of such conquests, nor have I heard of the fact that they expanded their national borders.
He also said that he often asked this question to the most knowledgeable historians in China, and their answers were completely consistent. There had never been any invasion or expansion, and such a thing could not happen. Matteo Ricci also specifically explained: Genghis Khan’s large-scale conquests at that time, the main parts of Chinese civilization were also the conquered objects rather than the conquerors.
The blending and collision of two civilizations
Matteo Ricci's Notes had a great influence in Europe. It was published in Germany in 1615. Later, there were four Latin versions, three French versions, one each in German, Spanish, Italian and English, so it had a great influence. Then I specifically talked about it in my keynote speech at the World Civilization Conference. I said:
Following Matteo Ricci's ideas, I also started my academic research. I read through historical documents from various countries around the world, and I found that the ancient Greeks, Persians, Romans, and Arabs, as well as the modern Spaniards, Portuguese, Dutch, British, Germans, and Japanese, all left a series of plans to conquer the world in historical documents. But in the vast sea of ​​various classics in China, no similar plan can be found.
I used Matteo Ricci’s conclusion to convince those who had doubts about Chinese culture in the world. It’s not clear whether I convinced it, but at least some of the cultural people at the conference at the time. If they had cultural logic, they should be able to feel the connection here. This is the first meaning of Matteo Ricci. He discussed the non-aggression and non-expansion nature of Chinese culture in "Notes on China". We are very grateful to Matteo Ricci for this, because he really told the truth.
In addition, Matteo Ricci also has a cultural role, and this cultural role is his meeting with Xu Guangqi. Because Xu Guangqi is a senior official in China, this is no small matter. Moreover, he was a Confucian, and Xu Guangqi himself was a Confucian. After the two of them met, they translated six volumes of "Elements of Geometry" together, and China began to understand Western mathematics, which had an epoch-making effect.
Xu Guangqi himself converted to Catholicism, believed in it devoutly, and continued to worship. This gives us a message that if China's top officials can follow Matteo Ricci's approach and accept Western civilization, it will be possible to implement docking and dialogue between the two civilizations in a peaceful way.
You see, because Xu Guangqi was a Catholic, the tombstone when he died was in Latin, which shows that the two cultures are connected. Even though he had a Latin tombstone when he died, the Chinese emperor still paid tribute to him. Do you think it is possible for the two cultures to live in harmony? But the result was that they did not live in harmony and started fighting.
I must tell you the fact that his grave was moved to his hometown after a while, which is a place outside Shanghai, which is now the old urban and rural area. At that time, there was a place outside the city. Because his tomb was there, people with the surname Xu also gathered there, so the place was called Xujiahui.
Later, the two civilizations they represented met, reconciled, quarreled, and finally went to war. The first thing that emerged after the war was the Opium War. Although the British won the war in Hong Kong, they felt that the resistance there was very strong, so when they went north along the coastline, they finally saw a city facing the sea with the mighty Yangtze River behind it. This place was more suitable for them to live than other places, so they settled there.
After settling down, they lived their lives and worshiped in their own way. While they were worshiping, they suddenly discovered that there was a place in Shanghai where Catholic worship services had been held. That was Xujiahui, where the tomb of Xu Guangqi was located. So they built churches, schools, and libraries there, and the Xujiahui civilization emerged.
I once specifically talked about it in the article "Shanghai People". I said: Xujiahui civilization is the hub of Shanghai civilization. Well, we can actually see something from this. From the perspective of culture and civilization, some blood-stained life-and-death struggles could have been resolved in a peaceful way. Nationalism and iron-blooded military may not be a historical necessity.
thank you all
!

summary.gistZh: 明末传教士利玛窦在中国成功传播西方科学与基督教，其经验揭示了中国文化崇尚和平、尊重智慧、不具侵略本性的文明特质。
summary.gistEn: The success of Jesuit Matteo Ricci in late-Ming China revealed the fundamental traits of Chinese civilization: revering peace and wisdom, with a inherently non-aggressive nature.

highlights.zh: 利玛窦的本土化策略：穿儒服、通汉语、尊孔孟，用科学（地图、天文学）与道德赢得中国士大夫的尊重。
highlights.en: Matteo Ricci's Localization Strategy: Wearing Confucian robes, mastering Chinese, and using science (maps, astronomy) and virtue to win scholars' respect.

highlights.zh: 非侵略性的证明：中国文化乐于接受外来的真理与科技，只要其不带有武力威胁或蛮横征服。
highlights.en: Proof of Non-Aggression: Chinese culture readily accepts foreign truth and technology as long as it arrives without military force or coercion.

highlights.zh: 东西方文明的黄金对话：利玛窦与徐光启的合作（翻译《几何原本》）树立了跨文化理性交流的典范。
highlights.en: Golden Age of East-West Dialogue: Ricci's collaboration with Xu Guangqi (translating Euclid's Elements) set a model for rational cross-cultural exchange.

highlights.zh: 包容非排他：中国文化天生具备融通其他文明成果的胸怀，而非非黑即白的文明对抗。
highlights.en: Inclusivity over Exclusivity: Chinese culture inherently possesses the capacity to integrate achievements of other civilizations.

title: 选拔文官：科举制度的五大优点
folderName: 10_选拔文官：科举制度的五大优点
audioPath: 10_选拔文官：科举制度的五大优点/audio.m4a
quoteCardPath: 10_选拔文官：科举制度的五大优点/quote_card.jpg
transcriptZh:
大家好，我是余秋雨，今天要讲中华文化长寿的一个实践性的大工程。这个工程延续了一千三百多年，那真叫大工程了，叫科举制度。我首先要撇除大家的一个误会，以为科举制度是在选择最好的诗人、散文家。搞错了，不是。科举制度选拔的是各级管理者，按照我们一般的说法叫做文官。
一个社会、一个国家、一个体制，不管在什么情况下需要延续下去，它都需要浩浩荡荡的一支管理队伍。世界上有的地方最后文明破败，有各种各样的原因，有个原因就是管理者不够了，有很多地方失控了，有好多行业失控了。有好多管理者人在，但他们能力不行或者威望不够，所以实际上也失控了。那么中国和其他文明一样，都想选择这样的管理者，所以就出现了这个科举制度，科举制度是这么来的。它重要在哪里呢？我想举几点来说明一下，也就是科举制度的优点。
保全文化土壤和统一的选拔
第一，从朝廷的角度看，一个大的国家需要很多管理人才。但是从文化的角度看，也就是从中国文化的角度看，它也需要有密密层层的管理人才。大家知道吗？当一个国家变得破碎的时候，文化往往也只能跟随着破碎。所以在这种情况下面，保全文化的土壤是文化一个非常重要的使命，科举制度就承担了这个使命。它不仅仅是为朝廷选择了管理人才，而且也为文化选择了保全的土壤。 这是它的第一点，这个意思我想大家都能够明白。
第二，其他重大的文明，在它开始的时候，由于在一代雄主的带领下，有很多他手下的能干的战友，构成了一个良好的管理系统。但是由于地域太大，方位太多，各地管理者很容易自成格局。时间一长，便会产生分裂。但是科举制度是全国统一的，以统一的标准、统一的机构完成统一的选拔。这样的方式堵塞了分裂的可能，同时反过来又保护了文化。
大家明白没有？如果我们国家分成很多很多小的地方政权，小的地方政权在选拔官吏的时候，最容易的是根据自己的意图来，根据自己的好恶来，根据自己的衡量标准来。结果，全国是不统一的，你这个地方选拔的干部放到其他地方是没法用的。不是实际上能用不能用，而是对方也不承认，这是你们这位太守选出来的官，你那个太守离我们那么远，他人又已经不在了，我们为什么要用你太守的标准，不用我们这里太守的标准呢？他们都可以用这样的一个标准来，所以就各自为政了。
但是没想到，科举制度它用了统一的标准、统一的机构，完成了统一的选拔。科学制度出来的人放到哪一个地方做官都可以了，因为它是全国统一的，这是科举制度第二个标准，也是保证我们中国这个国家统一，中国文化这个文化统一的一个基础。
源源不断的管理者
第三，这样的选拔，如果发生过几次、几十次已经是壮观了。但是即使这样，官员也会老去，也会病死，永远缺乏应该有的一支充足的队伍储备。那怎么办呢？我哪里有那么大的精力，去层层叠叠地以统一的标准去选拔官员呢？
没想到，科举制度每隔三年考试，这样的话就提供了大量的源源不断的管理人才，使中华文化保持着有序的延续，这是个重要原因。不是心血来潮，朝廷下令，我们已经十年没有选拔官员了，我们今年开始选拔；下次是二十年没选拔官员了，我们这次选拔，心血来潮，引起风潮，不行！中国的科举制度每三年一次，就为朝廷源源不断地提供官员，这也使得中国古代漫长的历史上，一直不缺乏管理者。
第四个原因，就是有那么多的需求，要做到这一点必须在全国找到非常丰沛的备考的队伍，这从哪里来呢？好，这作为一种国家力量，创造了一个非常了不起的事件。在古代中国，一个男性他如果要走一条比较好的路，就只能来靠科举。而科举当中，不分地域、不分门庭、不分职业、不分贫富，只要是男性都有资格。在唐代甚至于外国人也能应试，这就变成了一个全民的文化生命力的大动员。几乎所有的男性，不管年龄、不管地域和出身都来参与了，浩浩荡荡，而且时间那么久。这是科举制度了不起的第四个原因。
科举制度第五个了不起的原因呢，就是青年男子往往是一个社会群体当中最动荡的成分。他们在寻找工作，他们靠着自己的生命力在拼搏、在打斗、在竞争，总会引起很多很多的事情产生。但是，科举制度使全中国的青年男子的很大一部分，成为非常用功的备考人员、应试人员，而且很多人屡败屡考，终生应试，这个就大幅度地提高了整个社会的安全系数，而且安全在文化气氛当中。你想，全国所有的青年男子都在应考，这是非常了不得的。把最容易动荡的因素免除了。
这里我插个话。当时很不公平，女性不能考试，所以出现了《女驸马》这样的优秀的作品。其实在生活当中，在真的历史当中，他们出于各种各样的考虑，只能让男性参加。结果我不是在《十万进士》里边写到嘛，很多男性考上了很高的名次以后，去唐代的一些妓院里边玩，妓女突然笑眯眯地问：“什么题目啊？你是怎么来结构文章的？推荐的 提纲怎么样？”考上的考生就非常得意地在宣扬，结果这个妓女笑眯眯地说：“你的第一段和第二段应该改写一下，如果这样就会更好，否则你的思路不顺。”唉呀，听下来以后，考的人是大吃一惊，这个妓女的文化水准大大的高过自己！
但是，很不幸，当时女性不能参加考试。有很多很多这样的有趣的故事，但是这也是科举制度的当时的一个特点。这个特点也意味着他们不是考文采，是考管理人才。而中国国家这么大，管理人才需要全国到处奔波，从这个官到那个官，从那个官做到那个官，所以他们觉得青年男性才比较合适，这是当时的古代朝廷的一个基本思维。
好，今天讲这。
transcriptEn:
Hello everyone, my name is Yu Qiuyu, and today I’m going to talk about a major practical project for the longevity of Chinese culture. This project lasted for more than 1,300 years. It was really a big project, and it was called the imperial examination system. First of all, I want to get rid of a misunderstanding that everyone thinks that the imperial examination system is to select the best poets and essayists. Mistaken, no. The imperial examination system selects managers at all levels, which we generally call civil servants.
No matter what circumstances a society, a country, or a system needs to continue, it needs a vast management team. In some places in the world, civilization finally collapsed. There are various reasons. One reason is that there are not enough managers. Many places are out of control, and many industries are out of control. There are many managers, but they are incompetent or do not have enough prestige, so they are actually out of control. Well, China, like other civilizations, wanted to choose such managers, so the imperial examination system emerged. This is how the imperial examination system came about. Why is it important? I would like to cite a few points to illustrate, that is, the advantages of the imperial examination system.
Preserving cultural soil and unified selection
First, from the perspective of the imperial court, a large country needs many management talents. But from a cultural perspective, that is, from a Chinese cultural perspective, it also requires dense layers of management talents. Does anyone know? When a country becomes broken, the culture often can only be broken as well. Therefore, under this situation, preserving the soil of culture is a very important mission of culture, and the imperial examination system assumed this mission. It not only selected management talents for the imperial court, but also selected the soil for cultural preservation. This is the first point, and I think everyone can understand this meaning.
Second, other major civilizations, at the beginning, formed a good management system because they were led by a generation of heroes and had many capable comrades under him. However, because the area is too large and there are too many directions, it is easy for local managers to form their own pattern. Over time, divisions will occur. However, the imperial examination system is unified across the country, and unified selection is completed with unified standards and unified institutions. This approach blocks the possibility of fragmentation and in turn protects the culture.
Do you understand? If our country is divided into many, many small local governments, it would be easiest for the small local governments to select officials based on their own intentions, their own likes and dislikes, and their own standards. As a result, the country is not unified, and the cadres selected in your locality cannot be used in other places. It's not that it can actually be used or not, but that the other party doesn't recognize it. This is the official elected by your prefect. Your prefect is so far away from us, and he is no longer here. Why should we use your prefect's standards instead of ours? They can all use such a standard, so they go their own way.
But I didn't expect that the imperial examination system used unified standards and institutions to complete unified selection. People who come out of the scientific system can be officials anywhere, because it is unified across the country. This is the second standard of the imperial examination system, and it is also a basis for ensuring the unity of our country, China, and the unity of Chinese culture.
A steady stream of managers
Third, if this kind of selection happened several times or dozens of times, it would already be spectacular. But even so, officials will grow old and die of illness, and there will always be a lack of adequate team reserves. What to do? How can I have so much energy to select officials layer by layer with unified standards?
Unexpectedly, the imperial examination system provided examinations every three years, which provided a large number of management talents and maintained an orderly continuation of Chinese culture. This was an important reason. It is not a whim. The court ordered that we have not selected officials for ten years. We will start the selection this year. The next time we have not selected officials for twenty years, our selection this time will be a whim and cause a trend. No! China's imperial examination system, which takes place every three years, provides a continuous supply of officials to the imperial court. This has also ensured that throughout the long history of ancient China, there has been no shortage of administrators.
The fourth reason is that there is so much demand. To achieve this, we must find a very abundant team of people preparing for the exam across the country. Where does this come from? Well, that created a pretty remarkable event as a national force. In ancient China, if a man wanted to take a better path, he had to take the imperial examination. In the imperial examination, regardless of region, family, occupation, rich or poor, all men are eligible. In the Tang Dynasty, even foreigners could take the exam, which turned into a great mobilization of the cultural vitality of the whole people. Almost all men, regardless of age, region or origin, participated in the event in large numbers and for so long. This is the fourth reason why the imperial examination system is great.
The fifth great reason for the imperial examination system is that young men are often the most volatile component of a social group. They are looking for jobs, and they rely on their own vitality to fight, fight, and compete, which will always cause many, many things to happen. However, the imperial examination system has made a large number of young men in China become very diligent preparers and test takers, and many of them have failed repeatedly and have been taking exams their entire lives. This has greatly improved the safety factor of the entire society, and safety is embedded in the cultural atmosphere. If you think about it, all the young men in the country are taking the exam. This is very remarkable. The most volatile factors are eliminated.
Let me interject here. It was very unfair at that time that women could not take the exam, so excellent works like "The Female Consort" appeared. In fact, in life and in real history, due to various considerations, they can only allow men to participate. As a result, didn’t I write about it in "One Hundred Thousand Jinshi"? After many men passed the exam and went to some brothels in the Tang Dynasty to hang out, the prostitutes suddenly asked with a smile: "What is the topic? How did you structure the article? Recommended How about the outline?" The candidates who passed the exam were very proud to promote it, and the prostitute said with a smile: "You should rewrite the first and second paragraphs, if this will be better, otherwise your thinking will not go smoothly." After hearing this, the candidates were shocked. This prostitute's cultural level is much higher than hers!
But, unfortunately, women were not allowed to take the exam at that time. There are many, many interesting stories like this, but this was also a characteristic of the imperial examination system at that time. This characteristic also means that they are not testing literary talents, but management talents. China is such a big country, and management talents need to travel all over the country, from this official to that official, and from that official to that official, so they think that young men are more suitable. This was a basic thinking of the ancient imperial court at that time.
Okay, let’s talk about this today.

summary.gistZh: 科举制度是古代中国最伟大的制度创新之一，打破了世袭贵族垄断，建立了基于才学而非血统的平民阶层上升通道与文官治理体系。
summary.gistEn: The Imperial Examination (Keju) was one of ancient China's greatest institutional innovations, breaking noble monopolies and establishing merit-based mobility and civil service governance.

highlights.zh: 打破贵族世袭：取消门第限制，让寒门子弟通过读书朝为田舍郎，暮登天子堂。
highlights.en: Breaking Hereditary Aristocracy: Abolishing birthright barriers, enabling commoners to rise to state leadership through rigorous study.

highlights.zh: 科举五大优点：公平竞争、文官政治、全国文化一体化、崇尚知识的风气以及社会流动机制。
highlights.en: Five Meritocratic Advantages: Fair competition, civil governance, national cultural unification, societal reverence for learning, and upward mobility.

highlights.zh: 文官治理范式：领先西方千余年建立专业的常任文官管理体系，保障政府运转稳定。
highlights.en: Civil Governance Paradigm: Establishing a professional meritocratic bureaucracy over a millennium ahead of the West.

highlights.zh: 历史局限与启发：虽后期陷入八股僵化，但其「唯才是举、公平竞争」的核心精神依然是现代文官制度的基石。
highlights.en: Modern Resonance: Though later stifled by rigid formats, its core spirit of meritocracy and fair competition remains the bedrock of modern civil service.

vocabulary.explanationZh: 中国古代通过分科考试选拔文官的根本制度。始于隋唐，延续1300余年，以统一考试取代门阀贵族血缘世袭，是中华文化长寿的重要制度保障。
vocabulary.explanationEn: The nationwide imperial civil service examination system established in the Sui and Tang dynasties and persisting for over 1,300 years. It replaced aristocratic bloodline succession with merit-based selection.

vocabulary.explanationZh: 掌管国家政务、礼乐、民政与司法的行政官员，与武官（执掌军旅征战）相对。科举选拔的核心在于为庞大帝国构建专业且有文化底蕴的常任文官体系。
vocabulary.explanationEn: Civilian administrative officials responsible for governance, civil affairs, and state administration, as distinguished from military officers (武官). The core objective of the exams was cultivating an administrative corps.

vocabulary.explanationZh: 维护完整、使不受破坏。余秋雨先生指出，即使政权更替或国土受创，全国统一的文官知识分子队伍亦能保全中华文化的深厚土壤，使其历经浩劫而不散。
vocabulary.explanationEn: To preserve and keep intact. The lecture underscores that even amid dynastic upheavals, a unified civil bureaucracy protected the social and intellectual soil of Chinese civilization.

vocabulary.en: Formidable / Heroic Monarch of an Era
vocabulary.explanationZh: 具有宏大魄力与雄才大略的杰出君主。早期文明往往依赖雄主的个人魅力聚合战友，但若缺乏制度化体系，雄主离世后帝国极易瓦解。
vocabulary.explanationEn: A visionary, powerful monarch with exceptional leadership. Early civilizations often relied on heroic rulers, but without institutionalized succession, empires fractured upon the monarch's demise.

vocabulary.explanationZh: 地方官员在各自领地内形成封闭、自主的小天地或割据势力。古代版图辽阔，若无中央统一选拔流转机制，各地管理者便会自成格局并最终导致分裂。
vocabulary.explanationEn: Developing isolated regional power bases or autonomous fiefdoms. Given China's vast geography, regional administrators naturally drifted into localized fiefdoms without a standardized civil service.

vocabulary.explanationZh: 古代郡级行政区的最高军政长官。若各郡太守依个人好恶私自任免官吏，所选官员便无法跨区域任职，导致各地政令阻隔、互不承认。
vocabulary.explanationEn: The chief administrative governor of a commandery (prefecture) in ancient China. If each prefect appointed local protégés at will, governance standards would collapse across jurisdictions.

vocabulary.en: Each Pursuing Their Own Course / Fragmented Rule
vocabulary.explanationZh: 成语。各自按照自己的意愿和主张行事，缺乏统一部署。科举以全国统一的标准、统一的机构，彻底消除了地方官僚各自为政、互不认可的隐患。
vocabulary.explanationEn: Idiom: each ruling according to their own agenda without central coordination. The unified examination dismantled this regional parochialism by establishing nationwide equivalence of credentials.

vocabulary.explanationZh: 形容层次丰富繁密。指古代从中央部院到道、府、州、县绵密分布的多层级行政管理结构，需要大量合格人才常年充实其中。
vocabulary.explanationEn: Layer upon layer; referring to the multi-tiered administrative hierarchy stretching from imperial ministries down to prefectures and counties across a vast subcontinent.

vocabulary.explanationZh: 成语。形容接连不断地涌来。科举制度固定每三年举行一次大考，为朝廷稳定输送取之不竭、品学兼优的年轻文官队伍。
vocabulary.explanationEn: Idiom: a constant, unceasing stream. The triennial examination cycle guaranteed a regular, renewable replenishment of qualified scholar-bureaucrats across dynasties.

vocabulary.en: On a Sudden Whim / Impulsive Caprice
vocabulary.explanationZh: 成语。指一时冲动、毫无定规的举措。科举制度的严格周期性杜绝了君主凭心血来潮隔十几年才临时选官的弊端，使国家管理具有可预期的稳定性。
vocabulary.explanationEn: Idiom: acting on a capricious impulse. The institutional rhythm of scheduled exams prevented imperial regimes from capriciously suspending or improvising official recruitment.

vocabulary.explanationZh: 指家族门第与阀阅出身。魏晋南北朝时期仕途全凭家世门第垄断；科举制度打破门庭藩篱，不分贵贱贫富，唯才华与试卷定高下。
vocabulary.explanationEn: Ancestral lineage, clan pedigree, or aristocratic pedigree. The exam bypassed aristocratic gatekeeping, democratizing bureaucratic entry for ordinary commoners.

vocabulary.explanationZh: 发动调动全体社会成员的积极性。科举促成了全社会文化生命力的大动员，使全国各阶层男性终生向学，铸就了中华文明尊师重教的深厚传统。
vocabulary.explanationEn: Mobilization; rousing and activating the intellectual energies and social aspirations of the entire populace toward learning and statecraft.

vocabulary.en: Persistently Re-Sitting Exams Despite Repeated Failures
vocabulary.explanationZh: 哪怕屡试不中依然矢志不渝、继续备考。科举为士人提供了终生的合法希望，将社会精英的不满与能量导向学术钻研而非破坏性暴动。
vocabulary.explanationEn: Persistently re-taking the exams despite repeated failures. It provided a permanent legitimate avenue for ambition, transforming potential social rebellion into constructive scholarly discipline.

vocabulary.explanationZh: 维护社会安定秩序的保障程度。年轻男性最具躁动与叛逆倾向，科举成功将他们的大半精力引导在书卷文墨与考场竞争中，显著提升了社会稳定。
vocabulary.explanationEn: Societal safety margin. By channeling restless, energetic young men into scholarly pursuit and civil service ambitions, the system neutralized destructive unrest in a cultural atmosphere.

vocabulary.explanationZh: 科举殿试录取的最高等第，亦为古代知识分子的至高荣誉。余秋雨先生在著名文化散文《十万进士》中深入剖析了这一群体对中国历史与文化的深刻塑造。
vocabulary.explanationEn: The highest degree awarded in the imperial civil examination system. Yu Qiuyu explored this elite intellectual group extensively in his acclaimed cultural essay 'A Hundred Thousand Jinshi'.

vocabulary.explanationZh: 著名传统戏剧。讲述才女冯素珍为解救蒙冤未婚夫，女扮男装赴京考中状元并被选为驸马的奇闻。此剧折射出古代女性才识虽不让须眉，却被阻挡在科举门外的历史遗憾。
vocabulary.explanationEn: A celebrated classic Chinese opera recounting how Feng Suzhen disguised herself as a man, topped the imperial exam, and was betrothed as the imperial son-in-law, reflecting women's exclusion from the exams.

vocabulary.explanationZh: 文章的论点脉络与框架架构。科考策论极其讲究起承转合与破题提纲，展现应试者剖析国家治理问题时的周密逻辑与行政思路。
vocabulary.explanationEn: The thematic outline and structural blueprint of an essay, essential in imperial examinations for demonstrating logical rigor and administrative insight.

vocabulary.explanationZh: 文字的辞藻与文学修辞。余秋雨先生强调，科举选拔的终极落脚点并非纯粹的诗赋文采，而是具备全局眼光、务实操盘能力的治国管理人才。
vocabulary.explanationEn: Ornate poetic talent and literary rhetoric. The author underscores that the primary goal of the exam was practical administrative competence rather than pure poetry.

title: 君子之交：友谊是人生的一大难题
folderName: 11_君子之交：友谊是人生的一大难题
audioPath: 11_君子之交：友谊是人生的一大难题/audio.m4a
quoteCardPath: 11_君子之交：友谊是人生的一大难题/quote_card.jpg
transcriptZh:
大家好，我是余秋雨。
我们接着上一次讲君子之道，上次已经讲完了君子之道的九项要点，从今天开始要讲四项难点。因为我们的课程学术浓度比较高，所以我还需要来回顾性地解释一下一个整体结构，我们在讲中国文化的时候，用的是文化人类学的一个基本观点，一切文化的最后成果是人格，特别是集体人格。
君子之道的四个难点
我的课程在不断进行，进行到一定的时候，我就要讲中国文化的人格结构。当然，儒家、佛家和道家，人格结构是不一样的。儒家的人格结构的理想是君子，所以我们现在正在讲儒家的人格结构叫君子之道。我们整天在讲君子之道，讲君子之道什么呢？我概括了九项要点，温习一下：一个就是君子怀德，第二个要点是君子之德风，第三个要点是君子成人之美，第四要点是君子周而不比，第五个要点是君子坦荡荡，第六个要点是君子中庸，第七个要点是君子有礼，第八个要点是君子不器，第九要点是君子知耻。这九个要点大家都应该是听得很清楚了，我每个要点都讲的比较完整。
除了这九个要点之外，君子之道还有四个难点。这个难点我们在生活当中经常会实实在在遇到，这是这个要点之外值得我们仔细讨论的问题。这四个难点，一个叫君子之交，他怎么交朋友，怎么建立友情。第二个是君子之名，他怎么面对自己的名声和名誉。第三个是君子之伪，伪就是伪造的伪，虚假的，我们一般讲伪君子，这怎么回事。第四个叫君子之难，君子也会遇到很大的困难，有的时候甚至于遇到牢狱之灾，君子会怎么来对付。这四个难点我们今天开始一点一点地讲，讲完这些以后，我还要专门论述君子之道的反面论证——小人的天地，这个讲完以后，我们把君子之道就完成了。
请大家注意，就是三个结构：第一个是九项要点，第二个是四项难点，第三个是反面论证，也就是小人的天地。
君子之交
我们现在讲四项难点的第一点，叫君子之交。我们都知道，中国古代有句非常著名的话叫君子之交淡如水，这是中国文化对我们的一个非常重要的教导；但这话在生活当中好像不太有用，我们总是希望君子之交很浓，那么这怎么回事？对这个问题我们要从头讲，在君子之道里边，人际交往、友情的处理，是一个非常大的问题，而这一点恰恰是中国文化的一个非常重要的特征。作为中国文化的核心的儒家文化，它特别讲究人际关系。
我曾经在论述我们古代文化的时候，在2000多年以前，当巴比伦文化在关注天文学和数学的时候，当印度文化在探究人与梵天之间关系的时候，当希腊文化在询问人和自然之间的关系的时候，中国的智者最大的兴趣点一直是人与人的关系，以及如何来管理这种关系，这是儒家文化的主干。
请大家注意了，直到今天为止，我们在讲中国的文化的特点的时候，我们有的时候从反面的角度来看，特别讲究人际关系。但是我们最好不要给他以明确的反面的评价，因为这是我们文化的根基。当希腊的哲学家站在海边，看着人家的帆船，一艘艘出航，它到底能够有几艘能够回来，在思考的人和自然的关系的时候；当巴比伦的智者们抬起头来研究天文学的时候；当印度的那些宗教领袖们始终在思考着超乎人类经验的神秘力量的时候；中国古代的智者从海边回过眼神来，从天上回过眼神来，只注意自己的人和人之间的关系。你很难说，这是过于庸俗了，也很难说这过于低下了，这一点不低下。我们的诸子百家，各种各样问题都研究，但是他们对客观世界的自然东西兴趣不是很大，对天上的神秘力量的兴趣也不是很大。他们的兴趣在社会，在人际。
这是到现在为止，我们走来走去都感觉到中国文化这个特点，是其他文化还没法比的。我曾经有一段时间去考察世界各文化文明的遗址，快考察完的时候，我曾经对我的小伙伴们提出一个疑问，我说我们一起走了那么多国家，你们觉得他们共同和中华文化不同的一个特点是什么？他们每种文化都不一样，他们互相之间差别很大，他们总有一种文化和中国文化相比，他们有一个共同的一个特点是什么？没想到我的小伙伴们都共同作出回答，我们觉得他们的人际关系比中国人简单，不管他们现在陷于什么境地，都比中国人简单。所以这一点好像对我们来说稍稍有点负面，人际关系既让我们温暖，又让我们感到沉重，既让我们觉得理不清，又让我们觉得遇到困难的时候，能够抬起头来找到能够帮助我们的人等等等等。
人际关系确实是中国文化的一个特点，所以在这一点上我们有没有可能系统地梳理一下。作为中国人的优秀的成分，君子他如何来处理人际关系，特别是如何来处理友情。请大家注意，你如果是个管理者，那么就要管理人际关系，但是你不是个管理者的话，实际上所谓人际关系也就是处理友情。如何来处理友谊，我们有很多很多的各种各样的交往，在交往当中我们该怎么处理，这是个大问题，这也是中国文化给予我们的很多正面和反面的一种滋养。反面也能成为一种滋养，正面也能成为一种滋养，我们身上就是这种正面和反面对我们滋养的结果，我们要把它清理一下。几千年来特别注意人际关系的中国人，因友谊而快乐，因友谊而安适，又因友谊而痛苦，又因友谊而悔恨。天下各种各样的小人伎俩，几乎都会利用友谊；世界大量的犯罪记录，往往都是从错交朋友开始，因此友谊实在是君子人生的一大难题。
为了把这个问题讲清楚，我先从友谊的等级来说起。这个等级当中第一等级叫至谊，最高的友谊，至高无上的至，至谊。如果用我们君子之交的说法，君子之交里边也有一种是神交，高于我们一般的常交，我们一般的交往叫常交，它是神交。有这样的一种交往，不一定遇得到，但是却是我们对人际关系的一种最高的期盼。
这个我不能不从我小时候的阅读经验说起，我小的时候就像我们同龄的人一样，老在小人书摊里边看连环画。看连环画的时候，有一次不小心看到一本书，一本连环画，看到一个故事，把我真是深深地震撼了。我当时还很小很小，这个小人书里边讲，有一个地位很高的人，独自在江边弹琴，却被一个打柴的樵夫完全听懂了，他们就很快成了朋友。一年以后这个弹琴的高官再到那个地方，寻找这个打柴的樵夫，却听说樵夫已经死亡，他非常悲痛地找到了山间的那个坟墓，把自己的这张琴摔碎在墓碑上。
我很小的时候看到这个故事非常震撼，我记得那天我在小人书摊里边，当所有的人走完，当小人书的老板敲着我的肩说，我收摊了，我才醒过神来。我被这个故事所震撼了，后来我年纪慢慢长大了，我就读到了这个故事，这个故事就是我所说的最高的友情叫“至谊”的一个典范。
我相信我们听众已经知道我在讲哪个故事了，那么我们下次再讲。谢谢！
transcriptEn:
Hello everyone, my name is Yu Qiuyu.
We will continue to talk about the way of a gentleman from the last time. We have finished the nine key points of the way of a gentleman last time. From today on, we will talk about four difficult points. Because the academic concentration of our courses is relatively high, I also need to retrospectively explain the overall structure. When we talk about Chinese culture, we use a basic perspective of cultural anthropology. The final outcome of all cultures is personality, especially collective personality.
Four Difficulties in the Way of a Gentleman
My course is continuing, and when it reaches a certain point, I will talk about the personality structure of Chinese culture. Of course, Confucianism, Buddhism and Taoism have different personality structures. The ideal of Confucian personality structure is the gentleman, so we are now talking about the Confucian personality structure called the way of the gentleman. We talk about the way of a gentleman all day long, but what is the way of a gentleman? I have summarized nine key points to review: the first point is that a gentleman is virtuous, the second point is the virtue of a gentleman, the third point is the beauty of a gentleman, the fourth point is that a gentleman is uncompromising, the fifth point is that a gentleman is magnanimous, the sixth point is that a gentleman is moderate, the seventh point is that a gentleman is polite, the eighth point is that a gentleman is disrespectful, and the ninth point is that a gentleman knows his shame. Everyone should have heard these nine points clearly. I have explained each point in a relatively complete manner.
In addition to these nine points, there are four difficulties in the way of a gentleman. We often encounter this difficulty in real life. This is an issue worthy of careful discussion in addition to this point. Of these four difficulties, one is called friendship between gentlemen, how to make friends and how to establish friendship. The second is the reputation of a gentleman, how he faces his own reputation and reputation. The third is the hypocrisy of a gentleman. Hypocrisy means forgery, hypocrisy. We generally talk about hypocrites. What's going on? The fourth is the difficulty of a gentleman. A gentleman will also encounter great difficulties, and sometimes even face imprisonment. How will a gentleman deal with them? We will start to talk about these four difficulties bit by bit today. After talking about these, I will also discuss the negative argument of the gentleman's way - the world of villains. After this, we will complete the gentleman's way.
Please note that there are three structures: the first is the nine key points, the second is the four difficulties, and the third is the negative argument, which is the world of the villain.
friendship between gentlemen
Let us now talk about the first of the four difficulties, which is called friendship between gentlemen. We all know that there is a very famous saying in ancient China: The friendship between gentlemen is as light as water. This is a very important teaching of Chinese culture to us. But this saying does not seem to be very useful in life. We always hope that the friendship between gentlemen is as strong as water. So what is going on? Let’s talk about this issue from the beginning. In the gentleman’s way, the handling of interpersonal communication and friendship is a very big issue, and this is precisely a very important feature of Chinese culture. As the core of Chinese culture, Confucian culture pays special attention to interpersonal relationships.
When I was discussing our ancient culture, more than 2,000 years ago, when the Babylonian culture was paying attention to astronomy and mathematics, when the Indian culture was exploring the relationship between man and Brahma, and when the Greek culture was asking about the relationship between man and nature, the biggest interest of Chinese wise men has always been the relationship between people and how to manage this relationship. This is the backbone of Confucian culture.
Please note that until today, when we talk about the characteristics of Chinese culture, we sometimes look at it from a negative perspective, paying special attention to interpersonal relationships. But we'd better not give him a clear negative evaluation, because this is the foundation of our culture. When the Greek philosophers stood on the seaside, watching other people's sailing ships sailing one by one, how many of them could come back, and thinking about the relationship between man and nature; when the wise men in Babylon raised their heads to study astronomy; when the religious leaders in India were always thinking about the mysterious power beyond human experience; the wise men in ancient China looked back from the seaside, and looked back from the sky, only paying attention to the relationship between their own people. It's hard to say that this is too vulgar, and it's also hard to say that this is too low-level, but it's not low-level at all. Our various schools of thought study various issues, but they are not very interested in the natural things in the objective world, nor are they very interested in the mysterious power in the sky. Their interest is in society and interpersonal relationships.
Until now, we can feel this characteristic of Chinese culture when walking around, which is unmatched by other cultures. I once visited the ruins of various cultures and civilizations around the world for a period of time. When I was about to finish the inspection, I once asked my friends a question. I said that we have traveled to so many countries together. What do you think they have in common and are different from Chinese culture? Each of their cultures is different. They are very different from each other. They always have a culture. Compared with Chinese culture, what is the one characteristic they have in common? Unexpectedly, my friends all responded together. We think their interpersonal relationships are simpler than the Chinese. No matter what situation they are in now, it is simpler than the Chinese. So this seems to be a little negative for us. Interpersonal relationships make us feel warm and heavy at the same time. It makes us feel confused and makes us feel that when we encounter difficulties, we can raise our heads and find people who can help us, etc.
Interpersonal relationships are indeed a characteristic of Chinese culture, so is it possible for us to systematically sort out this aspect? As an outstanding element of Chinese people, a gentleman is how he handles interpersonal relationships, especially how he handles friendships. Please note that if you are a manager, then you have to manage interpersonal relationships, but if you are not a manager, in fact, the so-called interpersonal relationships are to deal with friendships. How to deal with friendships? We have many, many, various interactions. How should we deal with them during interactions? This is a big problem. This is also a kind of nourishment that Chinese culture has given us, both positive and negative. The negative side can also be a kind of nourishment, and the positive side can also be a kind of nourishment. We are the result of the positive side and the negative side nourishing us, and we need to clean it up. Chinese people, who have paid special attention to interpersonal relationships for thousands of years, are happy because of friendship, comfortable because of friendship, painful because of friendship, and regretful because of friendship. Almost all villains in the world use friendship for their tricks; a large number of criminal records in the world often start from making the wrong friends, so friendship is really a big problem in a gentleman's life.
In order to make this issue clear, let me start with the levels of friendship. The first level among this level is called Zhiyi, the highest friendship, the supreme Zhiyi, Zhiyi. If we use the term "gentlemen's friendship", there is also a kind of "spiritual friendship" among gentlemen's friendship, which is higher than our ordinary regular friendship. Our ordinary friendship is called "normal friendship", and it is "spiritual friendship". Having such a kind of interaction may not be possible, but it is our highest expectation for interpersonal relationships.
I have to start with my reading experience as a child. When I was young, just like people of our age, I always read comic books at the Little Man Bookshelf. When I was reading comic books, I accidentally came across a book, a comic book, and a story that really shocked me. I was still very young at the time. The book tells about a man of high status who was playing the piano alone by the river, but was completely understood by a woodcutter who was collecting firewood, and they quickly became friends. A year later, the senior official who played the piano returned to that place, looking for the woodcutter, but he heard that the woodcutter had died. He was very sad and found the tomb in the mountain, and smashed his piano on the tombstone.
I was very shocked when I saw this story when I was very young. I remember that day I was in the Little Man Books stall. When all the people had left, and the owner of the Little Man Books knocked on my shoulder and said, I closed the stall, I came to my senses. I was shocked by this story. Later, when I grew up, I read this story. This story is an example of what I call the highest friendship called "perfect friendship".
I believe that we listeners already know which story I am telling, so we will tell it next time. Thanks!

summary.gistZh: 「君子之交淡如水」体现了中国文化中关于友谊的最高智慧，强调情感的纯粹、人格的独立与长久的相互尊重，拒绝利益交换。
summary.gistEn: 'Friendship between gentlemen is as pure as water' reflects Chinese culture's highest wisdom on friendship, emphasizing emotional purity, personal independence, and mutual respect over transactional gain.

highlights.zh: 淡如水 vs 甘若醴：小人之交甘若醴（因利而聚、因利而散）；君子之交淡如水（不依附、不强求、久而弥香）。
highlights.en: Pure Water vs. Sweet Wine: Shallow friendship is sweet like wine for profit; noble friendship is pure as water—unattached, enduring, and respectful.

highlights.zh: 友谊是人生难题：人际关系最易毁于过于亲密导致的界限丧失与功利索取。
highlights.en: Friendship as a Life Challenge: Human relationships crumble easily when boundaries blur into needy utility or over-entanglement.

highlights.zh: 保持独立与尊严：真正的朋友相互理解独立的人格，无需频繁客套或利益捆绑。
highlights.en: Preserving Independence & Dignity: True friends honor each other's distinct individuality without requiring empty formalities or transactional ties.

highlights.zh: 知音难觅的精神寄托：从伯牙子期到竹林七贤，中国文化将友谊提升为灵魂深处的精神共鸣。
highlights.en: Spiritual Resonance of Soulmates: From Boya and Ziqi to the Seven Sages, Chinese culture elevates friendship into deep spiritual alignment.

title: 说真话：不用虚假替代真实
folderName: 12_说真话：不用虚假替代真实
