transcriptZh:
大家好，我是余秋雨，我们继续昨天的课程。
我上次讲到数字化的失控，是中国一个非常大的盲区，这个盲区就是实证思维的失落。对于这个问题，任何研究中国古代文化的人都会感觉到，特别是对中国古代的科技做出了非常高评价的著名汉学家李约瑟博士，他也发现了这个问题。他说，为什么中国那么的不在乎实证，那么的不在乎数字的准确性？他认为这和我们社会长期的官僚主义是有关的，它冲淡了实证主义。官僚主义怎么会冲淡实证主义呢？李约瑟讲了四个理由，我们可以听听。
伪证和证伪
李约瑟说，把褒贬放到了真实之上，不追求事实真相，只追求千古定论。所谓的千古定论，就是把天下之士分成忠和奸，正和邪，功和过，是和非，但是不在乎真和伪。在中国文化当中，是非之辨总是远远地超过真伪之辨，而且事情的真实没搞清楚，议论就很多了。我们现在在媒体里面也经常可以看到，事情到底怎么样不管，就是发表议论的人特别多。
李约瑟说，除了把褒贬放到了真实之上，第二点就是中国古代文化把仪式放到了真实之上；第三点是把理想放到了真实之上；第四点对制度之外的真实完全予以否定。李约瑟讲了这四点以后，他说真实就像被一次次漂洗过的水墨画一样，越来越淡，这个事情对中国来说就变成一个非常大的问题了。我们后来渐渐地很难提倡科学的发展、新的各种科技的进步，就和这个有关。
由于我们那么地否定实证，我们那么地轻视实证，我们又是那么地在乎随口讲的数字，所以中华文化就遇到了一个非常大的问题，叫伪证。大量的伪证出来以后，我们无法证明它是伪的。所以，这里边有一个字的颠倒，一个叫伪证，一个叫证伪，也就是要证明它是假的。证伪的能力非常重要，我们中国文化缺少这个能力。
大家想想看，不管你是什么身份，也不管你多大年龄，你如果遇到一个谣言，你只能大声地喊这是谣言，你找不到证伪的程序。即使找到了，别人也没兴趣，大家不愿意听一个证伪的过程和程序。所以好多人因为谣言而自杀，因为他找不到这个程序，这是中国文化的一个弊病，就是没法实证。大量的伪证出现以后，我们无法证明它是伪，所以就没有能力证伪。记住，伪证是不好的，证伪是好的，证伪是一种能力，但是我们缺少这个能力。
中国改革开放以后，在我们的经济数据上这个问题已经大体解决，这是很乐观了。但是我们从文化的意义上说，这个问题其实远远没有解决，因为多少年来的一个文化盲区，怎么可能在经济发展的过程当中完全解决呢？经济发展可以解决一部分，但是完全解决还不太可能。我们现在看我们的经济指标的那些数字都是可信的，但是在社会上为什么还有那么多智商不低的人相信谣言？而这个谣言不管压到什么等级的人头上，这些人都没有应对的策略？这个问题肯定不是数字化的经济数字能够解决的了，所以这问题在文化上我们还是要多思考一下。
诚实和事实
譬如，脑子再好的人，如果遇到一个社会信息的时候，我们想的首先是这个信息能不能符合我的内心期待；第二想的是这个信息它的刺激程度如何；第三想的是这个信息来源在哪里。但是，如果问到这个信息的真实与否，我们好像在这方面也比较迟钝，也比较不太在乎，我们很快就成了一个不知道真和假的信息的传递者。
这就像我们小时候做的一个游戏，击鼓传花的游戏，鼓声在响，我们把花传下去，传的时候对这个谣言可能会有几点疑问，但很快就自我解套了，因为信息从前面传过来的，我没有核实，前面的人已经核实过，那么我很快就会传给别人，别人很可能会去核实。结果，从头到底没有一个人去核实过，前面的人没核实过，后面的人没核实过，我不去核实，前面的人、后面的人都像我一样。造成的结果，就是谣言完全地把他控制了。如果有人对谣言持怀疑态度的话，那就成为这个传花游戏当中动作比较慢的人了，反而成为游戏当中败兴的人、扫兴的人，会淘汰出局。
所以在我们的文化当中，只要对在疯传的谣言产生一些疑虑的人，反而会被大家另眼看待，淘汰出局，成为一个边缘人物，这就是我们的文化造成的一个不好的结果。这里面就带来了我们文化当中很大的弊病了，就是由于没法实证，我们就靠找来的一些证人，因为是唯一的真实性的靠山。我因为经历过太多太多的事情，我可以证明这一点，就是生活当中有好多最诚实的人的记忆，也可能和事实不符。最诚实的人的记忆，也可能和事实不符。
我们五六个好朋友出去郊游，一个月以后，大家回忆的可能都不一样。有时候我发现一个非常有趣的情景，由于重点不一样，有的人记忆也会发生变化。比如我曾经讲过，就是学校里边一个职工，他在任何情况下都可以揭发被打倒的人，比如这个副校长被打倒了，他会讲很多很多这个校长身上非常坏的东西。这个系主任被打倒了，他只是个职工，也会讲很多很多这个系主任该被打倒的坏事情。后来，这个副校长又成领导了，这个人又可以想出很多很多这个副校长正面的东西。这个系主任又做了系主任，他又可以想出好多系主任身上正面的东西。这是投机分子吗？不是。
我见过很多这样的人，他其实社会地位很低，也是很诚实的人。人的心理结构经常会受到社会思潮的左右，在社会思潮的左右里边，他的每一个回忆都是真实的，他回忆这个副校长的好的地方是真实的，不好的地方也是真实的，只不过他根据思潮重组了。重组了以后，他所讲出来东西很可能成为打倒这个副校长的很重要的理由，也可以是让那个副校长非常痛苦的理由，但是这个揭发者不是坏人。
所以，在一个没有数字化控制的情况下，你即使找到这样的证人，我们把他作为真实的根据的话，问题也是非常严重了。更不要说，我们生活当中好多历史的良心是藏在小巷子的深处，他不愿意发言。也很可能，有的凶手为了掩盖自己，他成了喊声最高的人，甚至于成了假法官。这样的情况很多很多，所以就产生了我们一次次的灾难。
呼唤说真话
在生活当中，遇到未被实证证明的虚假信号太多太多。我记得有一次，经常来往于海峡两岸的佛教大师星云大师，他在接受一个私人采访的时候，问他目前中国遇到最大的问题是什么？星云大师对中国大陆是非常友好的，他想了一想说，我觉得是假，而且是假在文化上。他不是讲其它的假，他不是说经济数字假，也不是说政治上假，他认为是假在文化上。对于这个话，平心而论，你听一听会出汗。
你仔细想一想，我们不说星云大师，就说我们的一个前辈巴金，我们都非常尊重的巴金老人。他后半辈子呼吁的最响亮、最重复的话，叫“说真话”。他反复地要文化界说真话，他自己一生最后的遗嘱也是这三个字，叫“说真话”。这两个老人，星云大师和巴金老人，他们一辈子对于真的呼唤值得我们很好的思考了。大的灾难不说，就在小的事情上。我们也是被好多虚假东西套住了。
大家可能都还记得，我曾经在中央电视台做过连续八期大奖赛的总评委。在这个比赛过程当中，有一个环节是我们自己设计的，叫做“命题对话”。命题对话就是由我出题目，让那个人来答。我们要看他的综合素质，你不能光唱歌，你不能光搞乐器，你一定要用你的语言来回答我给你出的题目。
很遗憾的是，这些很优秀的当代青年，他们面对我们的题目，他们的回答永远是用朗诵腔、抒情调说套话、大话、空话、假话，多数都是如此。我想既然是中央电视台的一个大平台，所以我一定要用强有力的语言来阻止他们这么做。比如，我们题目要他们讲讲你的老师或者讲讲你的母亲、讲讲你的童年。这些选手他们是听不到其他选手回答问题的，他们是彼此隔离的，但是全国观众很惊讶地发现，他们的老师、他们的母亲、他们的童年是一样的，形象一样、痛苦一样、思念一样，他们全部的用语是一样，这显然是假的，因为他们用了一个标准去套老师、套妈妈、套童年，这就成了一个大问题了。
所以，我说你们用了虚假的方式让你的母亲、老师和你的童年都虚假了，这是我不可容忍的。这是虚假在我们可爱的仪式上、在可爱的年轻人身上，所体现的现象。还有，有的电视台经常会做这个城市和那个城市的魅力比较，各个城市有的时候市长、副市长出来，他讲自己城市魅力的时候，除了有一些主要项目之外，用语也基本一样。所以在这个问题上呢，我们显然就进入到了一个以套话、大话、空话、假话，来替代真实性的这么一个魔窟当中了。
好，今天讲到这，下次我们再见面。
transcriptEn:
Hello everyone, my name is Yu Qiuyu. Let’s continue yesterday’s lesson.
Last time I talked about the loss of control of digitalization, which is a very big blind spot in China. This blind spot is the loss of empirical thinking. Anyone who studies ancient Chinese culture will feel this problem, especially the famous sinologist Dr. Joseph Needham, who has made a very high evaluation of ancient Chinese science and technology. He also discovered this problem. He said, why does China care so little about empirical evidence and the accuracy of figures? He believes this is related to the long-term bureaucracy in our society, which dilutes positivism. How could bureaucracy dilute positivism? Joseph Needham gave four reasons that we can listen to.
Perjury and falsification
Joseph Needham said that he puts praise and blame above the truth and does not pursue the truth, but only pursues eternal conclusions. The so-called eternal conclusion is to divide the people of the world into loyal and traitorous, righteous and evil, merit and demerit, right and wrong, but it does not care about the truth and falsehood. In Chinese culture, the distinction between right and wrong always far outweighs the distinction between truth and falsehood, and before the truth of the matter is clear, there will be a lot of discussion. We can often see in the media now that no matter how things are, there are just a lot of people talking about them.
Joseph Needham said that in addition to putting praise and blame before reality, the second point is that ancient Chinese culture puts ritual before reality; the third point is that it puts ideals before reality; and the fourth point is that it completely denies the reality outside the system. After Joseph Needham talked about these four points, he said that reality is like an ink painting that has been washed over and over again, getting lighter and lighter. This matter has become a very big problem for China. Later, it became difficult for us to advocate the development of science and the advancement of various new technologies, and this is related to it.
Because we deny empirical evidence so much, we despise empirical evidence so much, and we care so much about casual numbers, Chinese culture has encountered a very big problem called perjury. After a large amount of perjury comes out, we cannot prove that it is false. Therefore, there is a reversal of the words here, one is called perjury, and the other is called falsification, which means to prove that it is false. The ability to falsify is very important, and our Chinese culture lacks this ability.
Think about it, no matter what your identity is or how old you are, if you encounter a rumor, you can only shout loudly that it is a rumor, and there is no procedure to falsify it. Even if it is found, others are not interested, and no one is willing to listen to the process and procedures of falsification. So many people commit suicide because of rumors because they can't find this program. This is a shortcoming of Chinese culture, that is, it cannot be verified. After a large amount of perjury appears, we cannot prove that it is false, so we have no ability to falsify it. Remember, perjury is bad, falsification is good, falsification is an ability, but we lack this ability.
After China's reform and opening up, this problem has been largely solved in our economic data, which is very optimistic. But from a cultural perspective, this problem is far from being solved, because how can a cultural blind spot that has existed for many years be completely solved in the process of economic development? Economic development can solve part of the problem, but it is unlikely to solve it completely. The numbers we see in our economic indicators are all credible, but why do so many people in society with high IQs believe in rumors? And no matter what level of people this rumor falls on, these people don't have a strategy to deal with it? This problem certainly cannot be solved by digital economic figures, so we still need to think more about this problem culturally.
Honesty and facts
For example, no matter how smart a person is, when we encounter a piece of social information, the first thing we think about is whether the information can meet our inner expectations; the second thing we think about is how stimulating the information is; and the third thing we think about is where the source of the information is. However, if asked whether the information is true or not, we seem to be relatively slow in this regard and care less. We quickly become a transmitter of information that does not know whether it is true or false.
This is like a game we played when we were kids, the flower-passing game. The drums are beating and we pass the flowers on. When we pass the flowers, we may have some doubts about the rumor, but we will soon get rid of it. Because the information came from the front, I did not verify it, and the people in front have verified it. Then I will soon pass it on to others, and others will probably verify it. As a result, no one has verified it from the beginning to the end. The people in front of me have not verified it, and the people behind me have not verified it. If I don’t verify it, the people in front of me and the people behind me are just like me. The result was that the rumors completely controlled him. If someone is skeptical about the rumors, they will become a slow person in this flower-passing game. Instead, they will become a loser and a spoiler in the game, and they will be eliminated from the game.
Therefore, in our culture, as long as people have some doubts about the rumors that are spreading wildly, they will be looked at in a different light, eliminated, and become a marginalized figure. This is a bad result of our culture. This has brought about a big shortcoming in our culture, that is, because there is no way to prove it, we rely on some witnesses we found, because they are the only backers of authenticity. I have experienced too many things, and I can attest to this. Even the memories of many of the most honest people in life may not be consistent with the facts. Even the most honest person's memory may not match the facts.
Five or six of us good friends went out for an outing. A month later, everyone may have different memories of the trip. Sometimes I find a very interesting scene. Because the focus is different, some people's memories will also change. For example, I once said that an employee in the school can expose the person who has been knocked down under any circumstances. For example, if the vice principal is knocked down, he will say many, many very bad things about the principal. The head of the department was knocked down. He was just an employee, and he would say many, many bad things that deserved to be knocked down. Later, the vice-principal became a leader again, and this person could come up with many, many positive things about the vice-principal. This department head has become the department head again, and he can think of many positive things about the department head. Is this an opportunist? no.
I have met many such people, who actually have a very low social status and are also very honest people. People's psychological structure is often influenced by social trends of thought. Within the influence of social trends of thought, every memory he has is true. The good things he recalls about the vice-principal are true, and the bad parts are also true, but he has reorganized them according to the trends of thought. After the reorganization, what he said may become a very important reason to overthrow the vice-principal, and it may also be a reason to make the vice-principal very painful, but this whistleblower is not a bad person.
Therefore, in a situation without digital control, even if you find such a witness and we use him as a true basis, the problem will be very serious. Not to mention, many historical consciences in our lives are hidden deep in alleys, and they are unwilling to speak. It is also very possible that in order to cover themselves up, some murderers become the loudest person or even become a fake judge. There are many such situations, so we have disasters again and again.
Call to tell the truth
In life, we encounter too many false signals that have not been empirically proven. I remember one time when Master Hsing Yun, a Buddhist master who often travels between the two sides of the Taiwan Strait, gave a private interview and asked him what was the biggest problem facing China at present. Master Hsing Yun is very friendly to mainland China. He thought about it and said, I think it is fake, and it is fake in terms of culture. He is not talking about other falsehoods, he is not saying that economic figures are false, nor is he false about politics. He thinks it is false about culture. To be honest, you will sweat after hearing this.
If you think about it carefully, we don’t talk about Master Xingyun, but we talk about one of our seniors, Ba Jin, whom we all respect very much. The loudest and most repeated call for him in the rest of his life was "tell the truth." He repeatedly asked the cultural community to tell the truth. His last testament in life was also these three words, called "tell the truth." These two old men, Master Xingyun and Old Man Ba ​​Jin, their lifelong calling for truth deserves our careful consideration. Not to mention big disasters, it’s all about small things. We have also been trapped by a lot of false things.
You may still remember that I once served as the chief judge of eight consecutive Grand Prix contests on CCTV. In the process of this competition, there is a link that we designed ourselves, called "Proposition Dialogue". In propositional dialogue, I ask the question and let the other person answer it. We need to look at his overall quality. You can't just sing, you can't just play musical instruments. You must use your language to answer the questions I give you.
It is a pity that when these outstanding contemporary young people face our questions, their answers are always recitative and lyrical, using clichés, big words, empty words, and lies. Most of them are like this. I think since it is a big platform of CCTV, I must use strong language to stop them from doing this. For example, our questions ask them to talk about your teacher or your mother or your childhood. These contestants cannot hear other contestants answer questions. They are isolated from each other, but the national audience is surprised to find that their teachers, their mothers, and their childhoods are the same. They have the same image, the same pain, the same longing, and all their terms are the same. This is obviously false, because they use one standard to apply to their teachers, mothers, and childhoods. This has become a big problem.
Therefore, I say that you have used false methods to make your mother, teachers, and your childhood false. This is something I cannot tolerate. This is the phenomenon of falsehood manifested in our lovely rituals and in our lovely young people. Also, some TV stations often compare the charm of one city with another. Sometimes the mayor or deputy mayor of each city comes out and talks about the charm of his or her city. Except for some major projects, the terms are basically the same. So on this issue, we have obviously entered a devil's nest of using clichés, big words, empty words, and lies to replace authenticity.
Okay, that’s it for today. Let’s meet again next time.

summary.gistZh: 真诚与说真话是中国传统文化中的道德底线，反对用虚伪和套话替代真实，主张求真务实与直面事实的勇气。
summary.gistEn: Sincerity and truth-telling form the ethical baseline of traditional Chinese thought, rejecting hypocrisy and empty rhetoric in favor of seeking truth from facts.

highlights.zh: 反对虚假繁荣：真正的文化繁荣建立在真实之上，任何虚构的历史与饰辞终将被历史唾弃。
highlights.en: Rejecting False Prosperity: True cultural vigor rests on honesty; fabricated histories and deceptive praise are eventually discarded by time.

highlights.zh: 史官精神：从齐太史到司马迁，中国历史学家宁死不改事实，奠定了「秉笔直书」的崇高道德传统。
highlights.en: The Historian's Courage: From ancient scribes to Sima Qian, Chinese historians risked death to record unvarnished truth, forging a noble tradition.

highlights.zh: 诚意正心：儒学将「诚」作为修身齐家的根本，不诚无物，虚伪是文明腐化的开始。
highlights.en: Sincerity of Mind: Confucianism places 'Sincerity' (Cheng) as the foundation of self-cultivation; hypocrisy marks the onset of cultural decay.

highlights.zh: 现实警示：在当代公共表达中，依然需要弘扬勇于说真话、不讲假话套话的清风。
highlights.en: Modern Imperative: In contemporary public dialogue, advocating courageous truth-telling remains a vital civic virtue.

title: 两种成功：中国文化的思维重点
folderName: 13_两种成功：中国文化的思维重点
audioPath: 13_两种成功：中国文化的思维重点/audio.m4a
quoteCardPath: 13_两种成功：中国文化的思维重点/quote_card.jpg
transcriptZh:
大家好，我是余秋雨。我们继续开课。
上次我正在讲中国文化长寿的第六个原因，叫淡化竞争。我们低头一想，我想好多朋友可能都会想到，我们身边的竞争还是蛮多的。那么我想告诉大家，强化输赢、强化成败，这是中国一部分人所做的事情，或者说在有一些历史阶段特别要做的事情。这个主要出现在譬如像科举、官场、商场等场景中，其中的竞争是蛮厉害的。
但是在多数情况下，多数中国人实在是不太在乎竞争，所以不管怎么样，最后都会回到大多数。这里我必须要给大家讲一讲一个非常麻烦的概念，这个概念叫成功。我在各种场合经常会遇到年轻人，或者年轻的家长叫我给他们写几个字，他们最喜欢我写的是成功、天道酬勤这样的概念，而我给他们写的往往是善良、快乐、健康，这是我本人的座右铭。
为什么你不写成功呢？有的人说你自己很成功，是不是把成功的秘诀埋下来了？不是。我个人觉得，现在中国社会最大的麻烦或者最大的悲哀，就是那么多人在求成功、那么多人怕输，这使我们日日夜夜睡不着觉，我们时时刻刻都要关注周围。我们经常心神不安的主要原因就是期盼着成功，不知道自己什么时候成功。这里边就出现两个概念的成功了，我并不是一般意义地反对“成功”这两个字，成功有两个概念，希望大家分开来。
第一个概念是把事情做成功，这是第一个概念。第二个概念是把别人比下去。我所主张的成功或者我所点头的成功，是第一个成功，就是把事情做成功。把那件事情做成了，我们可以祝贺成功。如果说成功的含义是把别人比下去的话，这个成功就有负面意义了，一种毒药就悄悄地埋藏在里边了。
把别人比下去的心理有各种各样，在权位上把别人比下去，在财富上把别人比下去，在名誉上把别人比下去。在这个问题上，中国人有的时候静下来想一想，要比欧美的很多人脑子都清醒一点。
乏味的官位
譬如对于官位，可能中国社会有很长时间的对于做官的某种崇拜心理，但自己真的去谋求官位，一步步上去的这种人物，数字并不太多。我们经常关注到，很多官员在一夜之间失去权力以后的那种沮丧的心理。其实，这种心理我看的非常非常多，所以我就希望大家不要努力地在追求官位，努力地把自己周围的人比下去，把自己的朋友比下去，把自己对手比下去，这是毫无必要的。
我看到多少退休的官员，天天在苦恼的就是下属对自己的变脸。其实我比较了解，不是变脸。下属他要工作，新的领导来了，布置了工作，我能不能认认真真地跟上去，也不要让新的领导觉得我是老领导的人，而且如果老是围绕在已经退休的老领导的身边，让人家感到这个单位里边有好多小圈圈，这非常的不好，所以他们故意回避了，并不是对你的不忠。但是权位失去以后，就天天苦恼在下属的不忠里，这确实很苦恼。
权位不是一件非常好的事情，这一点我一定要劝劝大家。它有很多承担，有很多牺牲，这一点让我们很感动。但是整体说来，它不是很重要。我遇到一个职位很高的领导，他退休了，幸好他喜欢我的书，所以我们有过一次交谈。
他跟我讲，他天天在写回忆录，已经写了三年了，退休以后在写回忆录，已经写了三年了。他太太告诉我，他是一边翻着我的书，一边在写回忆录。我认真地劝他，我说你既然是我的读者，我不能不告诉你一点，你能不能不要写了，不要写这样的回忆录。你去锻炼，你去投身艺术，你去写写书法，而不要写这样的回忆录。
理由何在呢？我说我们为大家付出的这个程序，结果不错，但是这个程序本身很乏味。你在回忆录里能写什么呢？你没有打过仗，你没有参加过惊心动魄的事情，你是迎来送往的。这个工程上去，那边合资能够谈成，这些东西写出来，我说了一句他听了不是很接受的话，后来很快就接受了，我说这样的回忆录，平心而论，你的儿子和你的孙子也不会看。所以我由此来说明一点，就是官位整体上是比较乏味的，是不值得夸张的，也不值得回忆的。
财富和名声
至于财富也是一样，中国人都非常明白，它成为好多抢劫、觊觎、期待的对象。而且你看好多有大财富的人，他们年纪还比较轻，但是我们去看看像香港、台湾，还有其他好多地方那些非常有钱的人，他们有钱的时间长了一点，几乎每个人都遇到了财富分割上的家族纷争。有的被媒体报道了，有的都不报道，但我知道这里边所埋藏着的骨肉之间的仇恨无与伦比。其实这个骨肉之间的仇恨，在这些富豪年纪还不是很老的时候，已经隐隐约约的看了出来，在耳边递小话的这个大儿子，在我眼前表现出各种各样希望的小儿子等等，他已经知道一场非常不好的家庭分裂将出现在自己的身后，事实也果然如此。
至于名声更是如此了。我专门写过一篇文章讲名声，天底下有多少人后来得到了自己所盼望的名声。不过在名声和它的现实之间，如果产生了非常紧密的结合，多数都是比较平庸的人，连人家来攻击的动力都没有了。所以，名声如果非常好，等他的事情过去了，当他的生命结束以后，名声很快也烟消云散了。所以很多人非常喜欢在自己的墓碑上写上诸如副厅级干部某某某，后面的括号里再写上“本单位没有正厅级”，这就很可笑了。名声最后落实在墓碑上或者落实在悼词上，这完全没有必要。至于政坛和文化界的各种名声由于风涌浪叠，很快就被大家遗忘了。
你看，这样的几个特点，说明了要把别人比下去的成功非常没有价值。所以我相信我们今天听课的人，我并不是在做心理的疏解，我只是在讲中国文化的一个本性。我所说的看穿，中国文化历史上都看穿了。这里我想讲几个中国古代经典名言，这个名言中国人几乎都知道，所以慢慢的就成了我们心里边的一种很厚的沉淀。
比如老子说的“祸兮福所依，福兮祸所伏”，就是说我们的祸和福是紧紧地依靠在一起的。老子又说，祸莫大于不知足。只要你去竞争的话，最大的祸就等待着你。我所说的竞争就是要把别人比下去的那种竞争，而不是把事情做成功的那种竞争。庄子说，安危相易，祸福相生。韩非子说，祸与福同门，利与害为邻。大诗人白居易说，祸福茫茫不可期,大都早退似先知。
这样的例子可以很多很多，这证明中国第一流的哲学家、思想家、文人、诗人，他们在这个问题上取得了一致。我几乎没有在我们中国古代的哲学、美学的论文当中，看到过一个鼓励大家去把别人比下去来获得竞争成功的例子，而所有的最高的话语系统，都紧紧地落实在“淡化竞争”这样的一个基本概念上。所以我可以比较有信心地说，这是中国文化主要的思维重点。
有一些不太重要的思维硬块也存在，就是我讲到的“追求输赢成败”也存在，但是它真正的文化重点是在淡化竞争。这个问题我下次还要讲。
transcriptEn:
Hello everyone, my name is Yu Qiuyu. We continue with classes.
Last time I was talking about the sixth reason for the longevity of Chinese culture, which is to downplay competition. When we lower our heads and think about it, I think many friends may think that there is still a lot of competition around us. Well, I want to tell you that strengthening winning and losing, strengthening success and failure is what some people in China do, or it is something that must be done especially in certain historical stages. This mainly appears in scenes such as imperial examinations, officialdom, shopping malls, etc., where the competition is quite fierce.
But in most cases, most Chinese people really don't care much about competition, so no matter what, they will eventually return to the majority. Here I have to tell you about a very troublesome concept called success. I often meet young people on various occasions, or young parents ask me to write a few words for them. What they like most is the concepts of success and God's reward for hard work, and what I write to them is usually kindness, happiness, and health. This is my personal motto.
Why don't you write about success? Some people say that you are very successful. Are you hiding the secret of your success? no. I personally feel that the biggest trouble or sorrow in Chinese society now is that so many people are seeking success and so many people are afraid of losing. This keeps us awake day and night, and we have to pay attention to our surroundings all the time. The main reason why we often feel uneasy is that we look forward to success and don't know when we will succeed. There are two concepts of success here. I am not opposed to the word "success" in a general sense. There are two concepts of success. I hope everyone can separate them.
The first concept is to do things successfully. This is the first concept. The second concept is to compare yourself to others. The success I advocate or the success I nod to is the first success, which is to get things done successfully. Get that thing done and we can congratulate you on the success. If the meaning of success is to compare with others, then this success has a negative meaning, and a kind of poison is quietly buried in it.
There are various psychology of comparing others to others, including comparing others in power and position, comparing others in wealth, and comparing others in reputation. On this issue, the Chinese people sometimes calm down and think about it, and they are more clear-headed than many people in Europe and the United States.
boring official position
For example, regarding official positions, Chinese society may have had a certain kind of admiration for officials for a long time, but there are not many people who really seek official positions and advance step by step. We often notice the frustration of many officials after they lose power overnight. In fact, I have seen this kind of psychology very, very much, so I hope that everyone will stop trying so hard to pursue official positions and try to compare themselves to those around them, their friends, and their opponents. This is unnecessary.
I have seen many retired officials who are worried about their subordinates' changing attitude towards them every day. In fact, I understand better, and I am not changing my face. A subordinate has to work. When a new leader comes and assigns work, can I follow him seriously? Don't let the new leader think that I belong to the old leader. Moreover, if I am always around the old leader who has retired, it will make people feel that there are many small circles in this unit. This is very bad, so they deliberately avoid it. It is not disloyal to you. But after losing power and position, he would be troubled by his subordinates' disloyalty every day, which was indeed very distressing.
Power and position are not a very good thing, I must advise everyone on this. It involves a lot of commitment and a lot of sacrifice, which moved us very much. But overall, it's not very important. I met a very senior leader who was retired, and luckily he liked my book, so we had a conversation.
He told me that he has been writing his memoirs every day for three years. He has been writing his memoirs for three years after retirement. His wife told me that he was writing his memoirs while flipping through my book. I seriously advised him, I said since you are my reader, I have to tell you something, can you please stop writing, don’t write such a memoir. You go exercise, you go engage in art, you go write calligraphy, instead of writing a memoir like this.
What's the reason? I say the program we paid for, the results were good, but the program itself was boring. What can you write in a memoir? You have never fought in a war, you have not participated in thrilling things, you have been welcomed and sent away. When this project was completed, a joint venture could be negotiated there, and after writing these things, I said something that he did not accept very well, but he quickly accepted it. I said that to be fair, your son and grandson would not read such a memoir. So I want to make a point from this, that is, official positions are relatively boring as a whole, and they are not worth exaggerating or remembering.
wealth and fame
The same goes for wealth. Chinese people know very well that it has become the object of many robberies, covetations, and expectations. And if you look at many people with great wealth, they are still relatively young, but if we look at the very wealthy people in Hong Kong, Taiwan, and many other places, they have been rich for a long time, and almost everyone has encountered family disputes over the division of wealth. Some are reported by the media, and some are not reported, but I know that the hatred between flesh and blood buried here is unparalleled. In fact, the hatred between flesh and blood has been vaguely seen when these rich people are not very old. The eldest son who whispers whispers in his ear, the younger son who shows all kinds of hope in front of me, etc. He already knows that a very bad family division will appear behind him, and this is indeed the case.
As for reputation, this is even more true. I wrote an article specifically about fame. How many people in the world later got the fame they longed for. However, if there is a very close connection between fame and its reality, most of them will be relatively mediocre people, and they will not even have the motivation to attack. Therefore, if the reputation is very good, after his incident is over and his life is over, the reputation will soon disappear. Therefore, many people like to write on their tombstones such as "deputy department level cadre so-and-so", followed by "this unit does not have a department level" in parentheses. This is ridiculous. It's totally unnecessary for reputation to end up on a tombstone or in a eulogy. As for the various reputations in the political and cultural circles, they were quickly forgotten by everyone due to the ups and downs.
You see, several characteristics like these show that success is very worthless when comparing yourself to others. So I believe that for those of us who are listening to the lecture today, I am not trying to explain psychology. I am just talking about the nature of Chinese culture. What I mean by seeing through has been seen through in Chinese culture and history. Here I would like to talk about a few ancient Chinese classics. Almost all Chinese people know this famous saying, so it has gradually become a deep deposit in our hearts.
For example, Lao Tzu said, "Misfortunes are where blessings depend, and blessings are where misfortunes lie." This means that our misfortunes and blessings are closely dependent on each other. Lao Tzu also said that there is no greater disaster than not being satisfied. As long as you compete, the greatest disaster awaits you. The competition I'm talking about is the kind of competition that involves comparing others to others, rather than the kind of competition that involves getting things done successfully. Zhuangzi said that safety and danger come to each other, and misfortunes and blessings come to each other. Han Feizi said that misfortune and blessing belong to the same family, benefit and harm are neighbors. The great poet Bai Juyi said that good fortune and misfortune are unpredictable, and most of them retire early like a prophet.
There are many such examples, which proves that China's first-class philosophers, thinkers, literati, and poets have reached consensus on this issue. I have hardly seen an example in ancient Chinese philosophy and aesthetics papers that encourages everyone to compare others to achieve competitive success, and all the highest discourse systems are tightly implemented on the basic concept of "downplaying competition." So I can say with some confidence that this is the main focus of thinking in Chinese culture.
There are some less important ideological blocks that exist, such as the "pursuing winning or losing, success or failure" that I mentioned, but its real cultural focus is on downplaying competition. I will talk about this issue next time.

summary.gistZh: 中国文化重新定义了「成功」，区分了世俗的功名利禄（一时之成功）与人格道德、文明贡献的立德立言（万世之成功）。
summary.gistEn: Chinese culture redefines 'Success', distinguishing ephemeral worldly status from eternal success achieved through moral virtue, ideas, and cultural contribution ('Three Immortalities').

highlights.zh: 两种成功对比：一种是权力、财富与权势（随生命消逝）；一种是思想、文章与品格（历千年而不朽）。
highlights.en: Two Types of Success: Worldly power and wealth fade with life; enduring ideas, literature, and character shine across centuries.

highlights.zh: 三不朽理念：立德、立功、立言，中国智者追求的是将个体生命融入文明的长河中。
highlights.en: The Three Immortalities: Establishing Virtue, Service, and Words—Chinese sages sought to merge individual life into civilization's river.

highlights.zh: 苏东坡与杜甫的例子：世俗命运坎坷颠沛，但因其伟大的精神与诗篇，获得了真正的终极成功。
highlights.en: Examples of Su Shi & Du Fu: Though materially tragic, their sublime spirit and poetry granted them ultimate historical victory.

highlights.zh: 破解功利焦虑：给被现代成功学困扰的人们提供了重新审视人生价值的高远视角。
highlights.en: Overcoming Modern Anxiety: Providing a elevated perspective for individuals trapped in modern hyper-utilitarian rat races.

title: 道教的三项呼唤：和平，自然，生命
folderName: 14_道教的三项呼唤：和平，自然，生命
audioPath: 14_道教的三项呼唤：和平，自然，生命/audio.m4a
quoteCardPath: 14_道教的三项呼唤：和平，自然，生命/quote_card.jpg
transcriptZh:
大家好，我是余秋雨，我们继续讲课。
我上次为道教辩护，讲了他们的第三个正面功能，养气护生。他非常重视我们的生命哲学，而且希望能够在大宇宙当中找一些很好的元气的东西来补充我们的身体的小宇宙。他们尽管在实验当中有好多失败的先例，但是也有很多成功的先例。
青蒿素的发现
我必须要讲一讲成功的先例了，因为我们听到过的都是失败的先例。大家知道，我们中国首位获得诺贝尔医学奖的屠呦呦教授，因为发明了青蒿素的药剂，而救活了世界上的几百万人的生命。屠呦呦教授坦陈，她对于青蒿素的注意，最早出自于葛洪的著作。我前面讲到过葛洪，除了前面所说过的，他是系统地整理了道教教义体系的第一人，他还是一位具有里程碑意义上的道教的药学家。他那么早就发现了青蒿素，我认为，屠呦呦教授在今天的获奖，也是给这位一千七百多年前的道教探索者送去了掌声。这掌声属于道家，也属于道教，至少是。在这一点上，我们对道教对于医学事业的贡献，我们一定要给予更多的正面评价。
大家知道，葛洪他是一位著名的炼丹师，他主张“内修形神，延命愈疾”，四个字的主张，一个叫做“内修形神”，另外四个字叫“延命愈疾”，把生命延续下去，把疾病能够治愈。他对道教的另一项贡献，写出了中国文化史上不可小看的学术著作，叫做《抱朴子》，比较完整地建立了道教的神仙理论体系。他认为仙人不是天生的，而是修来的，“长生可得，仙人无种”，任何人都能够成仙，只要你修炼，就叩动了仙门。
从葛洪，我们又可以联想到他的南京的同乡，比他晚了一百七十多年的道教名家，叫陶弘景，陶，那我们都知道陶渊明的陶，弘呢，弘扬中华文化的弘，景，风景的景。陶弘景，他是公元五世纪到六世纪的人物，他写过很多上清派的道法的著作，他也是一位名医，他所著的《本草经集注》七卷，极大地推动了中国的药学。在医学上，比陶弘景还要出名的，是比陶弘景晚了一百二十多年的道教名医，叫孙思邈。他是陕西人，他长时间的隐居在终南山，研习道教，辛苦地炼丹，又写出了中国医药史上的名著《千金药方》，《千金翼方》，《摄养枕中方》，《保生铭》等等，成为一代医学大师。
这些光辉的名字，还可以在道教的护生长廊当中一直排下去，他们在医学上的成就一点无愧于世界上的其他地方的同行。这些名字，曾经救助过多少生命，实在是无法统计了。无可怀疑的是，他们有效地护佑了世界上人口最多的民族的健康。与此相比，那么在炼丹炉边上发生的“医疗事故”，也不必要过多的计较了，因为他们实在是让中华民族成为人口最多的一个民族，这和道教的医学有关。
养气护生，生命第一，这是道教千年前的坚持。直到今天，当我们看到地震、海啸的救援队伍一遍遍地喊出“生命第一”口号的时候，我们总会想起道教很早的时候，就提出的在医学方面的一系列的主张。
中医与中药
这个问题，我需要多讲几句了。道家的医学家，构成了中国的医学文明的主干，这是我们现在的主张的医学人文的一个非常重大的思维。我到北京参加中国医学人文大会，我有一个主旨演讲。我的演讲主要也是讲道教的医学思维，不是一般的泛泛讲，这个中国没有普及，在世界上也没有普及，但是我们必须认真的讲。
我想起一件事情，在一九二九年的时候，当时的国民政府行政院开了一个全国医学大会，决定逐步取缔中医。当时的行政院长是汪精卫，他提出一个观点，他说日本的明治维新的第一件事就是取缔中医，所以我们也要取缔，他认为这是科学思维。但是，他缺少的是人文思维。这里边又造成了汪精卫和蒋介石的第一次矛盾，这个矛盾，蒋介石是对的，蒋介石是当时是国民政府主席，汪精卫是行政院长。过了不久，一九二九年的三月份，上海有一大批中医派的代表到南京去请愿的时候，最后蒋介石下令撤销那个全国卫生大会关于取缔中医的决定。
他用了一个基本的思维，说孙中山讲过，要保持中国固有的文明，并发扬光大。蒋介石在他的那个撤销令里边，专门讲了孙中山这句话。孙中山所说的保持中国的固有文明、固有智慧，并让它发扬光大，在这句话里边，毫无疑问，包括中国的医学人文，蒋介石把他引到这个撤销令上来也是对的。
大家想想看，中华文明怎么成立的？中华文明的成立是和炎帝亲尝草药，治百病，来抗拒我们原始人最大的敌人——传染病，这是有关的。好多民族、好多人群，为什么灭亡了？在早期，有的时候是由于战争，有的是由于自然灾害，有的就是属于自然灾害的一种，叫做传染病。我们的炎帝就亲尝草药、治百病，这是我们的人文的起点。至于人文的一个延续过程当中，我们道教医学家就创造了我前面讲到的我们固有的文明智慧，造成的结果是让中华民族成为世界上人口最多的民族，那是他们的人文成果。
更有趣的是，我们要面对这么个事实，当一九二九年全国医学大会，作出决议，要取缔中医的时候，汪精卫他们不清楚的一点是一个非常严峻的事实，全中国当时的中医的人数是八十三万，而西医全中国只有六千。大家想想看，八十三万的中医，而且药铺有二十多万家，这是保全了中华民族健康的一个基本的传统功能。西医虽然很好，从国外传进来的，它是科学主义，而不是人文主义，传进来以后，它只有六千人。中国那么大，人口那么多，六千人，六千人意味着什么？就是连很当时的很多县里边是连一个西医也找不到。
你西医，哪怕是再科学，它怎么能够面对要治疗中华民族这个大人口的这么一个人文课题，所以，我认为科学主义很好，但是，我们还要维护中国传统的医学人文，而医学人文的很大的主干，就是以道教医学家为主干的那个中医和中药。我们记得葛洪，我们记得陶弘景，我们记得孙思邈，这些人都是名字非常响亮的道教医学家，我们要尊重他们。
这样的话，我就讲了道教直到今天还具有价值的三项功能，清心戒杀，参赞天地，养气护生。这三项功能，用现在的话来说就是呼唤和平，呼唤自然，呼唤生命。清心戒杀，是呼唤和平；参赞天地，是呼唤自然；养气护生，是呼唤生命。大家想一想，在当代世界，还有什么比这三项呼唤更重要的？呼唤和平，呼唤自然，呼唤生命。我们想想在中国这块土地上，道教已经呼唤了千遍万遍，我们是不是应该对他们产生新的尊重？这个呢，我就回想起我在茅山的山壁上所题的那四个字，大道巍峨，一点不错。谢谢大家。
transcriptEn:
Hello everyone, I am Yu Qiuyu, let’s continue the lecture.
Last time I defended Taoism, I talked about their third positive function, which is to nourish qi and protect life. He attaches great importance to our philosophy of life, and hopes to find some good vitality things in the macrocosm to supplement the microcosm of our body. Although they have many failed experiments, they also have many successful ones.
Discovery of artemisinin
I have to talk about success stories because all we hear about are failures. As we all know, Professor Tu Youyou, China’s first Nobel Prize winner in medicine, saved the lives of millions of people around the world because of her invention of artemisinin. Professor Tu Youyou said frankly that her attention to artemisinin first came from Ge Hong's works. I mentioned Ge Hong before. In addition to what I said before, he was the first person to systematically organize the Taoist teaching system. He was also a landmark Taoist pharmacist. He discovered artemisinin so early. I think Professor Tu Youyou’s award today is also a round of applause for this explorer of Taoism more than 1,700 years ago. This applause belongs to Taoism and Taoism, at least. At this point, we must give more positive comments to Taoism's contribution to medicine.
As we all know, Ge Hong is a famous alchemist. He advocates "cultivating the body and spirit internally, prolonging life and making diseases more severe". One of his four-word propositions is "cultivating body and spirit internally", and the other four words are "prolonging life and healing diseases". It can extend life and cure diseases. Another contribution he made to Taoism was the writing of an academic work that cannot be underestimated in the history of Chinese culture, called "Baopuzi", which relatively completely established the Taoist theory system of immortals. He believes that immortals are not born, but are cultivated. "Immortality can be obtained, but immortals have no seeds." Anyone can become an immortal. As long as you practice, you will be able to gain access to immortality.
From Ge Hong, we can think of his hometown in Nanjing, a famous Taoist master who was more than 170 years later than him, named Tao Hongjing, Tao, then we all know Tao Yuanming's Tao, Hong, Hong, Jing, scenery Jing who promoted Chinese culture. Tao Hongjing was a figure from the fifth to sixth centuries AD. He wrote many Taoist works of the Shangqing School. He was also a famous doctor. His seven-volume "Compendium of Materia Medica" greatly promoted Chinese medicine. In medicine, even more famous than Tao Hongjing is a famous Taoist doctor named Sun Simiao who was more than 120 years later than Tao Hongjing. He is from Shaanxi. He lived in seclusion in Zhongnan Mountain for a long time, studied Taoism, worked hard to refine elixirs, and wrote famous works in the history of Chinese medicine, such as "Qian Jin Prescription", "Qian Jin Yi Prescription", "Chinese Prescriptions for Maintaining Pillows", "Baosheng Ming", etc., and became a generation of medical masters.
These glorious names can continue to be ranked in the Taoist nursing corridor. Their achievements in medicine are worthy of their counterparts in other parts of the world. It is impossible to count how many lives these names have saved. There is no doubt that they effectively protect the health of the world's most populous nation. Compared with this, there is no need to worry too much about the "medical accidents" that occurred near the alchemy furnace, because they have actually made the Chinese nation the most populous nation, and this is related to Taoist medicine.
To nourish qi and protect life, life comes first. This is the Taoist insistence thousands of years ago. To this day, when we see earthquake and tsunami rescue teams shouting the slogan "life first" over and over again, we always think of a series of medical propositions put forward by Taoism very early on.
Traditional Chinese Medicine and Traditional Chinese Medicine
I need to say a few more words on this issue. Taoist medical scientists form the backbone of China's medical civilization. This is a very important thinking in the medical humanities that we currently advocate. I went to Beijing to attend the Chinese Medical Humanities Conference, and I had a keynote speech. My speech was mainly about Taoist medical thinking, not a general talk. This is not popular in China, and it is not popular in the world, but we must talk about it seriously.
I remember one thing. In 1929, the Executive Yuan of the National Government held a national medical conference and decided to gradually ban traditional Chinese medicine. The executive president at that time was Wang Jingwei. He put forward a point of view. He said that the first thing Japan did during the Meiji Restoration was to ban traditional Chinese medicine, so we should also ban it. He thought this was scientific thinking. However, what he lacks is humanistic thinking. This caused the first conflict between Wang Jingwei and Chiang Kai-shek. In this conflict, Chiang Kai-shek was right. Chiang Kai-shek was the chairman of the National Government at the time, and Wang Jingwei was the executive president. Not long after, in March 1929, when a large number of representatives of traditional Chinese medicine practitioners from Shanghai went to Nanjing to petition, Chiang Kai-shek finally ordered the revocation of the National Health Assembly's decision to ban traditional Chinese medicine.
He used a basic idea and said that Sun Yat-sen said that China’s inherent civilization should be maintained and carried forward. Chiang Kai-shek specifically mentioned Sun Yat-sen's words in his revocation order. Sun Yat-sen said that China's inherent civilization and wisdom should be maintained and carried forward. In this sentence, there is no doubt that it includes China's medical humanities. Chiang Kai-shek was right to lead him to this revocation order.
Think about it, everyone, how did Chinese civilization come to be? The establishment of Chinese civilization is related to Emperor Yan's personal use of medicinal herbs to cure all diseases to resist the biggest enemy of our primitive people - infectious diseases. This is related. Why did so many ethnic groups and groups of people perish? In the early days, some were due to wars, some were due to natural disasters, and some were a type of natural disaster called infectious diseases. Our Emperor Yan personally tasted medicinal herbs and cured all diseases. This is the starting point of our humanities. As for the continuation of humanities, we Taoist medical scientists have created our inherent civilizational wisdom that I mentioned earlier, and the result has been that the Chinese nation has become the most populous nation in the world. That is their humanistic achievement.
What’s more interesting is that we have to face the fact that when the National Medical Congress in 1929 made a resolution to ban traditional Chinese medicine, what Wang Jingwei and others did not know was a very serious fact. The number of traditional Chinese medicine practitioners in China at that time was 830,000, while there were only 6,000 Western medicine practitioners in China. Think about it, everyone, there are 830,000 traditional Chinese medicine practitioners and more than 200,000 drug stores. This is a basic traditional function that protects the health of the Chinese nation. Although Western medicine is very good, it was introduced from abroad based on scientism, not humanism. After it was introduced, it only had 6,000 people. China is so big and has such a large population, six thousand people. What does six thousand people mean? Even many counties at that time could not find even a single Western medicine doctor.
Western medicine, no matter how scientific it is, can face such a humanistic issue of treating a large population of the Chinese nation. Therefore, I think scientism is very good, but we must also maintain the traditional Chinese medical humanities, and the major backbone of medical humanities is traditional Chinese medicine and traditional Chinese medicine, which is based on Taoist medical scientists. We remember Ge Hong, we remember Tao Hongjing, and we remember Sun Simiao. These people are all Taoist medical scientists with very famous names, and we must respect them.
In this case, I talked about the three functions of Taoism that are still valuable to this day: to purify the mind and abstain from killing, to counsel heaven and earth, and to nourish qi and protect life. These three functions, in current terms, are calling for peace, calling for nature, and calling for life. To be pure in mind and abstain from killing is to call for peace; to consult the heaven and earth is to call to nature; to nourish qi and protect life is to call for life. Think about it, everyone, in the contemporary world, what else is more important than these three calls? Calling for peace, calling for nature, calling for life. Let’s think about it. In China, Taoism has been called thousands of times. Should we have new respect for them? As for this, I recall the four words I wrote on the mountain wall of Maoshan Mountain. The road is majestic, which is true. Thank you all.

summary.gistZh: 道教作为中国本土宗教，核心呼唤在于对「和平、自然、生命」的关切，主张顺应天道、尊重生命规律与身心和谐。
summary.gistEn: As China's indigenous religion, Taoism's core calling lies in its reverence for 'Peace, Nature, and Life'—advocating alignment with the Tao, respect for vital laws, and mind-body harmony.

highlights.zh: 三大核心呼唤：呼唤和平（反对战争杀戮）、呼唤自然（天人合一）、呼唤生命（贵生重生）。
highlights.en: Three Core Callings: Peaceful harmony (anti-war), Natural resonance (oneness of cosmos and human), and Vitality (revering physical & spiritual life).

highlights.zh: 本土宗教的独特性：不同于向外探索或彼岸救赎，道教极其关切当下生命的健康、长寿与身心自在。
highlights.en: Uniqueness of Local Faith: Unlike religions focused purely on afterlife redemption, Taoism deeply cares for immediate health, longevity, and freedom.

highlights.zh: 天人合一生态观：将人类视为大自然的一部分，反对过度开发与违反自然的狂妄扩张。
highlights.en: Ecological Oneness: Viewing humanity as an intrinsic part of nature, opposing arrogant over-exploitation of environmental balance.

highlights.zh: 养生与艺术灵感：道教为中国中医药学、书法、山水画及养生哲学提供了源源不断的灵感。
highlights.en: Source of Healing & Arts: Inspiring Chinese traditional medicine, calligraphy, landscape painting, and holistic wellness practices.

title: 佛教最简明的精神支点与核心思维——《心经》

transcriptZh:
大家好，我是余秋雨，我们继续讲佛教。我讲到我和星云大师有非常密切的交往，在这个过程当中，我后来到印度释迦牟尼走过的很多地方一一去参拜，他出生的地方现在在尼泊尔，这个地方叫兰毗，我也在那儿待了很长时间。在考察佛教的最早的形迹的时候，我发现世界上很多很多文明的故地，确实都陷入在战乱和恐怖之中。
佛教经典中的经典——《心经》
我到佛教圣地去朝拜的时候，我其实是从地狱一步一步地去对比天堂。因为我看到的当时的世界，那么多的对立，那么多的争夺，那么多的仇恨，那么多的欲望，那么多的战乱，所有的冲突的对手都举着手指，指着对方的鼻子，滔滔怒斥，其实他们的毛病大同小异。就在这样恐怖主义的整体气氛当中，我风尘仆仆地赶到了印度的菩提伽耶，找到了那棵菩提树，不错，那就是佛陀释迦牟尼最早开悟的地方，经过很多佛教学者的考证，地点准确无误，但是时隔两千多年，当然已经不是那棵树了。据考证那是原来的那棵树的种子到了斯里兰卡，后来这个种子的种子又来到了这个菩提伽耶，他原来打坐那个地方。
我坐在那很长时间，世界各地赶来的僧侣有几十名，和我一起坐着。我一直在想，他在山洞苦修了很多年，最后终于来到了菩提树下，他到底在想什么？他开悟在这儿开悟的，他开悟的到底是哪一些观念、哪一些想法？这个是我认真的需要寻找的一个最简明的精神支点。我一直想寻找一个佛教的最简明的精神支点在哪里？我坐在菩提树下，想啊想啊想，想那次开悟的那个点，就是我要找的精神支点。所以我在想，我一定要找到一个文本，找了很多很多时间以后，读了很多很多经文以后，最早集中在《心经》，大家都知道的《心经》。
《心经》是大乘佛教里边最简明的范本，也是《般若经》里边的一个概要，我认为这里边既然是概要，里边的好多词汇、很多概念、很多哲理，需要我一点一点地去深入，我就把《心经》作为我的研究的一个重点。今天我在我的课程当中也是启发大家，如果大家要对佛教有深入了解的话，最好对《心经》能够更加深入。
我首先要说明一点，《心经》的“心”可能被很多人误会了，以为是研究心的学问，研究我们的心理，研究我们的心态，研究我们的心灵，所以叫《心经》。其实最早翻译的时候不是这个意思，这个“心”字指的是核心，指的是纲要，《心经》其实是所有经典当中的核心之经，纲要之经。大家理解我这个意思没有？它是经典中的经典，经典当中的精简物，就是《心经》。
《心经》的文本解读
《心经》我想很多人都会背诵，就是“观自在菩萨，行深般若波罗蜜多时，照见五蕴皆空，度一切苦厄。舍利子！色不异空、空不异色，色即是空、空即是色。受想行识、亦复如是。舍利子！是诸法空相。不生不灭、不垢不净、不增不减。是故空中无色、无受想行识。无眼、耳、鼻、舌、身、意。无色、声、香、味、触、法。无眼界、乃至无意识界。无无明、亦无无明尽。乃至无老死、亦无老死尽。无苦集灭道，无智亦无得，以无所得故”等等等等。
我不把它背完了，很多人每天背、很多人经常抄，但是它到底在讲什么，我把它翻译了一下，我用我对佛教的了解，也对于古代语文和现代语文之间的转换，我把它翻译成了一个大家都能听得懂的散文。我相信那是符合经典原文，是符合它的原本的哲学思想。去年我的翰墨展在中国美术馆展出的时候，展出了我所写的《心经》以及星云大师举着我的《心经》向世界佛教徒推荐时候的情景，推荐我的手写的文本。我同时又把《心经》翻译成了白话文张贴在展览的墙上的时候，我发现参观者在用手机来拍摄我的白话文本的《心经》的特别多。可见大家背《心经》念《心经》，却对《心经》的白话文本不太清楚。他到底是什么意思？我今天先向大家朗读一下我翻译的《心经》是什么样的内容。
《波若波罗蜜多心经》的精义是这样的：一个能够自在地进行观察的菩萨，在深度修行中以最高智慧获得关照，发现世界种种蕴集都空虚无常，于是一切痛苦和灾异都可以度过。舍利子啊，物质形态的色，全部都等于空，正可谓色不异空，空不异色，色即是空，空即是色。其实就连感受、想象、行为、见识，也都是这样。舍利子啊，各种概念都是空相，因此无所谓诞生和灭亡，无所谓污垢和洁净，无所谓增加和减少。
在空相中，没有真实的物质、感受、想象、行为、见识，没有真实的眼、耳、鼻、舌、身、意，也没有真实的视觉、听觉、嗅觉、味觉、触觉、记忆，从视觉到意识之间的种种界定，都不存在。在空相中，既没有无厘头的愚暗，也没有无明的结束；既没有老死的轮回，也没有老死的终止；既没有苦恼的聚集，也没有苦恼的断灭；既没有机制，也没有获得。
正因为一无所得，大菩萨凭着大智慧超度，心中就没有牵挂和障碍，所以也没有恐怖，能够远离种种颠倒梦想，终于达到真正的解脱——涅槃。
过去、现在、未来这三世，觉悟者只要凭着大智慧超度，就能获得最高正觉。大智慧超度就是神圣的咒语，光明的咒语，无上的咒语，无比的咒语。这咒语能够除去众生的一切痛苦，真实不虚。那么，就让我们来颂念这个咒语——去吧，去，到彼岸去。大家都去，赶快觉悟！
这就是我对《心经》的翻译。我们下次再讲。
transcriptEn:
Hello everyone, I am Yu Qiuyu, and we continue to talk about Buddhism. I mentioned that I had a very close relationship with Master Hsing Yun. During this process, I later went to India to pay homage to many of the places where Gautama Buddha visited. The place where he was born is now in Nepal. This place is called Lumpi, and I also stayed there for a long time. When I was investigating the earliest traces of Buddhism, I discovered that many places of civilization in the world were indeed mired in war and terror.
The classic among Buddhist classics - "Heart Sutra"
When I went to Buddhist holy places to worship, I actually compared heaven step by step from hell. Because the world I saw at that time was filled with so much opposition, so much competition, so much hatred, so much desire, and so many wars. The opponents in all conflicts raised their fingers, pointed at each other’s noses, and denounced them angrily. In fact, their problems were basically the same. In this overall atmosphere of terrorism, I rushed to Bodhgaya, India, and found the Bodhi tree. Yes, it was the place where the Buddha Sakyamuni first became enlightened. After verification by many Buddhist scholars, the location was accurate. However, after more than two thousand years, of course it was not that tree anymore. According to research, the seeds of the original tree came to Sri Lanka. Later, the seeds of this seed came to Bodh Gaya, where he originally meditated.
I sat there for a long time, and dozens of monks came from all over the world to sit with me. I have been thinking that he practiced hard in the cave for many years and finally came to the bodhi tree. What on earth was he thinking? He became enlightened here. What concepts and thoughts did he become enlightened about? This is the simplest spiritual fulcrum that I seriously need to find. I have always wanted to find the most concise spiritual fulcrum of Buddhism. I sat under the bodhi tree, thinking and thinking, thinking that the point of enlightenment was the spiritual fulcrum I was looking for. So I was thinking that I must find a text. After searching for a lot of time and reading many scriptures, I first focused on the "Heart Sutra", which everyone knows.
The Heart Sutra is the most concise model in Mahayana Buddhism, and it is also an outline of the Prajna Sutra. I think since it is an outline, there are many words, concepts, and philosophies in it that I need to go into in depth little by little, so I will make the Heart Sutra a focus of my research. Today, I am also inspiring everyone in my course. If you want to have a deep understanding of Buddhism, it is best to go deeper into the Heart Sutra.
First of all, I want to explain that the "heart" in the "Heart Sutra" may be misunderstood by many people, thinking that it is the study of the heart, our psychology, our mentality, and our soul, so it is called the "Heart Sutra". In fact, this was not what it meant when it was first translated. The word "heart" refers to the core and the outline. The Heart Sutra is actually the core sutra and the outline sutra of all classics. Do you understand what I mean? It is a classic among classics, a concise version of the classics, which is the Heart Sutra.
Text Interpretation of the Heart Sutra
I think many people will recite the "Heart Sutra", which is "Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, walking in the deep Prajnaparamita for a long time, saw that the five aggregates are empty, and survived all the hardships. Relic! The form is not different from emptiness, and emptiness is not different from color. Color is empty, and emptiness is color. Reception, thought, and awareness are also like this. Relic! This is the empty phase of all dharmas. They are neither born nor destroyed, nor stained nor pure. It does not increase or decrease. Therefore, there is no form, no thoughts, no eyes, no ears, no nose, no body, no mind. No vision, no unconscious world. There is no end of old age and death. There is no path of suffering, no wisdom, no gain, etc.
I have not finished memorizing it. Many people memorize it every day and many people often copy it. But what is it talking about? I translated it. I used my understanding of Buddhism and the conversion between ancient Chinese and modern language to translate it into a prose that everyone can understand. I believe that it is in line with the original text of the classic and its original philosophical thought. Last year, when my calligraphy exhibition was on display at the National Art Museum of China, the Heart Sutra I wrote and the scene when Master Hsing Yun held up my Heart Sutra to recommend it to Buddhists around the world were displayed, recommending my handwritten text. At the same time, I translated the Heart Sutra into vernacular and posted it on the wall of the exhibition. I found that many visitors were using their mobile phones to take pictures of my vernacular version of the Heart Sutra. It can be seen that everyone memorizes and recites the Heart Sutra, but they are not very clear about the vernacular text of the Heart Sutra. What does he mean? Today I will first read aloud to you what my translation of the Heart Sutra is like.
The essence of the Paramita Heart Sutra is as follows: a Bodhisattva who can observe freely, receives care with the highest wisdom in deep practice, and discovers that all the accumulations in the world are empty and impermanent, so all pain and disasters can be overcome. Relics, all colors in material form are equal to emptiness. It can be said that color is not different from emptiness, and emptiness is not different from color. Color is emptiness, and emptiness is color. In fact, even feelings, imagination, behavior, and insights are like this. Relic, all concepts are empty, so there is no birth or death, no dirt or cleansing, no increase or decrease.
In the empty phase, there are no real substances, feelings, imaginations, behaviors, and insights. There are no real eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind. There are also no real vision, hearing, smell, taste, touch, and memory. All kinds of definitions from vision to consciousness do not exist. In the emptiness, there is neither senseless darkness nor the end of ignorance; there is neither the reincarnation of old age nor the end of old age and death; there is neither the accumulation of suffering nor the cessation of suffering; there is neither mechanism nor gain.
Precisely because he gained nothing, the great Bodhisattva relied on his great wisdom to transcend. He had no worries and obstacles in his heart, so he had no fear. He was able to stay away from all kinds of upside-down dreams and finally achieved true liberation - Nirvana.
In the past, present and future, as long as the enlightened person transcends them with great wisdom, he can achieve the highest enlightenment. The salvation of great wisdom is the sacred mantra, the light mantra, the supreme mantra, the incomparable mantra. This mantra can remove all suffering from sentient beings, and it is true. So, let us chant this mantra - go, go, to the other side. Everyone, go and wake up quickly!
This is my translation of the Heart Sutra. We’ll talk about that next time.

summary.gistZh: 《心经》以极其精炼的文字（260字）阐释了佛教的核心智慧「色即是空，空即是色」，引导人们放下执念、破除恐惧，获得心灵的终极平静。
summary.gistEn: The Heart Sutra concisely (260 characters) encapsulates Buddhism's core wisdom: 'Form is Emptiness, Emptiness is Form'—guiding minds to relinquish attachments, dissolve fear, and achieve inner tranquility.

highlights.zh: 佛教最简明支点：仅260字，却构成了中国佛教思想史上影响力最大的精神支柱。
highlights.en: Most Concise Spiritual Pillar: At just 260 characters, it stands as the most influential spiritual anchor in East Asian Buddhism.

highlights.zh: 「色即是空，空即是色」：现象与本质互为表里，万物皆在变化流转中，不必偏执于暂时的得失。
highlights.en: 'Form is Emptiness, Emptiness is Form': Appearance and essence are interdependent; all phenomena shift, so do not cling rigidly to transient gain or loss.

highlights.zh: 无挂碍故，无有恐怖：破除对名利、生死与功利的执念，才能从根本上祛除焦虑与恐惧。
highlights.en: No Impediment, No Fear: Dissolving obsession with fame, life, or death cures anxiety and fear at their root.

highlights.zh: 中国化佛教的胜利：将深奥的印度佛学转化为中国人触手可及的切爽心灵智慧。
highlights.en: Victory of Sinicized Buddhism: Transforming complex Indian metaphysics into accessible, practical inner wisdom for daily life.

title: 李清照：中国第一女诗人
folderName: 16_李清照：中国第一女诗人
audioPath: 16_李清照：中国第一女诗人/audio.m4a
quoteCardPath: 16_李清照：中国第一女诗人/quote_card.jpg
transcriptZh:
大家好，我是余秋雨。
昨天我们已经讲了宋代文化的第二个方面，叫做两个文化高官：王安石和司马光。大家一定发现了这两个人对中国文化的君子人格做了惊心动魄的顶端事业。在行政上他们都没有成功，但是在文化上却成功了
,
最大的成功就是他们把文化人格推进了历史，让历史吓了一跳。
大家想想看，我上次讲了宋代的一个文化全才苏东坡，再加上这两个文化高官：王安石和司马光。仅仅这三个人，宋代文化已经虎虎有生气，但是我们肯定还没有讲完，因为还有一些非常精彩的人格范型。
我前面讲到，王安石和司马光能够攀登上国家行政的顶峰，有赖于宋代的一个特殊的文官体制。这文官体制当然让我们很兴奋，但是文官体制也带来很大的弊病。其中一条就是严重地削弱了军事力量。加上朝廷日益腐败，高压的宋朝，最不愿意听到的一些词汇，经常跑到朝野的耳朵边上来。
哪些词汇呢？如：遭袭、战败、被俘、乞降，成为宋朝历史上经常出现的词汇。后来，连两个皇帝宋徽宗、宋钦宗也成了俘虏，又不得不迁都临安，改为南宋，改为南宋以后仍然危机重重。
这些历史，很多书籍都写到了，我就不重复了。我只想告诉大家，在一层一层军事失败的愁云惨雾当中，中国文化竟然选择了英雄主义，英雄地比将士还要英雄。
而且这种文化上的英雄主义并不是标语口号，并不是虚张声势，而是熔炼成了一种高超的美学人格，成为真正的文学。所以接下来我们的讲课内容就要进入到《三位战乱诗人》。我们回顾一下：一个文化全才，两个文化高官，三个战乱诗人。
我要讲的第一个战乱诗人一定会出乎大家的意料之外。因为初一看
,
她的作品几乎没有刀剑之气，反而充满了无限优雅
,
她就是女诗人李清照。
李清照怎么也能成了战乱诗人？因为她比谁都更加清晰地表现了和平和战争的极端性的差别，写出了一个最典雅东方女子经历家破人亡、离乱逃难的时候的心理感受，一种无以言表的忧愁，已经成为能够挑地起一代人大苦大悲的精神杠杆。这也是宋代文学的一个骄傲，在战乱当中一个个雨中的黄昏，悄悄站起了中国第一女诗人。
荒诞的逃亡
说起李清照，一开头，就要与我前面讲的两位文化高官联系起来了，因为在司马光否定了王安石的变法，后来两人又相继去世之后，形成了复杂的党争。在这个党争当中，司马光被划入了所谓的元佑党人，被新的朝廷否定了。而李清照的父亲李格非也被这个名单所牵连，罢职流放。
这是李清照还是年纪很轻的时候发生的事情。光这个事情已经很悲哀，更悲哀的是，处理这个案件的恰恰是自己新婚丈夫赵明诚的父亲赵挺之，而新婚夫妻的感情又非常好。
李清照曾经写信给自己的公公赵挺之，希望他能够顾及儿子儿媳亲家的脸面，但是没想到公公赵挺之后来也受到了朝廷的打击。这种肃杀的政治气氛，正说明北宋内部已经处于一种互相斗争的泥涛当中了。在这种情况下面，北宋显然已经没有力量来对付周边虎视眈眈的敌对势力，更无法和北方的金国对峙。
李清照和丈夫赵明诚面对父辈的名誉重压，百口莫辩，只能回到故乡齐州居住，过了十多年安静而风雅的生活。我们经常读到的有关他们两个人一起在生活当中写诗，品尚古董的生活，其实都是和这十几年有关。
赵明诚，也就是李清照的丈夫，是一个远近闻名的鉴赏家，但身体不好，不久又犯了重病。在重病期间，曾经有北方的一位探望者带了一把石壶请他过目，赵明诚鉴定以后不久就不幸去世了。
他刚去世，就有谣言兴起了，说他直到临死还把一把玉壶献给了北方的金国。当时因为宋金之间正在激烈交战，这个谣言触及到了中国文化人最喜欢挂在嘴上的所谓气节问题，并且由气节问题延伸到了是不是叛国的民族大义，其实是一种极其脆弱的乱世逻辑。
但是李清照坐不住了，诬陷自己倒也罢了，居然诬陷到自己刚刚去世的丈夫，这怎么能够容忍？她很清楚，这是一个最拙劣的小谣言。因为那把壶就是北方人带来的，以为是玉壶，赵明成一看是石壶，那个人就带回去了。而且那个人只是来自于北方，怎么又和政治扯上了关系？
但是面对气势汹汹的舆论，李清照知道自己说不清楚了，即使赵明诚还活着，他也说不清楚了，这就是谣言的特点，特别是政治谣言的特点。
李清照决心以自己全部力量为自己挚爱的亡夫洗刷名誉，但是她又不知道如何来洗刷。想来想去，我们最诚实的女诗人想出了一个最笨拙的方法，就是带上夫妻两人多年辛苦收藏的全部古董文物，跟随着宋朝的皇帝赵高，赵高当时正好在被金兵追赶，就跟着他一起逃难。
她用这么一个笨拙的方法来表明一个简单的道理：
宋朝已经在逃难了，我都愿意把自己的全部的古董文物去追随朝廷，甚至愿意全部献给朝廷。那么在宋朝还没有逃难的时候，我丈夫怎么会有二心？怎么会将一把壶送给金国呢？
她建立了这么一个勉强的逻辑，让人很感动的逻辑。古董文物不少，一路上颠沛流离，装卸非常辛苦，我们可怜的李清照就天天辛苦地押运着，追赶着朝廷的逃难路。
其实，慌乱中的朝廷完全不知道后面跟着这么一个女人，这么一堆货物，这么一番苦心，更不知道她要用这种方式来洗刷自己家的名誉，来洗刷自己丈夫的名誉。
这就是李清照生命的漫漫长途：逃难、逃难、逃难，押着丈夫的名誉和全部珍宝，永远在战争的缝隙当中着陆。她的词作只是在漫漫长途中的轻轻地喘息，因此她成了一个真正的战乱诗人。
宋高宗在东南沿海一带逃难的时候，曾经一度慌张地居住在海船上，可怜的李清照就远远地跟在后面。她从今天的绍兴到今天的宁波，再经过奉化、台州入海，又经过温州返回绍兴。宋高宗的这一路非常狼狈，而李清照的这一路却非常荒诞。
她为什么会做这么荒诞的选择？我想可能只有一个答案：因为她是诗人，而且还是单身的女诗人。
凄惨的晚年生活
终于谢天谢地，极其疲劳的李清照在路上找到了一个脑子还比较清楚的亲戚，亲戚强烈地劝她立刻终止这一毫无意义的颠沛流离。其实李清照也实在是走不动了，她听从了这位亲戚的话，但是一盘点，她带在身边的文物，一路上已经损失了极大部分。这个时候，女诗人李清照已经年近
50
，这在当时已经算是很高的年岁了，她终于想停步了。
她突然发现，以前每天赶路，除了追赶朝廷，也是为了逃避整体思考。现在一切都不必追赶了，就可以细细想一想了。一想，她不能不摇头叹息，自己从青年时期开始，父亲的名誉，公公的名誉，丈夫的名誉，撕肝裂胆地折腾了自己大半辈子。现在一想究竟有多大意义？
所谓名誉只是出现在别人心目当中，但是那些别人现在在哪里？他们还记得吗？而且这所有的名誉都和朝廷有关，现在连朝廷都找不到自己名誉了，我们又怎么来和朝廷一起分辨是非曲直呢？李清照想来想去，决定告别过去，决定过一种安定的生活。
在宋代，这么一个孤苦伶仃的女性要想过一种比较安定的生活，那就应该找一个家，一个普普通通的家。
当时正好有个军队的财务人员一直在向自己求婚。她想年纪也不小了，那就答应了吧。她当然知道，在当时，一个出身官宦之家的上层女子，与亡夫的感情又很深，已经年近半百，如果再婚，一定受到社会上上下下的指责和嘲笑。但是李清照现在已经把名誉看得很淡，决定走自己的路。
就在这个关口上，她表现出了一种破釜沉舟般的勇敢。如果事情仅仅到此为止那倒罢了，李清照完全可以关起门来和新丈夫一起过一种平凡而安定的生活。但是万万没想到，这个丈夫竟然是一个不良之徒。
他以一个奸商的目光看上了李清照在逃难当中已经所剩无几的古董文物，所谓结婚只是诈骗的一种手段，等到古董文物到手，他立即对李清照拳脚相加、百般虐待。这个奸商的名字叫张汝舟。汝是三点水边上加一个女性的“女”，舟是舟山的“舟”。
实在是可怜到了极点的李清照，只要还有一点点可以容忍的余地，是不会向门外来公布自己的家丑的。但她毕竟知道生命的珍贵，知道善良和高贵不应该在邪恶当中埋没。所以就在结婚三个月以后，她向官府提出上诉，要求离婚。
李清照知道宋代有一项奇怪的法律，妻子上告丈夫，即使丈夫真的有罪，妻子也要被官府关押一阵，但是李清照情愿被关押，也要离婚。结果，离婚是成了，张汝舟被问罪，李清照被关押，幸好在亲戚的帮助下，她没有被关押太久。
后来有不少学者为了保护李清照的名誉，否定李清照曾经再婚并离婚。但这是一种好心，很难掩盖我们所看到的像李心传、王佐、胡仔和赵公武这些人的记载。而且我们还能读到李清照在写给亲戚的一封信，当中还提到了这件事，她在信中担心再婚离婚这件事一定会在后世被讥笑，她希望智者能够阻止他人的诽谤，于是就这样悄悄地进入了老年。
于是到现在，我们就能够真正地读懂她写于晚年的《声声慢》了。那就让我们再读一遍：
寻寻觅觅，冷冷清清，凄凄惨惨戚戚。乍暖还寒时候，最难将息。三杯两盏淡酒，怎敌他、晚来风急？雁过也，正伤心，却是旧时相识。
满地黄花堆积，憔悴损，如今有谁堪摘？守着窗儿，独自怎生得黑？梧桐更兼细雨，到黄昏、点点滴滴。这次第，怎一个愁字了得！
这下终于能读懂了吧？
李清照的经历，可能很多人都不清楚。我之所以在前面说的比较仔细，是想借此来表达几项文化的特性。
第一项文化特性是：一些世界的谣传，看起来黑云森森，其实都是瞬息烟尘，因此千万不要为了悠悠之口而心神不宁，文化最终的声誉在于作品。
第二项文化特性是：最大的悲痛，在作品中也要保持分寸，让更多的读者都能够感应，一旦感情夸张，那就无法踏入文学之门。
第三项文学特性是：即使在混乱和沮丧中，也能提炼出第一流的审美范型，传之永恒。
这是李清照的经历，给我们带来在文化特性上的三项启示。
transcriptEn:
Hello everyone, my name is Yu Qiuyu.
Yesterday we talked about the second aspect of Song Dynasty culture, which is called two high-ranking cultural officials: Wang Anshi and Sima Guang. Everyone must have discovered that these two people have done a thrilling and top-notch work on the gentleman personality of Chinese culture. Administratively they failed, but culturally they succeeded
,
The greatest success is that they pushed cultural personality into history and shocked history.
Think about it, everyone. Last time I talked about Su Dongpo, a cultural all-rounder in the Song Dynasty, plus these two high-ranking cultural officials: Wang Anshi and Sima Guang. With just these three people, the culture of the Song Dynasty is already very vibrant, but we are definitely not done yet, because there are still some very wonderful personality models.
As I mentioned earlier, Wang Anshi and Sima Guang were able to reach the pinnacle of state administration because of a special civil service system in the Song Dynasty. This civil service system certainly excites us, but it also brings great disadvantages. One of them is to seriously weaken the military strength. Coupled with the increasing corruption of the court and the high-pressure Song Dynasty, some words that were least wanted to be heard often came to the ears of the government and the public.
What words? For example: being attacked, defeated, captured, and begging to surrender have become frequently used words in the history of the Song Dynasty. Later, even the two emperors Song Huizong and Song Qinzong became prisoners, and had to move the capital to Lin'an and changed it to the Southern Song Dynasty. After the name was changed to the Southern Song Dynasty, there were still many crises.
Many books have written about this history, so I won’t repeat it. I just want to tell you that amidst the misery of military defeats, Chinese culture has chosen heroism, and the heroic land is more heroic than the soldiers.
Moreover, this kind of cultural heroism is not a slogan or a bluff, but it is melted into a superb aesthetic personality and becomes real literature. So the next part of our lecture will be "Three War Poets". Let’s review: a cultural all-rounder, two high-ranking cultural officials, and three war-torn poets.
The first war poet I am going to talk about will definitely surprise everyone. Because at first glance
,
Her works have almost no sword spirit, but are full of infinite elegance.
,
She is the poetess Li Qingzhao.
How could Li Qingzhao become a war poet? Because she expresses the extreme difference between peace and war more clearly than anyone else, and writes about the psychological feelings of the most elegant oriental woman when her family is destroyed, her family is destroyed, and she is fleeing from chaos. An indescribable sadness has become a spiritual lever that can stir up the great suffering and sorrow of a generation. This is also a pride of Song Dynasty literature. In the rainy evenings during the war, China's first female poet quietly stood up.
absurd escape
Speaking of Li Qingzhao, at the beginning, we must connect it with the two senior cultural officials I mentioned earlier, because after Sima Guang denied Wang Anshi's reforms, and later the two died one after another, a complicated party struggle formed. In this party struggle, Sima Guang was classified as a so-called Yuanyou party member, which was rejected by the new court. Li Qingzhao's father, Li Gefei, was also implicated in this list and was dismissed from office and exiled.
This happened when Li Qingzhao was still very young. This incident alone is already very sad, but what is even sadder is that the person handling this case is Zhao Tingzhi, the father of her newlywed husband Zhao Mingcheng, and the newlyweds have a very good relationship.
Li Qingzhao once wrote a letter to his father-in-law Zhao Tingzhi, hoping that he would take into account the face of his son and daughter-in-law's family. However, he did not expect that his father-in-law Zhao Ting would also be attacked by the court later. This chilling political atmosphere shows that the Northern Song Dynasty was already in a quagmire of mutual struggle. Under this situation, the Northern Song Dynasty obviously no longer had the power to deal with the surrounding hostile forces, let alone confront the Jin Kingdom in the north.
Li Qingzhao and her husband Zhao Mingcheng were unable to defend themselves against the heavy pressure on their father's reputation, so they had no choice but to return to their hometown of Qizhou, where they lived a quiet and elegant life for more than ten years. What we often read about the two of them writing poetry and enjoying antiques together in their lives is actually related to these more than ten years.
Zhao Mingcheng, Li Qingzhao's husband, was a well-known connoisseur, but he was in poor health and soon fell seriously ill. During his serious illness, a visitor from the north brought a stone pot to him for inspection. Zhao Mingcheng unfortunately passed away shortly after the inspection.
Immediately after his death, rumors arose that he dedicated a jade pot to the Kingdom of Jin in the north until his death. Because there was a fierce war between the Song and Jin Dynasties at that time, this rumor touched upon the so-called integrity issue that Chinese intellectuals like to talk about most, and extended from the integrity issue to the national justice of whether it was treason. In fact, it was an extremely fragile logic in troubled times.
But Li Qingzhao couldn't sit still. It was okay to frame himself, but he actually framed her husband who had just passed away. How could he tolerate this? She knew very well that this was the worst little rumor. Because the pot was brought by a northerner, he thought it was a jade pot. When Zhao Mingcheng saw it was a stone pot, the man took it back. And that person is only from the north, so why is he related to politics?
But in the face of the fierce public opinion, Li Qingzhao knew that he could not explain clearly. Even if Zhao Mingcheng was still alive, he could not explain clearly. This is the characteristic of rumors, especially political rumors.
Li Qingzhao is determined to use all her strength to clear her beloved late husband's reputation, but she doesn't know how to clear it. After much deliberation, our most honest female poet came up with the clumsiest method, which was to take all the antique cultural relics that the couple had collected over the years and follow the Emperor Zhao Gao of the Song Dynasty. Zhao Gao happened to be chased by the Jin soldiers at the time, so he fled with him.
She used such a clumsy way to illustrate a simple truth:
The Song Dynasty was already on the run, and I was willing to follow the imperial court with all my antiques and cultural relics, and I was even willing to dedicate them all to the imperial court. So why did my husband have second thoughts before the Song Dynasty fled? How could you give a pot to the Kingdom of Jin?
She established such a reluctant logic, a logic that is very touching. There were a lot of antiques and cultural relics, and the journey was very difficult. Loading and unloading were very hard. Our poor Li Qingzhao had to work hard every day to escort them and chase the imperial court's escape route.
In fact, the panicked court had no idea that such a woman, such a pile of goods, and such painstaking efforts were following behind her, let alone that she was going to use this method to clear her family's reputation and her husband's reputation.
This is the long journey of Li Qingzhao's life: fleeing, fleeing, fleeing, holding on to her husband's reputation and all his treasures, forever landing in the cracks of war. Her lyrics are just a gentle breath on the long journey, so she became a real war poet.
When Emperor Gaozong of the Song Dynasty fled along the southeastern coast, he once lived in panic on a sea ship, with poor Li Qingzhao following far behind. It went from today's Shaoxing to today's Ningbo, then passed through Fenghua and Taizhou to the sea, and then returned to Shaoxing through Wenzhou. Song Gaozong's journey was very embarrassing, but Li Qingzhao's journey was very absurd.
Why would she make such a ridiculous choice? I think there may be only one answer: because she is a poet, and a single female poet.
miserable old age
Finally, thank God, Li Qingzhao, who was extremely tired, found a relative with a clear mind on the road. The relative strongly advised her to end this meaningless wandering immediately. In fact, Li Qingzhao really couldn't walk anymore. She listened to this relative's words, but after taking stock of the cultural relics she brought with her, she had lost most of them along the way. At this time, the female poet Li Qingzhao was already nearly 10 years old
50
, which was considered a very old age at the time, and she finally wanted to stop.
She suddenly discovered that she used to travel every day not only to catch up with the court, but also to escape from overall thinking. Now that there is no need to catch up, you can just think about it carefully. When she thought about it, she couldn't help but shake her head and sigh. Since her youth, her father's reputation, her father-in-law's reputation, and her husband's reputation have been tormenting her for most of her life. Now that I think about it, how significant is it?
The so-called reputation only appears in the minds of others, but where are those others now? Do they remember? Moreover, all these reputations are related to the imperial court. Now that even the imperial court cannot find its own reputation, how can we distinguish right from wrong with the imperial court? After much thought, Li Qingzhao decided to bid farewell to the past and live a stable life.
In the Song Dynasty, if such a lonely woman wanted to live a relatively stable life, she should find a home, an ordinary home.
At that time, there happened to be an army financial officer who had been proposing to me. She thought she was not too young, so she agreed. Of course she knew that at that time, an upper-class woman who came from an official family and had a deep relationship with her deceased husband, who was nearly fifty years old, would definitely be criticized and ridiculed by the society if she remarried. But Li Qingzhao now takes reputation very lightly and decides to go his own way.
At this juncture, she showed a kind of courage that was as desperate as breaking the boat. If things only ended there, that would be fine. Li Qingzhao could have closed the door and lived an ordinary and stable life with her new husband. But I never expected that this husband turned out to be a delinquent.
With the eyes of a profiteer, he set his sights on the few antique cultural relics that Li Qingzhao had left during his escape. The so-called marriage was just a means of fraud. When he got the antique cultural relics, he immediately punched and kicked Li Qingzhao and abused him in every possible way. The name of this profiteer is Zhang Ruzhou. You are the "female" with a female on the edge of the water at three o'clock, and Zhou is the "boat" of Zhoushan.
Li Qingzhao, who was really pitiful to the extreme, would not reveal his family scandal to the outside world as long as there was still a little room for tolerance. But after all, she knows the preciousness of life, and knows that kindness and nobility should not be buried in evil. So just three months after getting married, she appealed to the government for divorce.
Li Qingzhao knew that there was a strange law in the Song Dynasty. If a wife sued her husband, even if the husband was really guilty, the wife would be imprisoned by the government for a while, but Li Qingzhao would rather be imprisoned than get a divorce. As a result, the divorce was finalized, Zhang Ruzhou was questioned, and Li Qingzhao was imprisoned. Fortunately, with the help of relatives, she was not imprisoned for too long.
Later, in order to protect Li Qingzhao's reputation, many scholars denied that Li Qingzhao had ever remarried and divorced. But this is a kind of good intention, which can hardly cover up the records we have seen of people like Li Xinchuan, Wang Zuo, Hu Zai and Zhao Gongwu. And we can also read a letter written by Li Qingzhao to relatives, in which she also mentioned this matter. In the letter, she worried that remarriage and divorce would be ridiculed in future generations. She hoped that wise men could prevent others from slandering her, so she quietly entered old age.
So now, we can truly understand "Slow Voice" which she wrote in her later years. So let’s read it again:
Searching and searching, deserted and miserable. It is most difficult to breathe when it is warm and then cold. How can three cups and two glasses of light wine defeat him, who comes late and is in a hurry? The wild geese are passing by, and I am sad, but it is an old acquaintance.
The yellow flowers are piled up all over the ground, and they are haggard and damaged. Who is worthy of picking them now? Watching the window, how can you be alone in darkness? The phoenix trees are covered with drizzle, and it rains bit by bit at dusk. This time, how could there be such a thing as "sorrow"!
Can you finally understand it now?
Li Qingzhao’s experience may not be clear to many people. The reason why I said it more carefully before is because I want to express several cultural characteristics.
The first cultural characteristic is: some rumors in the world may seem like dark clouds, but they are actually all fleeting smoke and dust. Therefore, do not worry about what you say. The ultimate reputation of culture lies in its works.
The second cultural characteristic is: the greatest sorrow must be measured in the works so that more readers can feel it. Once the emotions are exaggerated, it will be impossible to enter the door of literature.
The third literary characteristic is: even in chaos and frustration, it can refine first-class aesthetic models and pass them on to eternity.
This is Li Qingzhao’s experience, which brings us three enlightenments on cultural characteristics.

summary.gistZh: 李清照作为中国历史上最伟大的女词人，其作品展现了绝顶的文学才华、对爱情与家国命运的深刻体验，以及不让须眉的骨气与独立人格。
summary.gistEn: Li Qingzhao, China's greatest female poet, demonstrated unsurpassed literary genius, profound reflection on love and national fate, and extraordinary personal fortitude.

highlights.zh: 文学史上的奇迹：突破封建时代对女性的压抑，以极高艺术成就跻身宋词最高巅峰。
highlights.en: A Historical Miracle: Shattering feudal constraints on women, reaching the absolute pinnacle of Song Dynasty Ci poetry.

highlights.zh: 前期与后期的转折：前期闺情清丽缠绵，后期国破家亡后词风变为苍凉悲壮、沉郁顿挫。
highlights.en: Artistic Evolution: Early works capture luminous love and joy; later poetry transforms into tragic, haunting elegies after war and exile.

highlights.zh: 不让须眉的骨气：「至今思项羽，不肯过江东」，对妥协偏安的南宋统治者提出最犀利的批判。
highlights.en: Heroic Fortitude: Lines like 'Still missing Xiang Yu, who refused to retreat across the River' offered fierce criticism of cowardly court appeasement.

highlights.zh: 独立人格典范：晚年宁可坐牢也要与人品卑劣的丈夫离婚，展现了中国女性罕见的尊严与勇气。
highlights.en: Model of Independence: In old age, she endured imprisonment rather than remain married to a corrupt husband, proving rare dignity and courage.
