transcriptZh:
大家好，我是余秋雨。根据昨天的预告，今天要讲宋代的生活方式了，这个作为我们讲宋代文化的一个基础，一个背景。
在讲宋代的生活方式的时候呢，我们首先要把它与我们曾经高度赞扬过的唐代的生活方式作对比。
我们前面不是多次提到唐代东市的一场大火烧掉了多少店铺吗？那么宋代清明上河图里边的汴京一带的商业景象，如果拿出来一比,长安的西市和东市就太局促了。毕竟没有唐代这样的坊，没有这样的限制，而是完全开放，自由流通。
仅仅是手工业，汴京的手工业就比长安多了四倍，记住，四倍。作为农业大国，宋代的水稻种植面积比唐代扩大了整整一倍，种植的技术更是迅速提高。江浙一带的水稻的亩产量已经达到了八九百斤。蚕桑丝织，瓷器的烧制，我们说什么窑什么窑的烧制更是进入了高度专业化的生产阶段，产量和质量都突飞猛进。
那么，城市又怎么样呢？仅仅在北宋，城镇的总量已经接近2000，而城市人口已经占到全国总人口的12%，就是在宋代，中国人口突破了一亿大关。根据已故的美籍历史学家黄仁宇先生的统计，宋代当时的商品流通量如果要折合成我们现在国际间的价格，大概已经到了60亿美金到70亿美金。毫无疑问，中国宋代的经济水平是当时的世界之最。
宋朝的精神文化基调
生活方式的拓展和提升，也必然地带动了精神价值的拓展和提升。
宋代在科学技术上的创造力达到了整个中国古代史的顶峰，让国际间一切研究人类科技史的专家称颂不已。我可以随口讲几点了，比如，是宋代把雕版印刷推进到了活字印刷，宋代把火药用于战争，宋代把指南针用于航海，这些技术都相继传到西方，极大地推动了人类的文明进程。
在宋代还出现了一系列重要的科学技术著作，像沈括的《梦溪笔谈》、秦九昭的《数书九章》、苏颂的《新仪象法要》、王唯一的《铜人腧穴针灸图景》等等,各门学科出现了一派认真研究的专业气象。
我本人在30多年前写作中国戏剧史的时候，曾经花费很多时间研究宋代的市井生活，因为我研究的中国戏剧的起点和市井生活有关。因此在研究的过程当中，我仔细地阅读了《东京梦华录》、《都城纪胜》、《梦粱录》、《武林旧事》等等著作。
知道北宋都城汴京和南宋都城临安，已经是一个非常精致的市民社会。在这个市民社会当中，教育也突破了唐代后期的门阀权势，出现了平民化、普及化的趋势。科举制度更是扩充了规模。总的说来，宋代是中国古代史当中文化教养最高的朝代。这我再说一遍，在整个中国古代史当中，宋代的文化教养最高。
说到这里，我又要作一番国际比较了。宋代历史300多年，这个期间西方依然陷落在中世纪的漫漫荒路当中，只有意大利佛罗伦萨的几条由坚硬的鹅卵石铺成的街道上，开始出现了一点市民社会的清风。
我后来是一次次走在这些鹅卵石的街道上，想着中西对比的历史。在南宋王朝最终结束的那一年，被称作欧洲中世纪最后一个诗人的但丁只有14岁。直到170年后，文艺复兴的第一位大师达芬奇才诞生，由文艺复兴兴起的欧洲社会的大变革，更是以后的事情了。
我将时间这么一排大家就知道了，中国宋代，欧洲还无可比较。
但是宋代如此精彩，却好像给我们种印象，就在集体的文化人格上，不太昂扬。生活虽然很好，却严重的缺少安全感。四周的战事频频，而且败仗居多，国势国运明显的失落了天地元气。这种整体态势使很多文化人不可能像盛唐时候那样朝气蓬勃，他们普遍出现了一种忧患、内向、自为的状态。
在这么一种状态当中呢，文化显得稳重沉着，已经告别了青春气息，进入了中年时代。我做个比喻，只要是宋代人的创造，即使出于青年人之手，创造的作品总是带有细细皱纹的成熟的表情。
我必须补充这么一个情况，就是处于迷惘和忧患中的宋代文化人，又得到了朝廷格外的尊重。宋朝很奇怪，它一开始就重视文官胜于武将，立下规矩不杀文官，给文官以空前的薪酬待遇。这个薪酬待遇照我看来也是绝后的，而且宋代还可以让最高阶位的文人担任最高阶位的官职，这我后面要讲到。
这一切使宋代文人和朝廷缩短了心理距离，再加上朝廷常常在外部征战当中精疲力尽、手忙脚乱，那更使文化人产生了某种同情心理和介入心理。
因此，在宋代很少有文化上的极端诉求，基本上处于自由、自立、自在的境界，这很让其它时代的文化人羡慕。那种宋代在不太强悍的情况下的自由自立自在的这种状况，后来随着社会危机的加深，出现了一些强悍的人格力量，而且体现在一些强悍的诗人身上，这我慢慢要讲到。但是总体说来，宋代的生活是不错的。
我看到经常有人来问近代的文化人，如果你们把历史都放在眼前的话，你们愿意生活在哪个朝代，或者愿意生活在什么地方？欧洲的汤恩比他说，他非常希望能够生活在塔里木河边上。我听到更多老一代的中国文人都说愿意生活在唐代，但是在我看来，文化人生活最好的是宋代。
比较起来，唐代虽然是意气风发，但是就生活而言，它还没有摆脱经济基础的薄弱，他还没有摆脱这样一个很变动的不安定。宋代，尽管大环境经常有一种威胁感，但是就日子而言，唐代打下了基础，物质条件有了，生活方式也慢慢的建立了，所以日子是过的特别的自在，特别的和谐。
好，我们讲了宋代的生活方式，也讲了宋代的精神基调，那么我们就可以认真地来讲一讲宋代的文化成就到底表现在哪些方面？
宋朝的文化成就
宋代的文化成就是说不尽的，实在是太多了。那么我着重想给大家讲三个方面，请大家记一记。这三个方面我要用一二三来表达：
1. 一位文化全才
2. 两位文化高官
3. 三位战乱诗人（在战乱当中写诗的人）
这一二三的结构，只要是稍稍熟悉宋代文化的人，基本上就要猜出我要讲谁了，好，我就慢慢地讲下去。
先讲第一项，一位文化全才。对，你们都猜出来了，我讲的是苏东坡。
苏东坡对于宋代的重要性，怎么说都不为过。我甚至于可以用一个想象中的虚拟场景来说明。我们设想哪一天九天之上要评一下中国文化史的顶级高峰，要求非常严。那么每个朝代的代表一定会发出激烈的争吵，因为名额很少。
为什么要争吵呢？因为仅仅一个名字就会决定那几百年是否有公认的荣耀，争吵到最后，声音就会越变越小。因为明确的等级出现了，先秦是屈原，秦代没有，汉代是司马迁，魏晋是陶渊明，唐代有两个：李白、杜甫，那么宋代，就是苏东坡。就他一个人就能把宋代的文化等级大大拉高，使宋代变得无愧于整个文化史的任何一个段落了。
请大家注意，每一个朝代文人很多，优秀文人也能够数出一批。但是能够让这个朝代获得百世骄傲的，往往只有一个名字，也可能完全找不到这样一个名字。有反讽意义的是，那些找不到名字的朝代，在文化上往往显得特别热闹。
更反讽的是，那个被公认的能够为整个朝代带来百世骄傲的名字，仔细一看，总在受苦、总在被流放。这在屈原、司马迁、陶渊明、李白、杜甫身上我们已经看到，苏东坡当然也不会成为例外。
对于苏东坡我写过不少文章，很多人都读过。有的读者告诉我，我写苏东坡的那些句子，他们都抄在纸上，放在写字台玻璃板底下，这个情景我倒是多次亲眼看到。
台湾《中国时报》的创办人，已故的余纪忠先生，在生前亲自告诉我，他在读了我的《苏东坡突围》以后，再去根据我文章里边的介绍，去读了林语堂先生写的苏东坡传，他表示同意我对林语堂先生的批评。而星云大师竟然亲自指令，把我写苏东坡的文章转载在佛教刊物上。那么长，佛教刊物居然全登了。
我说东坡的那些话，在华人世界的影响确实比较大。比如有一次我到马来西亚吉隆坡远郊的一家小餐厅里吃饭，居然有个服务员也是我的读者，很长时间和我讨论苏东坡在思想上真正成熟的时间是什么时候。
由此可见，苏东坡直到今天还是庞大的中国文化领域的通关密码，一讲苏东坡，整个学中文的人都能够兴奋起来。对于苏东坡这个人格形象，我今天没法讲很多，但是我在《中国文脉》里边有一段话想给大家朗读一下，这可以概括我今天要讲的那个意思了。
我是这样写的：
苏东坡是一个文化全才，诗、词、文章、书法、音乐、佛理都非常精通，尤其是词赋、散文、书法这三样，都可以雄视千年。 但是苏东坡对中国文化最大的贡献，是留下了一个快乐而可爱的人格形象。
中国历史上的多数的文化巨匠大多是可敬有余，可爱不足，从屈原、司马迁到陶渊明都是如此，它们的可敬毋庸置疑。但他们可爱吗？没有足够的资料可以证明。
诗写得很好的曹操太具有威慑感，当然挨不到可爱的边。魏晋名士中，不少人应该是可爱的，但他们过于怪异，过于固执，过于孤傲，我们可以欣赏他们的背影，却很难与他们随和地交朋友。
到唐代，以李白为首的诗人一定是可爱的，但那时候诗风浩荡，他们常常成为众人瞩目的红人，而红人总是很难保持可爱，因为他们身边常常有喧哗的声音，使他们变得不是非常正常。
谁料到，到了宋代出现了这么一个有正常体温和正常表情的苏东坡。不管是悠久的历史、辽阔的天宇、个人的苦恼，到了他笔下都有了一种美好的诚实，让读者每个人都能产生感应。他不仅可爱，而且可亲，成了人人心中的兄长、老友。这种情况在中国文化史上几乎绝无仅有。
因此苏东坡是一种人格奇迹，以一种最诚实最可爱最正常的人格，打通了所有华人读者的集体人格，这就是奇迹所在。
这是我在中国文脉当中写的一段话，但是苏东坡还没讲完，我们明天继续。
transcriptEn:
Hello everyone, my name is Yu Qiuyu. According to yesterday's preview, today we will talk about the lifestyle of the Song Dynasty. This serves as a basis and a background for us to talk about the culture of the Song Dynasty.
When talking about the lifestyle of the Song Dynasty, we must first compare it with the lifestyle of the Tang Dynasty, which we have highly praised.
Didn’t we mention many times before that a fire in the East Market of the Tang Dynasty burned down many shops? If we compare the commercial scene in Bianjing in the Qingming River Scene in the Song Dynasty, the West Market and East Market in Chang'an would be too cramped. After all, there was no such thing as the Tang Dynasty, and there were no such restrictions. Instead, it was completely open and free to circulate.
Just the handicraft industry, Bianjing's handicraft industry is four times more than that of Chang'an, remember, four times. As a major agricultural country, the rice planting area in the Song Dynasty doubled that of the Tang Dynasty, and planting technology improved rapidly. The rice yield per mu in Jiangsu and Zhejiang has reached 800 to 900 kilograms. Silk weaving and porcelain firing have entered a highly specialized stage of production, with both output and quality improving by leaps and bounds.
So, what about cities? In the Northern Song Dynasty alone, the total number of cities and towns was close to 2,000, and the urban population accounted for 12% of the country's total population. It was in the Song Dynasty that China's population exceeded 100 million. According to the statistics of the late American historian Mr. Huang Renyu, if the commodity circulation volume in the Song Dynasty were to be converted into our current international prices, it would have reached US$6 billion to US$7 billion. There is no doubt that the economic level of China's Song Dynasty was the highest in the world at that time.
The spiritual and cultural tone of the Song Dynasty
The expansion and improvement of lifestyle will inevitably lead to the expansion and improvement of spiritual values.
The scientific and technological creativity of the Song Dynasty reached the pinnacle of the entire ancient Chinese history, and has been praised by all experts in the world who study the history of human science and technology. I can talk about a few points casually. For example, it was the Song Dynasty that advanced woodblock printing to movable type printing, the Song Dynasty used gunpowder for warfare, and the Song Dynasty used compasses for navigation. These technologies were all spread to the West one after another, greatly promoting the progress of human civilization.
In the Song Dynasty, a series of important scientific and technological works also appeared, such as Shen Kuo's "Mengxi Bi Tan", Qin Jiuzhao's "Nine Chapters of Shu Shu", Su Song's "New Yixiang Fa Yao", Wang Weiwei's "Pictures of Acupuncture and Moxibustion on the Bronze Man's Acupoints", etc., and a professional atmosphere of serious research appeared in various disciplines.
When I was writing the history of Chinese drama more than 30 years ago, I spent a lot of time studying street life in the Song Dynasty, because the starting point of my study of Chinese drama was related to street life. Therefore, during the research process, I carefully read "Tokyo Menghua Lu", "Capital Records", "Mengliang Lu", "Old Martial Arts" and other works.
We know that Bianjing, the capital of the Northern Song Dynasty, and Lin'an, the capital of the Southern Song Dynasty, were already very sophisticated civil societies. In this civil society, education also broke through the power of the clans in the late Tang Dynasty, and showed a trend of civilianization and popularization. The imperial examination system even expanded its scope. Generally speaking, the Song Dynasty was the most culturally educated dynasty in ancient Chinese history. Let me say this again, in the entire ancient Chinese history, the Song Dynasty had the highest level of cultural education.
At this point, I have to make another international comparison. The Song Dynasty has a history of more than 300 years. During this period, the West was still trapped in the long and barren roads of the Middle Ages. Only a few streets paved with hard cobblestones in Florence, Italy, began to see a little breeze of civil society.
Later, I walked on these cobblestone streets again and again, thinking about the contrasting history between China and the West. In the year when the Southern Song Dynasty finally came to an end, Dante, known as the last poet in the European Middle Ages, was only 14 years old. It was not until 170 years later that Leonardo da Vinci, the first master of the Renaissance, was born, and the great changes in European society that emerged from the Renaissance would only happen later.
If I arrange the time in this way, everyone will know that the Song Dynasty in China and Europe are still incomparable.
However, the Song Dynasty is so wonderful, but it seems to give us the impression that the collective cultural personality is not too high-spirited. Although life is good, there is a serious lack of security. There are frequent wars all around, and most of them are defeated. The country's destiny has obviously lost its vitality. This overall situation makes it impossible for many cultural people to be as vigorous as they were during the heyday of the Tang Dynasty. They generally appear in a state of worry, introversion, and self-centeredness.
In such a state, culture appears stable and composed, saying goodbye to youthfulness and entering middle age. Let me make an analogy: as long as it is created by the people of the Song Dynasty, even if it is made by young people, the created works will always have a mature expression with fine wrinkles.
I must add that the intellectuals of the Song Dynasty, who were in confusion and distress, received special respect from the imperial court. The Song Dynasty was very strange. From the beginning, it valued civil servants more than military generals. It established rules not to kill civil servants and gave them unprecedented salaries and benefits. In my opinion, this salary package is also unprecedented, and the Song Dynasty also allowed the highest-ranking literati to hold the highest-ranking official positions, which I will talk about later.
All this shortened the psychological distance between the Song Dynasty scholars and the imperial court. In addition, the imperial court was often exhausted and in a hurry during external campaigns, which gave rise to a certain kind of sympathy and intervention among the intellectuals.
Therefore, there were few extreme cultural demands in the Song Dynasty, and they were basically in a state of freedom, self-reliance, and ease, which was the envy of cultural people in other eras. The situation of freedom and self-reliance in the Song Dynasty without being too strong. Later, as the social crisis deepened, some strong personality power appeared, and it was reflected in some strong poets, which I will talk about slowly. But overall, life in the Song Dynasty was good.
I see people often ask modern cultural people, if you put history before your eyes, which dynasty would you like to live in, or where would you like to live? Toynbee from Europe said that he very much hoped to live by the Tarim River. I have heard more Chinese literati from the older generation say they would like to live in the Tang Dynasty, but in my opinion, the best life for literate people was in the Song Dynasty.
In comparison, although the Tang Dynasty was high-spirited, in terms of life, it had not yet gotten rid of its weak economic foundation, and it had not yet gotten rid of such a volatile and unstable situation. In the Song Dynasty, although the general environment often had a sense of threat, in terms of life, the Tang Dynasty laid the foundation, the material conditions were established, and the lifestyle was slowly established, so life was particularly comfortable and harmonious.
Okay, we have talked about the lifestyle of the Song Dynasty and the spiritual tone of the Song Dynasty. Then we can seriously talk about what aspects of the cultural achievements of the Song Dynasty are manifested?
Cultural achievements of the Song Dynasty
The cultural achievements of the Song Dynasty are indescribable, there are simply too many. So I would like to focus on three aspects for you, please remember them. I will express these three aspects in terms of one, two and three:
1. A cultural all-rounder
2. Two senior cultural officials
3. Three war poets (people who wrote poetry during the war)
With this two-three structure, anyone who is slightly familiar with the culture of the Song Dynasty will basically be able to guess who I am going to talk about. Okay, I will go on slowly.
Let’s talk about the first item first, a cultural all-rounder. Yes, you have all guessed it, I am talking about Su Dongpo.
The importance of Su Dongpo to the Song Dynasty cannot be overstated. I can even use an imaginary virtual scene to illustrate. We imagine that one day, Nine Days will be able to comment on the top peak of Chinese cultural history, and the requirements are very strict. Then the representatives of each dynasty will definitely quarrel fiercely, because there are very few places.
Why quarrel? Because just a name will determine whether there is recognized glory in those hundreds of years, and the voice will become smaller and smaller in the end of the quarrel. Because clear grades appeared, Qu Yuan was in the pre-Qin Dynasty, but there was no one in the Qin Dynasty, Sima Qian was in the Han Dynasty, Tao Yuanming was in the Wei and Jin Dynasties, there were two in the Tang Dynasty: Li Bai and Du Fu, and in the Song Dynasty, it was Su Dongpo. He alone could greatly raise the cultural level of the Song Dynasty, making the Song Dynasty worthy of any paragraph in the entire cultural history.
Please note that there are many literati in each dynasty, and a number of outstanding literati can be counted. But there is often only one name that can make this dynasty proud for centuries, or such a name may not be found at all. Ironically, those dynasties whose names cannot be found often appear to be particularly lively culturally.
What's even more ironic is that the name that is recognized as being able to bring pride to the entire dynasty for centuries, if you look closely, you will see that he is always suffering and always being exiled. We have seen this in Qu Yuan, Sima Qian, Tao Yuanming, Li Bai, and Du Fu, and Su Dongpo will certainly not be an exception.
I have written many articles about Su Dongpo, and many people have read them. Some readers told me that they copied the sentences I wrote about Su Dongpo on paper and placed them under the glass plate of their desk. I have seen this scene with my own eyes many times.
The late Mr. Yu Jizhong, the founder of Taiwan's "China Times", personally told me during his lifetime that after reading my "Su Tungpo's Breakout", he then read Mr. Lin Yutang's biography of Su Tungpo based on the introduction in my article. He expressed his agreement with my criticism of Mr. Lin Yutang. However, Master Hsing Yun personally ordered that my article on Su Dongpo be reprinted in Buddhist publications. It's so long that it's published in all Buddhist publications.
What I said about Dongpo did have a greater impact in the Chinese world. For example, one time I went to eat in a small restaurant in the outskirts of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. There was actually a waiter who was also a reader of mine. He discussed with me for a long time when Su Dongpo truly matured in thought.
It can be seen that Su Dongpo is still the key to the huge Chinese cultural field to this day. Once Su Dongpo is taught, all Chinese students can get excited. I can't say much about the personality of Su Dongpo today, but there is a passage in "Chinese Context" that I want to read aloud to you. This can summarize what I want to talk about today.
This is what I wrote:
Su Dongpo was a cultural all-rounder. He was very proficient in poetry, poetry, articles, calligraphy, music, and Buddhism. Especially in poetry, prose, and calligraphy, he could be regarded for thousands of years. But Su Dongpo's greatest contribution to Chinese culture is that he left behind a happy and lovely personality.
Most of the cultural giants in Chinese history are more than respectable but not enough lovable. This is true from Qu Yuan and Sima Qian to Tao Yuanming. Their respectability is beyond doubt. But are they cute? There is not enough data to prove it.
Cao Cao, who wrote very good poems, was too intimidating, so of course he couldn't be considered cute. Many of the celebrities in the Wei and Jin Dynasties should be cute, but they are too weird, too stubborn, and too aloof. We can admire their backs, but it is difficult to make easy-going friends with them.
In the Tang Dynasty, poets headed by Li Bai must have been cute, but at that time the poetry was so powerful that they often became celebrities in the spotlight, and it was always difficult for celebrities to stay cute because there were often noisy voices around them, which made them abnormal.
Who would have expected that in the Song Dynasty, there would be such a Su Dongpo with normal body temperature and normal expression. Whether it is the long history, the vast sky, or personal troubles, there is a beautiful honesty in his writing that every reader can relate to. He is not only cute, but also amiable, and has become a brother and old friend in everyone's heart. This situation is almost unique in the history of Chinese culture.
Therefore, Su Dongpo is a miracle of personality. With the most honest, lovely and normal personality, he has opened up the collective personality of all Chinese readers. This is the miracle.
This is a passage I wrote in the Chinese context, but Su Dongpo hasn’t finished speaking yet. We will continue tomorrow.

summary.gistZh: 宋代创造了中国古代最精致、优雅、富有生活情趣的文明形态，将茶道、瓷器、金石学与文人审美推向了世界历史的巅峰。
summary.gistEn: The Song Dynasty birthed China's most exquisite, elegant lifestyle, elevating tea rituals, ceramics, antiquarianism, and scholarly aesthetics to global historic peaks.

highlights.zh: 生活美学的巅峰：点茶、焚香、插花、挂画「四般闲事」，将日常平淡生活升华为艺术享受。
highlights.en: Pinnacle of Living Aesthetics: Tea whisking, incense burning, flower arranging, and art appreciation transformed mundane life into fine art.

highlights.zh: 极简与典雅的审美：宋瓷（如汝窑）追求极简、素雅与温润，领先现代极简主义设计近千年。
highlights.en: Minimalist Elegance: Song ceramics (like Ru ware) embraced serene minimalism and subtle luster, anticipating modern design by 1,000 years.

highlights.zh: 市民文化与经济繁荣：取消宵禁，夜市繁华，清明上河图展现了充满活力的城市文明。
highlights.en: Vibrant Urban Civilization: Abolishing night curfews, thriving night markets—immortalized in the 'Along the River During the Qingming Festival' scroll.

highlights.zh: 陈寅恪的评价：「华夏民族之文化，历数千载之演进，造极于赵宋之世。」
highlights.en: Historian Chen Yinke's Tribute: 'The culture of the Chinese nation, evolving over thousands of years, reached its absolute zenith in the Song Dynasty.'

title: 罗素：中国文化的优点和中国人缺点
folderName: 19_罗素：中国文化的优点和中国人缺点
audioPath: 19_罗素：中国文化的优点和中国人缺点/audio.m4a
quoteCardPath: 19_罗素：中国文化的优点和中国人缺点/quote_card.jpg
transcriptZh:
大家好，我是余秋雨，我继续讲课。
上次我因为讲完了中国文化能够长寿的这个原因之后，我们对中国文化有一次整体扫描。在整体扫描的时候，我不能不感谢一个英国人，这个人叫罗素，他改变了我对自己立足的中国文化的一种立场，我必须要提提他。罗素在中国最糟糕的时候（1920年）来到了香港、上海、杭州、南京、长沙，最后是北京，他待了整整九个月。现在想起来，当时的中国真是叫国破家亡，什么都不行，到处都是列强，生活贫困到无与伦比的程度。
罗素在中国逗留了九个月，主要在北京，他在北京发表了五场正式的演讲。讲的都是他的专业，不知道下面听的人，希望在英国人那听到救国之道的人，能够听到什么？因为我看了一下他的题目，一场是《数理逻辑》，另外一场是《物的分析》，另外一场是《心的分析》，还有一场是《哲学问题》，最后一场叫《社会结构》。除了这些演讲以外，他还开了一些讲座，关于唯心论、因果论、相对论、万有引力等等。罗素的演讲不管听得懂、听不懂，当时中国的年轻人多么想改变中国的现实，所以听的人非常多，场场火爆。罗素的听众当中，有年轻的毛泽东和周恩来。
罗素在中国待了九个月，后来他说：“我在中国讲课后越来越发现，我从中国学到的东西比中国向我学的东西要多得多。我问了很多长期在中国讲学的西方学者，他们和我有同样的观点，什么观点呢？就是我们能向中国学的东西要多得多。”请注意，这是非常了不起的一种思维，因为中国当时到处是一片破败。
中国文化的知音
罗素在1922年出版那本《中国问题》，他一开头就说，“在今后两个世纪，不管中国是变好还是变坏，都对世界有决定性的影响。”那么决定性的影响是什么呢？罗素讲了一句很重要的话，他说，“不管中国还是世界，文化最重要。只要文化问题能够解决，无论中国采取什么样的政治体制和经济体制，我都接受。”这句话，我想再读一遍，他说，“不管中国还是世界，文化最重要，只要文化问题能解决，无论中国采取什么样的政治体制和经济体制，我都接受。”所以出于这样的高度呢，罗素成了中国文化的知音。
我以前读过好多西方学者论中国文化的著作，像布莱尼茨、歌德、伏尔泰、黑格尔、韦伯、斯宾格勒，有的评价高，有的评价低，但是让我感到最知心的是罗素。你看，他说了这句话，我当时读的时候心里一动，他说，“进步和效率使我们富强，却被中国人忽视了。但是在我们骚扰他们之前，他们还国泰民安。”我当时看的时候眼泪都掉下来了。他说：“进步和效率使我们富强，却被中国人忽略了。但是在我们骚扰他们之前，他们还国泰民安。”这是一个知心的、一个了解中国文化的整体相貌的、一个国际级的大师的语言。
他怎么得出这些结论的呢？他接触了好多具体的中国人。譬如，在1921年的初夏的一天，罗素在一批中国友人的陪同下，坐着轿子去登山。当时这个路完全不好走，只能坐轿子了。那天天气非常热，而且热得很突然，山道又很崎岖，所以轿夫们非常非常辛苦，终于爬到了最高峰，大家就休息一会儿。这些中国的轿夫坐成一排，拿出了烟管乐滋滋地抽烟，而且互相开玩笑，好像世界的外事在他们的笑声当中完全就无牵无挂了。罗素看着他们，心里想，如果这个事情换了别的国家，今天天气无预警地突然酷热，那些轿夫一定因为酷热难当、山道崎岖要增加小费。即使像自己这样的欧洲人，到了山上也不会一点没有牵挂，而一定会担心下山以后交通工具会怎么样。但中国人一有空闲就取笑逗乐，这实在是另一种文化。
由此想开去，他说：“我不管到任何地方，欧洲人首先会告诉你这个地方的交通设施、实用信息，而中国人告诉你的，一定不是最实用的事情。他会告诉你，古代有个诗人住在这里。”罗素当然不能简单地来裁定这样的事情，到底谁好还是谁坏，但是他很公平地感觉到，西方的文明并不是唯一的标准。下面这段话我读一下，大家听：
“白种人有强烈地支配别人的欲望，中国人却有不想统治他国的美德，正是这一美德使中国在国际上显得虚弱。其实，如果世界上有一个国家自豪地不屑于打仗，这个国家就是中国。如果中国愿意，它能够成为世界上最强大的民族。”
罗素说了我曾经在联合国那个世界文明大会上讲过的话，也就是中国的非侵略本性。但是罗素因为他是外来人，所以他可以跳开去用一种幽默的方式来讲。我如果这样讲呢，就显得太骄傲了，太过度了，所以我对罗素的这段话还要读一遍。他说：
“白种人有强烈地支配别人的欲望，中国人却有不想统治他国的美德。正是这一美德，使中国在国际上显得虚弱。其实如果世界上有一个国家自豪地不屑于打仗，这个国家就是中国。如果中国愿意，它能成为世界上最强大的民族。”
这是罗素讲的话，他认为中国由于不想侵略，所以他认为中国虚弱就是这么来的。但是如果中国愿意，就能够成为世界上最强大的民族。因为自豪，对自己文化的自豪，就自豪地不想打仗。
中国人的缺点
接下去我还想讲一讲，他对中国的各种各样的分析的一些点。他说：“中国是我接触过的最好的国家之一，现在受到列强如此虐待，我对这些列强发出最严重的抗议。中国人也有缺点，我因为他们对我们不薄，我不想掐他们的短处，这是为了真理，也是为了中国，我不能隐瞒。我在离开中国的时候，有个中国文人要我指出中国人的主要弱点。我讲了三点，他们不但不生气，而且认为我评判地比较恰当。”
罗素认为中国人有三种普遍的缺点，第一个缺点是贪婪，第二个缺点是胆小，第三个缺点是冷漠。他把贪婪看成是中国人的第一缺点，他说中国人除了少数人之外，很多人一有机会就贪污腐败，甚至为了很少的钱，都敢于去冒险。政界的人士接受贿赂，已经成为中国难以有力地抵抗列强的原因之一。他好心地希望，等到中国经济得到发展，道德水平也会随之提高。
罗素认为中国人的第二缺点是胆小，中国人能够被动地忍耐，缺乏主动地勇敢。在战争当中，常常两方面都不认真，没怎么打就溃不成军。他说，这对于爱好名誉的欧洲人来说，简直是不可想象的。但罗素说了这样的话以后，马上补充道：“我打听到了，这种战争都是军阀混战，雇佣并不卖力是可以理解的。如果中国人遇到真正的大灾难，他们还是必然可以勇敢的。”这是罗素讲的中国人第二缺点。
罗素讲的中国人的第三个缺点叫做冷漠。他说中国人缺少人道主义的冲动，很少去做慈善赈灾的事情。更不可原谅地是，在中国的街道上，如果一条可爱的狗被汽车撞伤了，多数路人都会觉得好笑。在民间，别人的灾难往往会激发快感，而不是同情。
除了这三点，罗素还分析了中国的其他一些毛病，譬如，缺少前进的动力和效率，司法的疲弱和混乱，爱面子等等。等到他离开的时候，他已经深切地感觉到中国的改革者们，试图改变中国的惰性所产生的无力感，并由此产生了自己置身于亿万中国人中，无可逃避的无奈感。但是直到这个时候，他对中国文化的基本面还是非常欣赏。
罗素讲到了中国文化的优点，又讲到了中国人的缺点，这对我的感受是很强烈的。好，谢谢，我下次再讲。
transcriptEn:
Hello everyone, I am Yu Qiuyu, and I will continue to lecture.
After I talked about the reason why Chinese culture can live long last time, we conducted an overall scan of Chinese culture. During the overall scan, I cannot but thank an Englishman named Russell. He changed my attitude towards the Chinese culture that I am based on. I must mention him. Russell came to Hong Kong, Shanghai, Hangzhou, Nanjing, Changsha, and finally Beijing during the worst time in China (1920), where he stayed for a full nine months. Now that I think about it, China at that time was really in ruins, with nothing going for it, foreign powers everywhere, and living in unparalleled poverty.
Russell spent nine months in China, mainly in Beijing, where he delivered five formal speeches. What he talks about is all about his profession. I wonder what the people listening below hope to hear from the British about how to save the country? Because I looked at his topics, one was "Mathematical Logic", another was "Analysis of Objects", another was "Analysis of Mind", another was "Philosophical Issues", and the last one was called "Social Structure". In addition to these lectures, he also gave some lectures on idealism, causality, relativity, gravity, etc. Regardless of whether Russell's speech was understood or not, the young people in China at that time wanted to change China's reality, so there were many people who listened to it, and the scene was very lively. Among Russell's audience were the young Mao Zedong and Zhou Enlai.
Russell stayed in China for nine months. Later he said: "After lecturing in China, I found more and more that I learned much more from China than China learned from me. I asked many Western scholars who had been lecturing in China for a long time. They had the same point of view as me. What point of view? That is, we can learn much more from China." Please note that this is a very remarkable kind of thinking, because China was in ruins everywhere at that time.
Chinese cultural confidant
When Russell published "The China Question" in 1922, he said at the beginning, "In the next two centuries, whether China gets better or worse, it will have a decisive impact on the world." So what is the decisive impact? Russell made a very important statement. He said, "Whether China or the world, culture is the most important. As long as cultural problems can be solved, no matter what political and economic system China adopts, I will accept it." I want to read this sentence again. He said, "No matter China or the world, culture is the most important. As long as cultural problems can be solved, no matter what political system and economic system China adopts, I will accept it." So because of this high level, Russell has become a confidant of Chinese culture.
I have read many works on Chinese culture by Western scholars, such as Breinitz, Goethe, Voltaire, Hegel, Weber, and Spengler. Some have high evaluations, some have low evaluations, but the one I feel most intimate with is Russell. You see, he said this sentence, and my heart moved when I read it. He said, "Progress and efficiency have made us rich and powerful, but they have been ignored by the Chinese. But before we harassed them, they returned to peace and prosperity." I shed tears when I read it. He said: "Progress and efficiency have made us rich and powerful, but they have been ignored by the Chinese. But before we harass them, they will return to peace and prosperity." This is the language of an intimate, an understanding of the overall appearance of Chinese culture, and an international-level master.
How did he come to these conclusions? He came into contact with many specific Chinese people. For example, one day in the early summer of 1921, Russell, accompanied by a group of Chinese friends, went hiking in a sedan chair. At that time, the road was not easy to walk at all, so we had to take a sedan chair. The weather was very hot that day, and the heat came very suddenly, and the mountain road was very rugged, so the bearers worked very hard. Finally, they climbed to the highest peak, and everyone took a rest. These Chinese bearers sat in a row, took out their pipes, smoked happily, and joked with each other, as if the foreign affairs of the world had no concern at all in their laughter. Russell looked at them and thought, if this happened in another country, and the weather suddenly became very hot without warning today, the bearers would have to pay more because of the unbearable heat and the rugged mountain roads. Even a European like me will not be without worries when we reach the mountain, but will definitely worry about what will happen to the transportation after going down the mountain. But Chinese people make fun of people whenever they have free time. This is really another culture.
Thinking about it, he said: "No matter where I go, the Europeans will first tell you the transportation facilities and practical information of the place. But what the Chinese tell you is definitely not the most practical thing. He will tell you that there was a poet who lived here in ancient times." Of course Russell cannot simply judge such things, who is good or bad, but he feels fairly that Western civilization is not the only standard. Let me read the following passage, and everyone listens:
"Caucasians have a strong desire to dominate others, but Chinese people have the virtue of not wanting to dominate other countries. It is this virtue that makes China appear weak internationally. In fact, if there is a country in the world that proudly disdains war, this country is China. If China is willing, it can become the most powerful nation in the world."
Russell said what I once said at the United Nations Conference on World Civilizations, that is, China's non-aggressive nature. But Russell, because he was an outsider, could step away and speak in a humorous way. If I say it this way, it would seem too proud and excessive, so I have to read Russell's passage again. He said:
"Caucasians have a strong desire to dominate others, but Chinese people have the virtue of not wanting to dominate other countries. It is this virtue that makes China appear weak internationally. In fact, if there is a country in the world that proudly disdains war, this country is China. If China is willing, it can become the most powerful nation in the world."
This is what Russell said. He believed that China was weak because it did not want to invade. But if China wants, it can become the most powerful nation in the world. Because of pride, pride in their own culture, they are proud and do not want to fight.
Disadvantages of the Chinese
Next, I would like to talk about some of his various analyzes of China. He said: "China is one of the best countries I have ever come into contact with. Now it is so mistreated by the foreign powers. I issue the most serious protest against these foreign powers. The Chinese also have shortcomings. Because they are not soft on us, I do not want to pinch their shortcomings. This is for the sake of truth and for China. I cannot hide it. When I left China, a Chinese scholar asked me to point out the main weaknesses of the Chinese people. I talked about three points. Not only were they not angry, but they thought my judgment was more appropriate."
Russell believes that Chinese people have three common shortcomings. The first shortcoming is greed, the second shortcoming is timidity, and the third shortcoming is indifference. He regards greed as the number one shortcoming of the Chinese people. He said that except for a few people, many Chinese people are corrupt whenever they have the opportunity, and even dare to take risks for a small amount of money. Acceptance of bribes by political figures has become one of the reasons why China cannot effectively resist foreign powers. He kindly hopes that when China's economy develops, its moral standards will also improve.
Russell believes that the second shortcoming of the Chinese is timidity. The Chinese can be passively patient and lack active courage. In war, both sides are often not serious, and the army is defeated without much fighting. He said that this was simply unimaginable to the reputation-loving Europeans. But after Russell said this, he immediately added: "I have heard that this kind of war is a melee between warlords, and it is understandable that people do not work hard. If the Chinese encounter a real catastrophe, they will still be brave." This is the second shortcoming of the Chinese people mentioned by Russell.
The third shortcoming of the Chinese people mentioned by Russell is called indifference. He said that Chinese people lack humanitarian impulse and rarely do charity and disaster relief. What is even more unforgivable is that if a cute dog is hit by a car on the streets of China, most passers-by will find it funny. Among civilians, other people's disasters tend to inspire pleasure rather than sympathy.
In addition to these three points, Russell also analyzed some other problems in China, such as the lack of motivation and efficiency, the weakness and chaos of the judiciary, the lack of face, etc. By the time he left, he had deeply felt the powerlessness caused by the inertia of China's reformers in trying to change China, and from this he felt an inescapable sense of helplessness among hundreds of millions of Chinese. But until this time, he still had a great appreciation for the fundamentals of Chinese culture.
Russell talked about the advantages of Chinese culture and the shortcomings of the Chinese people. This made me feel very strongly. Okay, thank you, I'll talk about it next time.

summary.gistZh: 英国哲学家罗素对中国文化进行了深刻客观的剖析，盛赞中国人的和平理性、幽默与忍耐，同时也尖锐指出了缺乏现代科技与效率的弱点。
summary.gistEn: British philosopher Bertrand Russell offered a profound, objective evaluation of Chinese culture—praising its peaceful rationality and humor, while warning of deficiencies in modern science and efficiency.

highlights.zh: 罗素的独特视角：作为西方智者，在1920年代造访中国，写下《中国问题》，给予中国文明极高敬意。
highlights.en: Russell's Unique Vision: Visiting China in the 1920s, the Western sage authored 'The Problem of China', offering immense respect for its civilization.

highlights.zh: 中国文化的极佳优点：崇尚和平、反对侵略扩张、富有生活幽默感、对自然的尊重与深沉的耐力。
highlights.en: China's Great Virtues: Love of peace, anti-expansionism, gentle humor in daily life, reverence for nature, and immense resilience.

highlights.zh: 历史缺陷与短板：缺乏现代科学逻辑、公共效率低下、面对工业强国侵略时过于软弱。
highlights.en: Historical Deficiencies: Lack of modern scientific logic, inefficient public administration, and vulnerability when facing industrialized aggression.

highlights.zh: 跨文化互补启示：西方需要学习中国的和平生活智慧，中国需要学习西方的科技与法治，双方互为救赎。
highlights.en: Cross-Cultural Complementarity: The West needs China's wisdom of peaceful living; China needs Western science and rule of law—each complementing the other.

title: 文化创新：让文化走在科技前面
folderName: 20_文化创新：让文化走在科技前面
audioPath: 20_文化创新：让文化走在科技前面/audio.m4a
quoteCardPath: 20_文化创新：让文化走在科技前面/quote_card.jpg
transcriptZh:
大家好，我是余秋雨。
中国文化的第四个弱项，就是对于前辈的迷思的这个问题，我还需要再讲一讲。我们有一些思维的弊病，经常干扰我们的思维。只要卷入到传统，卷入到遗产，我们的智商就会降低。
我的学生都记得，我在很多很多年以前曾经举过例子，我举的是上海崇明岛的例子，你如果不开放的话，就会以为我们这个岛最好，你问从来没有离开过崇明岛的人，你们的岛好在哪里？他说我们这冬天有什么花，春天有什么花，问来问去，和其他地方都差不多。但是由于它没有进行更大空间的比较，他把公共的东西当做了自己的特点，而自己的缺点又看不到。真正懂得这个崇明岛的人一定是走到了很远的地方，回来才发现自己这个岛的毛病和自己岛的美。
那么我们对于中国文化也应该成为这样的人，而不应该成为封闭式的岛屿文化。我们的传统都是好的，你完全经不起更大空间的对比。这个现在已经变成了一个实实在在的大问题了。
遗产与创新
我在台湾的一个非常好的朋友叫林怀民，他是国际有名的大舞蹈家。他给我讲一件事，他有一次和他的舞蹈团的其他艺术家一起坐出租车，在上海街上走的时候，就看到旁边的石库门房子，其中有两个人说，这个石库门房子如果能够保全保留下来就好了，没想到两台出租汽车的司机都把车停下了，说你们下去，你们为了文化，为了你们可以看，你知道石库门里面过什么日子？难道不能让我们上海人过好一点的日子？你知道里边是手提马桶吗？你知道里边没有煤气是煤球炉吗？你知道里边的房子都不隔音吗？结果，林怀民说我终于明白，文化不应该以牺牲当代生态作为代价，这讲得很好了。
林怀明是一个专门研究中国东方传统文化向世界各地传播的人，他都有了这个认识。所以我们要明白一点，我们现在对文化传统和文化遗产的认识，不能进入迷思。这里我需要讲一个理论上的问题，就是遗产的“遗”这个字，我们不要看成是蒙了灰尘的、发霉的、老朽的物件，千万不要。一件物体能够遗下来，而且遗下来的过程当中还要受人尊敬，表示它有强悍的生命力，它能够穿越时间，能够披荆斩棘，能够留存世间。因此，“遗产”这两个字不是老旧的象征，而是强大生命力的象征。
这个话很重要，我再讲一遍，“遗产”这两个字并不是老旧的、衰败的象征，而是强大生命力的象征。它和与它同时出现的事物相比，它的生命力要强过千万倍，仅仅只有它保留下来了，我们一定要知道这不是偶然因素，是因为它的优秀。所以我们在找遗产的时候，找的是里边的一种生命力，是一种前进的力量，而不是找到一种后退的力量。
文化遗产让我们产生有关人类足以笑傲历史的自信，笑傲的根源就是当初的创造力。所以请记住，它们既然能够把时间凿通，把人类的智慧凿通，那就是一种让我们感到必须敬仰的创造者的声音。所以，文化遗产这门课，应该是一门创新之课、高贵之课、品位之课，而不是老旧的课程，不是整天在摩挲着一些老旧的细节，把玩不已，这完全搞错了。文化遗产本身也会愤怒，也会怒吼，我不是这样的。你要找到里边让它能够传到今天还有可能创新的那些因素，这一定要注意。
科技创新与文化创新
大家知道吗？我讲这个课的时候，有一个非常重要的宣传话语。我说，中国文化是一条川流不息的万里长江，而不是江边的枯藤、老树、昏鸦。我还是坚持这个思维，我们因为川流不息，应该要着眼于明天，着眼于未来。在川流不息的过程当中，文化也能沉淀成河床，这个河床就是人格，就是我们的集体人格。我们一定要秉承中国文化强有力的生命力，一步步地往前走，如果还是停留在前辈迷思那个地方，问题就比较严重了。这个严重就是严重地制约了创新思维，严重地影响了国际形象。
请注意，好多人说我们的科技已经在创新了，文化落后点不要紧。现在中国有一个非常大的迷思，以为创新是科技的事情，文化就是保护传统，这完全不对。文化它的创新能力应该在科技创新之前，文化是一种集体的精神共识，如果精神共识都在传统，那么科技怎么可能创新？所以请记住，欧洲在进行近代化改革的时候，首先是文艺复兴，科技是在后面，文化首先必须创新。他们所谓的复兴并不是完全恢复古希腊、古罗马的文化，他们恰恰是一种根据古代话语所完成的一种重大创新工程。创新一定要走在前面，因为创新它是人类的一个基本思维的面向。面向可以创新的话，那么整个全社会就可以带动起来了。
如果我们讲到文化的时候，永远是古代的东西，永远是陈旧的东西，永远是保守的东西，那么我们的文化思维怎么可能全盘都上去呢？所以，“文化是保守的，科技是创新的”这个二元结构是长不了的，而且一定会破碎。所以在这个情况下，文化要保存是可以保存很多东西，我们也有能力，但是，文化的创新部分一定要很好地成长起来。如果老一代的文化人已经不可以了，那么我们新一代的文化人一定要以创新作为自己的主业。掉到传统和遗产的迷思当中的那些人呢，掉进去一会儿，希望你们能够早一点出来。我知道你们是爱国的，但是我相信会容易导致这么一个结果：
在抗日战争开始的时候，很多国学非常深的人，纷纷的都成了汉奸，这让我感到非常头疼；而在欧洲和美国的大道上，穿了一身西装，用漂亮的英语在那儿的街边喊“我的祖国受到侵略了，希望你们能够支持我们中国”的这些人，却是当年被大家说成是数典忘祖的人、满口学英语的人，他们很多是爱国者，包括当时东京大审判的法官，包括我们好多外交家都是这样的人，非常了不起。而到最后审判汉奸的时候，站在审判席上的人，好多都是穿着长袍马褂、过去素养非常高的人。所以在这个问题上，国家的荣耀一定和“创新”两个字有关，一定和国际化和开放有关，而恰恰不是那些老文具、那些老规则。
让文化后退，让科技前进，这条路是很难走的下去的。倒过来，让文化走到科技前面，成为一种非常好的创新力量，鼓动我们前进、前进、前进，创新、创新、创新，文化才有真正的力量。我们想想看，比我们的中华文化更年长的文化还有好几个，比如巴比伦文化，比如埃及文化，如果现在伊拉克的人老是拿着巴比伦时代的哲学家的话，来证明它伊拉克文化的光荣；如果埃及当代的文化人老是拿法老的预言，来说明埃及文化必须在当代世界出现他们新的地位，我们的心里是不是会有一点暗暗可笑？
过去的光荣真的不能代替今天和明天的价值，完全不能替代。如果我们能够把创新做好了，文化创新做好了，那么我可以讲，我们的屈原、我们的司马迁、我们的李白杜甫、我们的苏东坡都会高兴。如果我们老是讲他们而忘记了新的文化创新的话，他们一定会恼怒。
谢谢大家。
transcriptEn:
Hello everyone, my name is Yu Qiuyu.
The fourth weakness of Chinese culture is the issue of the myth of the predecessors. I need to talk about it again. We have some thinking defects that often interfere with our thinking. As long as we are involved in tradition and heritage, our IQ will decrease.
My students all remember that I gave an example many, many years ago. I gave the example of Chongming Island in Shanghai. If you don’t open up, you will think that our island is the best. If you ask people who have never left Chongming Island, what is good about your island? He asked us what kind of flowers we have in winter and what kind of flowers we have in spring. They are similar to other places. But because it did not make a larger space for comparison, it regarded public things as its own characteristics, while its own shortcomings could not be seen. Those who truly understand this Chongming Island must have traveled far away, only to discover the shortcomings and beauty of their own island when they came back.
Then we should be like this when it comes to Chinese culture, and should not become a closed island culture. Our traditions are all good, and you simply cannot stand the contrast of a larger space. This has now become a real big problem.
Heritage and Innovation
A very good friend of mine in Taiwan is called Lin Huaimin. He is an internationally famous dancer. He told me about an incident. He once took a taxi with other artists from his dance troupe. When walking on the streets of Shanghai, he saw the Shikumen house next to him. Two of them said that it would be great if this Shikumen house could be preserved. Unexpectedly, the drivers of the two taxis stopped the car and said, "Come down, you are here for culture, so that you can see it. Do you know what life is like in Shikumen?" Can’t we Shanghai people live a better life? Did you know there's a portable toilet in there? Did you know that there is no gas in it and it is a briquette stove? Did you know that the houses inside are not soundproofed? As a result, Lin Huaimin said that I finally understand that culture should not be at the expense of contemporary ecology. This is a very good point.
Lin Huaiming is a person who specializes in the spread of traditional Chinese oriental culture to all parts of the world, and he has this understanding. Therefore, we must understand that our current understanding of cultural traditions and cultural heritage cannot enter into myths. Here I need to talk about a theoretical issue, which is the word "legacy" in heritage. We should not think of it as a dusty, moldy, or decayed object. We must not. An object can be left behind, and it must be respected while being left behind, which means that it has strong vitality, can travel through time, overcome obstacles, and remain in the world. Therefore, the word "heritage" is not a symbol of obsolescence, but a symbol of strong vitality.
This word is very important. I will say it again. The word "heritage" is not a symbol of oldness and decay, but a symbol of strong vitality. Compared with the things that appeared at the same time, its vitality is tens of millions of times stronger. It is the only one that has been preserved. We must know that this is not an accidental factor, but because of its excellence. So when we are looking for heritage, we are looking for a kind of vitality in it, a force to move forward, rather than a force to retreat.
Cultural heritage gives us confidence that human beings can be proud of history. The root of pride is the original creativity. So please remember that since they can chisel through time and human wisdom, they are the voice of a creator that we must admire. Therefore, the course of cultural heritage should be a course of innovation, nobility, and taste, rather than an old course. It should not be about playing with some old details all day long. This is completely wrong. Cultural heritage itself can also be angry and roar, but I am not like that. You have to find those factors that make it possible to innovate even today, and you must pay attention to this.
Scientific and technological innovation and cultural innovation
Does anyone know? When I taught this class, I had a very important promotional message. I said that Chinese culture is an endless stream of the Yangtze River, not the dead vines, old trees, and dim crows on the riverside. I still stick to this thinking. Because we are constantly flowing, we should focus on tomorrow and the future. In the process of continuous flow, culture can also settle into a river bed. This river bed is personality, our collective personality. We must uphold the strong vitality of Chinese culture and move forward step by step. If we still stay in the place of the myths of our predecessors, the problem will be more serious. This seriously restricts innovative thinking and seriously affects the international image.
Please note that many people say that our technology is already innovating, and it does not matter if our culture is lagging behind. There is a very big myth in China now, that innovation is a matter of science and technology, and culture is about protecting tradition. This is completely wrong. The innovation ability of culture should precede technological innovation. Culture is a collective spiritual consensus. If the spiritual consensus is all in tradition, how can technology innovate? So please remember that when Europe is carrying out modernization reforms, the Renaissance comes first, science and technology comes later, and culture must first innovate. Their so-called revival is not a complete restoration of the culture of ancient Greece and Rome. They are precisely a major innovative project based on ancient discourse. Innovation must be at the forefront, because innovation is a basic aspect of human thinking. If the orientation can be innovative, then the whole society can be stimulated.
If when we talk about culture, we always talk about ancient things, always old things, always conservative things, then how can our cultural thinking be comprehensive? Therefore, the binary structure of "culture is conservative and technology is innovative" cannot last and will definitely be broken. So in this case, if culture needs to be preserved, a lot of things can be preserved, and we have the ability to do so, but the innovative part of culture must grow well. If the older generation of cultural people are no longer capable, then our new generation of cultural people must take innovation as their main business. For those of you who have fallen into the myth of tradition and heritage, fall in for a while, and I hope you can come out soon. I know you are patriotic, but I believe it will easily lead to this result:
At the beginning of the Anti-Japanese War, many people with profound Chinese studies became traitors one after another, which made me feel very troubled; but on the streets of Europe and the United States, I wore a suit and shouted in beautiful English on the street, "My motherland has been invaded, I hope "You can support us, China" are people who were said by everyone back then to be people who forgot about their ancestors and learned to speak English. Many of them were patriots, including the judges of the Tokyo Trial at that time, and many of our diplomats. They were such people. They were very remarkable. And when the traitors were finally tried, many of the people standing on the trial bench were wearing long robes and mandarin jackets and were very well-educated people in the past. So on this issue, the country's glory must be related to the word "innovation", to internationalization and openness, but not to those old stationery and those old rules.
Letting culture retreat and letting science and technology advance is a difficult path to follow. On the other hand, let culture come to the forefront of technology and become a very good force for innovation, encouraging us to move forward, move forward, move forward, innovate, innovate, innovate. Only then will culture have real power. Let’s think about it. There are several cultures that are older than our Chinese culture, such as Babylonian culture and Egyptian culture. If people in Iraq now always use the words of philosophers from the Babylonian era to prove the glory of Iraqi culture; if contemporary Egyptian cultural people always use the prophecies of Pharaoh to explain that Egyptian culture must assume its new status in the contemporary world, wouldn’t we feel a little secretly ridiculous in our hearts?
The glory of the past really cannot replace the value of today and tomorrow, not at all. If we can do a good job in innovation and cultural innovation, then I can say that our Qu Yuan, our Sima Qian, our Li Bai, Du Fu, and our Su Dongpo will all be happy. If we keep talking about them and forget about new cultural innovations, they will definitely be angry.
Thank you all.

summary.gistZh: 真正的文化创新不是被动跟在科技后面，而是让人文精神与文化伦理走在科技前面，为人工智能与技术时代提供方向与良知。
summary.gistEn: True cultural innovation does not passively trail tech; it positions humanistic ethics ahead of science, providing direction and conscience in the AI age.

highlights.zh: 文化与科技的关系：科技提供工具与效率，文化提供目的与灵魂；没有文化的科技可能导向毁灭。
highlights.en: Culture & Tech Synergy: Science supplies tools and speed, while culture provides purpose and soul; tech without humanities risks catastrophe.

highlights.zh: 让文化走在科技前面：在数字与AI革命中，必须先建立人文伦理规范，防范科技异化与心灵空虚。
highlights.en: Leading Science with Culture: In AI and digital revolutions, humanistic ethics must lead to prevent technological alienation.

highlights.zh: 创新不是摒弃传统：真正的创新是在深厚文明土壤上长出的新芽，而非切断历史根脉的狂妄破坏。
highlights.en: Innovation vs. Tradition: Authentic innovation is a fresh bloom from deep historical soil, not reckless destruction of cultural roots.

highlights.zh: 中华文化的当代使命：用「天人合一、中庸和谐」的东方智慧为全球科技伦理治理贡献力量。
highlights.en: China's Contemporary Mission: Contributing Eastern wisdom of harmony to global technological and ethical governance.

title: 新儒学：儒学的反思与转向
folderName: 21_新儒学：儒学的反思与转向
audioPath: 21_新儒学：儒学的反思与转向/audio.m4a
quoteCardPath: 21_新儒学：儒学的反思与转向/quote_card.jpg
transcriptZh:
大家好，我是余秋雨，我们继续讲课。
上次我们把佛教已经讲完了，按照我们的预期，应该在讲中国文化的集体人格的时候，先讲君子之道，然后佛教讲的是觉者的目标，君子，觉者，道家讲的是真人，这三个。所以，严格讲起来，我们要讲儒家，佛家和道家。
面对佛教产生的困惑，儒学转型的契机
儒家，君子之道，我花了很长时间，大家都听了。佛家我其实也已经讲完了，讲到禅宗，讲到上一次我已经讲完了，照理应该讲道家了。但是请等一等，佛教这样在中国轰轰烈烈的传播，好多人都投向了佛教，而且佛教展现出那么高的智慧，那么高的境界。这一点，中国的基本的思维毕竟还是儒家思维，因为国家需要治理，民间需要管理，在这种情况下面，完全是用出家的佛教，在中国这个社会当中，它不太可能成为真正的社会管理的主流。所以，儒家的思维者，面对了佛教的兴盛和人们对佛教的接受的程度，开始反思自己。
我们的君子之道，我们的修身、齐家、治国、平天下，我们一直非常非常喜欢的，而且坚守的我们的理念，遇到佛教以后，为什么我们就显得有点窝囊了？为什么那么多老百姓，他们都慢慢地走向了佛教，而渐渐地冷落了我们？而且，更麻烦的是，很多知识水平很高，早期接受儒家教育的智者，他们也渐渐地走向了佛教，而且在走向佛教的过程当中写出了很多美丽的文章，写出了很多美丽的诗歌。这一点儒家学者产生了深思，产生了动摇。
所以，我必须在讲道家之前，讲一讲儒家的动向，这一点非常重要了。儒家，我们不能把儒家就停留在孔子、孟子的时代，它后面因为在不断地在发展，不断地在弘扬，不断地在中国的社会管理和社会思维的起跌上，一直起着老家长的作用。但是，家长一代代在继承，这些管理着国家、管理着社会、管理着人心的这样的人，他们面对佛教的时候，一开始有抱怨，我前面讲到过，比如像韩愈，他很抱怨，还有很多人抱怨。问题是，时间一长，你抱怨，没用，因为这块土地已经被佛教渗透了，这么多人民已经接受了佛教了，佛教本身的思维能力也让那些高智商的智者，心里边打鼓了。
显而易见，有好多问题，是超越了我们儒教儒家的思维了，在这一点上呢，儒学产生了变革。这个就使我必须在讲道家之前，先要关照一下我们的儒学的变化，这一点也是我们中国思维领域里边的一个重大的动向。
儒家学者当中有两种人，一种是善于学习的，一种是不善于学习的。那善于学习的人呢，他们渐渐明白了，佛教的盛行正好暴露了儒学的短板。儒学张扬的是社会秩序，佛教探究的是人心的本性，社会秩序是统治者的课本，人心本性是一切人的疑问。社会秩序的课本一定会参照大量的权势者的意愿，而人心本性的疑问，却会启发天下众生的觉悟，这是不一样的。
既然如此，一直占据统治地位的儒学，能不能改变一下自己的身段，从外部获得更多的教益？但是，要儒学获得教益是一件麻烦的事情，因为它的历史很长，它的背景很宽，它的资源很多，它很难大幅度的转型。如果不是大幅度的转型，它能够获得的教益总是有限。大家理解吗？一个负载非常重的车，要叫它在路上大幅度的转型，难度很大，当时的儒学就是这个形态。它一直占据统治地位，它的学者很多，它的书籍很多，它的学校很多，让它转型难度很大，如果小小的转，那等于没转。如果大大的转，那由谁来转？这个司机是谁？这个问题就比较大了。
幸好，儒家学者当中还有一些杰出的明白人，而且不止一个两个。于是从唐代开始，尤其在宋明两代，儒学发生了重大的转型，就产生了新儒学。
我们现在讲新儒学，往往是指现在，我的朋友像杜维明教授啊，他们做的。不，在唐宋那个时候，已经有新儒学了。旧儒学的重点在于弘扬伦常秩序，新儒学的特点就是学佛教了，要挖掘人心的本性了。这毫无疑问是受到了佛教和禅宗的影响。大家想一想啊，老的儒学，主要是弘扬伦常秩序；新儒学学了佛教以后，它主要是挖掘人心本性，这肯定是受到佛教影响了。
儒学的转型：新儒学对禅宗的借鉴
新一代的儒家学者认为，社会秩序中的种种是非，关及一种比较抽象的本性。孔子、孟子很多话说的很好，但是它的这个社会秩序要维持，它的是非在哪儿？一定有一种性，这个性，性质的性，一定是和天有关。所以，儒家学者他们在《尚书》、在《左传》、在《孟子》里边，拼命地找各种有关天人之间的神秘关系的文句，进而就进一步深讨人世的起点和归结。这种研究呢，旧的儒家学者兴趣是不大的，就是研究天和人之间的神秘关系，探究人世的起点和终点，孔子、孟子和老一代的传统儒学，他们兴趣不大的；但是在新儒学当中，却突飞猛进。
新儒学既然在研究那种问题了，就研究与天有关的各种各样的有关人世的起点和归结，但是和禅宗仍然有极大的差别。在外部看起来，研究这些高深学问的新儒家，也不光后来叫理学还是心学，看上去都显得很严肃，很沉重，很吃力；而禅宗却一直是这样的轻盈、波俏、干脆。为什么会这样呢？因为新儒家里边的理学和心学，总是想识别天下的是非善恶，总是在一刀一刀的来切割是非。那禅宗呢，却没有意识要来分割，没有心思要去识别，所以它就显得特别轻松。
对这个问题，我觉得我们不能嘲笑那些新儒学的学者，他们处于非常艰苦转型中这样的一种思维的危机阶段，他们一直秉持着一系列社会责任感，也秉持着一些社会理想，这是他们的安身立命之本。因此，无论他们想得多么玄妙，想得多么高深，想得多么虚幻，他们也不可能脱空而去，反而他们会回过头来，面对佛教禅师们，做出他们的思考。
禅师们可以非常轻松地在山顶想着那些自由自如的问题，但是我们的新儒家的学者们，他们很难放弃社会责任，很难放弃人间理想，他们很难放弃自己安身立命之本。他们会问禅师，你们的那些机锋、那些顿悟，妙是非常妙，普天下到底有多少人能够真正领会呢？如果你们永远局限于在山巅上、在白云间的少数智者，那么佛里所说的引渡众生，又怎么完成呢？
请大家注意一个问题，儒家学者在这个问题上的提问，实在是有点道理的。你们的禅宗，你们的佛理，你们的顿悟，你们的机锋，当然是非常高妙，但是普天下有多少人能够领会？如果这一切只能属于山巅上白云间的极少数的智者，那么，山脚下呢，那么多你们要引渡的众生怎么来引渡呢？平心而论，儒家学者觉得，这种问题有一点义正词严，因为这是一大群中国的士子，他们的精神自守，我们只能直面，很难指责。
我们想一想，包括我、包括我的很多朋友，其实都是其中的一员。我们有社会责任，我们有人间理想，我们关心着很多很多实实在在大众，而不是佛教比较空洞的讲的是，引渡终生。我们想的是社会街道上的各种各样的具体的人，乡村田麦间的各种各样的人，我们想到是这个。怎么来解决呢？所以，这个问题呢，儒家学者的提问实在是有一定道理的。
我本人也非常能够理解他们的思维，只不过我稍微有点特殊，因为我对魏晋名士特别怀念，而且由于对艺术美学的投入，对于禅宗，就有一种迷醉毕生的那种艺术思维的沟通的能力。对我来说，我因魏晋而靠近艺术，我因为禅宗而靠近我的天性，总的说来是比较能够接受佛教的禅宗，正因为这样，我站在这个立场上来看新儒学，立场比较客观。
谢谢！
transcriptEn:
Hello everyone, I am Yu Qiuyu, let’s continue the lecture.
We have finished talking about Buddhism last time. According to our expectations, when talking about the collective personality of Chinese culture, we should first talk about the way of the gentleman. Then Buddhism talks about the goal of the enlightened person, the gentleman, the enlightened person, and Taoism talks about the real person, these three. So, strictly speaking, we have to talk about Confucianism, Buddhism and Taoism.
Facing the confusion caused by Buddhism, the opportunity for the transformation of Confucianism
Confucianism, the way of a gentleman, I spent a long time and everyone listened to it. I have actually finished talking about Buddhism, and when it comes to Zen Buddhism, I have already finished talking about it last time, so logically I should talk about Taoism. But please wait a minute. With the vigorous spread of Buddhism in China, many people have turned to Buddhism, and Buddhism shows such high wisdom and high realm. In this regard, China's basic thinking is still Confucian thinking after all, because the country needs governance and the people need management. In this case, it is entirely possible to use monastic Buddhism. In Chinese society, it is unlikely to become the mainstream of real social management. Therefore, Confucian thinkers began to reflect on themselves when faced with the rise of Buddhism and people's acceptance of Buddhism.
Our gentleman's way, our self-cultivation, family management, country governance, and world peace, we have always liked and adhered to our ideas very much. Why do we seem a bit useless after encountering Buddhism? Why are so many ordinary people slowly moving towards Buddhism and gradually neglecting us? What’s more, what’s even more troublesome is that many wise men with high levels of knowledge and early Confucian education gradually moved toward Buddhism, and in the process of moving toward Buddhism, they wrote many beautiful articles and poems. This point caused Confucian scholars to think deeply and waver.
Therefore, before I preach about Taoism, I must talk about the trends of Confucianism. This is very important. Confucianism, we cannot stop at the era of Confucius and Mencius. Since then, it has continued to develop and promote, and it has continued to play the role of the patriarch in the ups and downs of China's social management and social thinking. However, parents inherit it from generation to generation. These people who manage the country, manage society, and manage people's hearts. When they faced Buddhism, they complained at the beginning. As I mentioned before, for example, Han Yu complained very much, and many people complained. The problem is, as time goes by, it is useless for you to complain, because this land has been penetrated by Buddhism, so many people have accepted Buddhism, and the thinking ability of Buddhism itself has also made those wise men with high IQs feel drummed in their hearts.
Obviously, there are many issues that go beyond our Confucian thinking. At this point, Confucianism has undergone changes. This makes me have to pay attention to the changes in our Confucianism before preaching. This is also an important trend in the field of Chinese thinking.
There are two kinds of people among Confucian scholars, those who are good at learning and those who are not good at learning. As for those who are good at learning, they gradually understand that the popularity of Buddhism has exposed the shortcomings of Confucianism. Confucianism promotes social order, while Buddhism explores the nature of the human heart. Social order is the textbook for rulers, and the nature of the human heart is a question for all people. Textbooks on social order will definitely refer to the wishes of a large number of powerful people, but questions about the nature of people's hearts will inspire the awareness of all living beings in the world. This is different.
In this case, can Confucianism, which has always been dominant, change its status and gain more lessons from the outside? However, it is troublesome for Confucianism to benefit from it, because it has a long history, a broad background, and many resources, and it is difficult to transform it significantly. Without a major transformation, the lessons it can gain will always be limited. Do you understand? It is very difficult for a car with a very heavy load to undergo a large-scale transformation on the road. This was the form of Confucianism at that time. It has always been dominant. It has many scholars, many books, and many schools. It is very difficult for it to transform. If it changes slightly, it means it has not changed. If it changes significantly, who will do it? Who is this driver? This problem is relatively big.
Fortunately, there are still some outstanding understanding people among Confucian scholars, and there are more than one or two. So starting from the Tang Dynasty, especially during the Song and Ming dynasties, Confucianism underwent a major transformation, giving rise to New Confucianism.
When we talk about New Confucianism now, we often refer to the present. My friends like Professor Du Weiming, they do it. No, during the Tang and Song Dynasties, there was already Neo-Confucianism. The focus of old Confucianism is to promote the ethical order, while the characteristic of new Confucianism is to study Buddhism and explore the true nature of people's hearts. This is undoubtedly influenced by Buddhism and Zen. Think about it, everyone. Old Confucianism mainly promoted the moral order; after New Confucianism learned Buddhism, it mainly focused on exploring the nature of the human heart, which must have been influenced by Buddhism.
The Transformation of Confucianism: Neo-Confucianism’s Reference to Zen Buddhism
The new generation of Confucian scholars believe that all kinds of right and wrong in the social order are related to a more abstract nature. Confucius and Mencius said many good things, but if the social order is to be maintained, what is its right and wrong? There must be a kind of nature, and this nature, the nature of nature, must be related to heaven. Therefore, Confucian scholars desperately searched for various passages about the mysterious relationship between heaven and man in "Shangshu", "Zuo Zhuan" and "Mencius", and then further delved into the starting point and conclusion of the human world. The old Confucian scholars were not very interested in this kind of research, which was to study the mysterious relationship between heaven and man, and to explore the beginning and end of the human world. Confucius, Mencius, and the older generation of traditional Confucianism were not very interested; but among New Confucianism, it has advanced by leaps and bounds.
Since Neo-Confucianism is studying that kind of issue, it is studying various starting points and endings related to heaven and earth, but it is still very different from Zen Buddhism. From the outside, the New Confucianists who studied these profound knowledge, later called Neo-Confucianism or Xinxue, looked very serious, heavy, and strenuous; while Zen Buddhism has always been so light, playful, and straightforward. Why is this happening? This is because Neo-Confucianism and the philosophy of mind always want to identify right and wrong in the world, good and evil, and always cut right and wrong with one knife. As for Zen Buddhism, there is no consciousness to separate and no mind to identify, so it seems particularly relaxed.
Regarding this issue, I think we cannot laugh at those Neo-Confucian scholars. They are in a crisis stage of thinking in the midst of a very difficult transformation. They have always upheld a series of social responsibilities and some social ideals. This is the foundation of their lives. Therefore, no matter how mysterious, profound or illusory their thoughts are, they cannot escape. Instead, they will come back and face the Buddhist Zen masters to make their own thoughts.
Zen masters can think about those free issues on the mountain top very easily, but it is difficult for our New Confucian scholars to give up social responsibilities, human ideals, and the foundation of their lives. They will ask the Zen master, your wits and epiphanies are so wonderful, how many people in the world can truly understand them? If you are always limited to a few wise men on the top of the mountain and among the white clouds, then how can you accomplish what Buddha said about extraditing sentient beings?
Please pay attention to a question. The question raised by Confucian scholars on this issue actually makes some sense. Your Zen Buddhism, your Buddhist principles, your epiphanies, and your wits are of course very superb, but how many people in the world can understand them? If all this can only belong to a handful of wise men among the white clouds on the top of the mountain, then how can you extradite so many sentient beings at the foot of the mountain that you want to extradite? To be fair, Confucian scholars feel that this kind of question is a bit righteous, because this is a large group of Chinese scholars. Their spiritual self-preservation can only be faced directly, and it is difficult to criticize them.
If we think about it, including me and many of my friends, we are actually one of them. We have social responsibilities, we have human ideals, and we care about many, many real people, rather than the more empty Buddhist talk of extradition for life. What we think of are all kinds of specific people on the streets of society, all kinds of people in the fields of the countryside, and this is what we think of. How to solve it? Therefore, as for this question, the question raised by Confucian scholars actually makes some sense.
I am also very able to understand their thinking, but I am a little bit special, because I miss the celebrities of the Wei and Jin Dynasties very much, and because of my investment in artistic aesthetics, I have the ability to communicate artistic thinking that has fascinated me throughout my life in Zen Buddhism. For me, I am closer to art because of the Wei and Jin Dynasties, and I am closer to my nature because of Zen Buddhism. Generally speaking, I am more accepting of Zen Buddhism. Because of this, I look at New Confucianism from this standpoint, which is relatively objective.
Thanks!

summary.gistZh: 新儒学是对传统儒学在近现代遭遇危机后的深刻反思与自我革新，试图将儒家伦理与现代民主、科学及人权价值有机融通。
summary.gistEn: New Confucianism is a profound reflection and self-renewal of traditional Confucianism facing modernity, bridging ancient ethics with science, democracy, and human rights.

highlights.zh: 近现代儒学危机：面对西学东渐与新文化运动，传统儒学曾被误认为阻碍现代化的绊脚石。
highlights.en: The Crisis of Modernity: Facing Western impact, traditional Confucianism was once misdiagnosed as an obstacle to modernization.

highlights.zh: 新儒家的历史功绩：熊十力、牟宗三、唐君毅等大师证明了儒学核心精神与现代文明并不冲突。
highlights.en: New Confucian Legacy: Masters like Xiong Shili and Mou Zongsan demonstrated that Confucian ethics harmonize with modern values.

highlights.zh: 内圣开出外王：从内在心性道德（内圣）开显出现代民主与科学制度（外王），完成文明的现代转向。
highlights.en: Inner Sage to Outer King: Deriving modern democratic institutions and scientific inquiry from inner moral self-cultivation.

highlights.zh: 全球化时代的价值：为现代人破解工具理性泛滥、道德滑坡与精神无家可归提供心灵归宿。
highlights.en: Global Value: Offering a spiritual sanctuary for humanity confronting modern hyper-rationalism and moral disorientation.

title: 文化大迁徙：在移动中活得更好的中国文化
